Referee report
Overall decision
Decision on the present submission: reject and invite a substantially reframed resubmission elsewhere.
This is not a rejection on the former APAL grounds. The revised manuscript now states its limitations with unusual clarity: the principal finite-group result is explicitly tied to a chosen good-cover site, finite nerves, a constant finite band, and chosen non-split lift data; it expressly denies that the construction is an invariant of bare empirical models.  It also correctly states that the higher semantic layers are classes of supplied typed expansions, not an existence or closure theorem for pre-existing lower-layer models. 
My rejection is instead based on four remaining matters:


The priority account is not yet safe. The central â€œcomponent gerbe over a global component sectionâ€ construction has a direct Giraud antecedent more exact than the manuscript acknowledges.

There is a real missing hypothesis in the general finite-nerve ÄŒechâ€“simplicial comparison. The flagship wedge theorem can be repaired without changing its conclusion, but Section 5 is presently stated too generally.


The proofs of the two claims most capable of carrying originalityâ€”the representative-rigid terminal theorem and the prescribed-image prestack constructionâ€”are in the unavailable supplement. The main article itself identifies these as supplement material.  I therefore assess their statements and priority below, but I cannot certify those proofs from main.pdf.


I do not find evidence in the displayed statements of a false flagship finite-group equivalence. The problem is priority, significance, architecture, and one correctable coefficient hypothesisâ€”not an obvious contradiction in the finite-abelian algebra.

2. Priority audit
Bottom-line priority judgment
The priority narrative is accurate about scope but not yet accurate about mathematical ancestry.
The manuscript now correctly denies a new general classification of gerbes, a presentation-free invariant, a construction from bare empirical models, and an unconditional non-split lifting theorem. That part is satisfactory.
The unsafe part is the claim that the articleâ€™s own contribution includes the component-gerbe construction and a broad family of construction/classification results without identifying how directly those are already contained in classical stack and gerbe theory. There is one definite omitted theorem-level antecedent and several theorem families that are standard lemmas in specialized notation.
I did not find a previously published theorem stating the entire bespoke two-label wedge classification verbatim. That does not make it a substantial priority claim: exact statements manufactured by composing standard equivalences can be formally new while having little independent mathematical priority.

3. Mathematical and expository objections requiring correction
3.1 The finite-nerve ÄŒechâ€“simplicial comparison is missing connectedness
Proposition 5.6 identifies an ordered ÄŒech n-cochain with one element of A for every nonempty (n+1)-fold intersection, and then identifies that with one coefficient on the corresponding simplex of the ordinary nerve. 
That is not valid merely because the band is trivialized as a constant sheaf. For a disconnected overlap Ui0â€‹â‹¯inâ€‹â€‹,

not one copy of A. The ordinary nerve records that the overlap is nonempty but not how many connected components it has.
The open-star good covers used in the flagship theorem have contractible, hence connected, nonempty intersections. Thus this does not destroy Theorem 6.16. It does invalidate the generality claimed in Section 5.
Resolution: choose one:

replace the ordinary nerve by the ÄŒech simplicial set/component nerve, with one simplex for each connected component; or


formulate the comparison with the appropriate local coefficient system.


This correction is mandatory. Without it, Section 5 contains a false general assertion.

3.2 The generated-site Leray comparison needs an explicit Comparison Lemma
The proof of Lemma 6.14 passes quickly from contractible open-star intersections to sheaf cohomology of âˆ£Kâˆ£ on the generated site. Contractibility alone does not identify the sheaf category or derived cohomology of an abstractly generated finite-intersection site with the usual topological site.
The required statement is plausible: the open stars and their finite intersections form a basis stable under finite intersections, and the generated coverage should be the induced basis topology. But that equivalence must be stated and proved.
Resolution: add a theorem saying that:


the all-subdivision open-star/intersection category is a basis for XÎ²â€‹;

3.3 The presentation-comparison groupoid currently proves too little
The groupoid is freely generated by refinements already assumed to induce H2â€‹-isomorphisms, cocycle replacements, band retrivializations, and inverses. The preservation of KÏ‰â€‹ under those chosen arrows is then UCT naturality. Distinct zigzags may act by different automorphisms, and no path independence is asserted. 
This is legitimate bookkeeping, but not a meaningful invariance theorem. The category has been defined so that the subgroup transports.
Resolution: either:

For the present paper, the second option is the realistic one.

These are correct, but their theorem-level presentation makes the paper look padded and obscures the few claims that need expert scrutiny.
Resolution: reduce the article to approximately:


one semantic-interface proposition;


one standard component-gerbe proposition;


one matching/non-neutrality theorem;


one terminal-rigidity theorem;


one finite-site realization theorem;


one UCT/aggregate proposition;


the wedge corollary;


the empirical-model boundary theorem.


The rest should be remarks, clauses, or omitted calculations. The theorem count should fall substantially; preserving it is not a virtue.

3.5 The team-semantic architecture is not causally connected to the classification
The upper model class admits arbitrary supplied finite sites, presheaves, prestacks, and stack lifts satisfying the typing conditions. The manuscript correctly admits that this is a model-class convention.  Consequently, the wedge construction is not derived from team semantics. It is inserted into a class broad enough to accept it.
That makes â€œover Teams and Presheavesâ€ an overstatement of what drives the main result.
Resolution: retitle the paper along the lines of:

Component Gerbes and Homological Images on Finite Good-Cover Sites

or

Finite-Site Realizations of Component Gerbes and Homological Quotients

Reduce Sections 2â€“3 to the minimum interface needed for the matching predicate. Keep the lower-fragment separation result in an appendix. This would make the actual mathematical centre visible.
The alternativeâ€”proving that a nontrivial, independently defined class of team-semantic models naturally produces the required non-split liftsâ€”would be substantially new research and is not a realistic revision requirement.

3.6 The â€œauxiliary registerâ€ results should be deleted as a theorem package
Without restrictions on admissible encodings, the minimum size of an auxiliary set needed to inject a fibre of size m is m. The sharpness construction uses arbitrary set-theoretic sections. This is fibre counting, not an information-theoretic theorem.
Resolution: replace all register definitions and theorems with one sentence:

Since the quotient fibres are cosets of the kernel, the minimum cardinality of an unrestricted auxiliary set separating each fibre is the kernel cardinality.

If an actual application imposes locality, equivariance, continuity, computability, or common encoder constraints, a nontrivial result could remain. No such constraint is presently present.

3.7 The 48+50-page architecture is still too large
The old 96-page article has been transformed into a 48-page article plus a 50-page supplement, but the mathematical referee burden remains 98 pages. More importantly, the supplement contains the rigidity and realization proofs that should determine acceptance. 
This is not the same presentation defect as the former opaque terminology, but it remains an editorial obstacle.
Resolution: produce a self-contained article of at most about 40 pages for Cahiers:


integrate the full rigidity proof;


integrate the core prescribed-image construction proof;


remove routine semantic and quotient calculations;


retain a technical appendix only for variants and extended examples.


Dividing into two papers is not attractive because the quotient half is too elementary to stand independently.

3.8 Machine evidence has no bearing on the decision
The finite Python checks are useful regression tests. They do not verify the general theorems, and the inert leanverified markers provide no evidence at all.
Resolution: remove any suggestion in the manuscript or cover letter that these checks support mathematical correctness. A repository note may describe them as sanity checks. Either provide actual Lean artifacts or omit formal-verification language entirely.

Overall decision
Decision on the present submission: reject and invite a substantially reframed resubmission elsewhere.
This is not a rejection on the former APAL grounds. The revised manuscript now states its limitations with unusual clarity: the principal finite-group result is explicitly tied to a chosen good-cover site, finite nerves, a constant finite band, and chosen non-split lift data; it expressly denies that the construction is an invariant of bare empirical models. 2. Priority audit
Bottom-line priority judgment
The priority narrative is accurate about scope but not yet accurate about mathematical ancestry.
The manuscript now correctly denies a new general classification of gerbes, a presentation-free invariant, a construction from bare empirical models, and an unconditional non-split lifting theorem. That part is satisfactory.
The unsafe part is the claim that the articleâ€™s own contribution includes the component-gerbe construction and a broad family of construction/classification results without identifying how directly those are already contained in classical stack and gerbe theory. There is one definite omitted theorem-level antecedent and several theorem families that are standard lemmas in specialized notation.
I did not find a previously published theorem stating the entire bespoke two-label wedge classification verbatim. That does not make it a substantial priority claim: exact statements manufactured by composing standard equivalences can be formally new while having little independent mathematical priority.
Claim-by-claim audit

3. Mathematical and expository objections requiring correction
3.1 The finite-nerve ÄŒechâ€“simplicial comparison is missing connectedness
Proposition 5.6 identifies an ordered ÄŒech n-cochain with one element of A for every nonempty (n+1)-fold intersection, and then identifies that with one coefficient on the corresponding simplex of the ordinary nerve. 
That is not valid merely because the band is trivialized as a constant sheaf. For a disconnected overlap Ui0â€‹â‹¯inâ€‹â€‹,
Î“(Ui0â€‹â‹¯inâ€‹â€‹,Aâ€‹)â‰…AÏ€0â€‹(Ui0â€‹â‹¯inâ€‹â€‹),
not one copy of A. The ordinary nerve records that the overlap is nonempty but not how many connected components it has.
The open-star good covers used in the flagship theorem have contractible, hence connected, nonempty intersections. Thus this does not destroy Theorem 6.16. It does invalidate the generality claimed in Section 5.
Resolution: choose one:


add the hypothesis that every nonempty finite intersection is connected and that the coefficient trivializations identify its section group coherently with A; or


replace the ordinary nerve by the ÄŒech simplicial set/component nerve, with one simplex for each connected component; or


formulate the comparison with the appropriate local coefficient system.


This correction is mandatory. Without it, Section 5 contains a false general assertion.

3.2 The generated-site Leray comparison needs an explicit Comparison Lemma
The proof of Lemma 6.14 passes quickly from contractible open-star intersections to sheaf cohomology of âˆ£Kâˆ£ on the generated site. Contractibility alone does not identify the sheaf category or derived cohomology of an abstractly generated finite-intersection site with the usual topological site.
The required statement is plausible: the open stars and their finite intersections form a basis stable under finite intersections, and the generated coverage should be the induced basis topology. But that equivalence must be stated and proved.
Resolution: add a theorem saying that:


the all-subdivision open-star/intersection category is a basis for XÎ²â€‹;


its generated topology agrees with the induced open-cover topology;


restriction induces an equivalence of sheaf categories;


the paperâ€™s â€œgenuine constant sheafâ€ corresponds to the ordinary constant sheaf;


the relevant intersections are acyclic;


the filtered ÄŒech colimit computes derived H2.


If the supplement already proves exactly this for the all-subdivision site, cite the theorem verbatim in Lemma 6.14 rather than replacing it by two sentences. If it proves only the comparison for one finite intersection site, an additional passage to the common generated site is still needed.

3.3 The presentation-comparison groupoid currently proves too little
The groupoid is freely generated by refinements already assumed to induce H2â€‹-isomorphisms, cocycle replacements, band retrivializations, and inverses. The preservation of KÏ‰â€‹ under those chosen arrows is then UCT naturality. Distinct zigzags may act by different automorphisms, and no path independence is asserted. 
This is legitimate bookkeeping, but not a meaningful invariance theorem. The category has been defined so that the subgroup transports.
Resolution: either:


prove coherence/path independence over a naturally occurring category of presentations; or


demote the groupoid to a definition and one naturality proposition, and remove it from the principal originality list.


For the present paper, the second option is the realistic one.

3.4 The theorem count misrepresents the amount of new mathematics
Examples include:


composition of truth-preserving reducts;


singleton-team agreement;


UCT kernel equivalences;


first-isomorphism and third-isomorphism consequences;


primary decomposition of a quotient;


exact fibre cardinalities;


maximum fibre size for a common auxiliary set.


These are correct, but their theorem-level presentation makes the paper look padded and obscures the few claims that need expert scrutiny.
Resolution: reduce the article to approximately:


one semantic-interface proposition;


one standard component-gerbe proposition;


one matching/non-neutrality theorem;


one terminal-rigidity theorem;


one finite-site realization theorem;


one UCT/aggregate proposition;


the wedge corollary;


the empirical-model boundary theorem.


The rest should be remarks, clauses, or omitted calculations. The theorem count should fall substantially; preserving it is not a virtue.

3.5 The team-semantic architecture is not causally connected to the classification
The upper model class admits arbitrary supplied finite sites, presheaves, prestacks, and stack lifts satisfying the typing conditions. The manuscript correctly admits that this is a model-class convention.  Consequently, the wedge construction is not derived from team semantics. It is inserted into a class broad enough to accept it.
That makes â€œover Teams and Presheavesâ€ an overstatement of what drives the main result.
Resolution: retitle the paper along the lines of:

Component Gerbes and Homological Images on Finite Good-Cover Sites

or

Finite-Site Realizations of Component Gerbes and Homological Quotients

Reduce Sections 2â€“3 to the minimum interface needed for the matching predicate. Keep the lower-fragment separation result in an appendix. This would make the actual mathematical centre visible.
The alternativeâ€”proving that a nontrivial, independently defined class of team-semantic models naturally produces the required non-split liftsâ€”would be substantially new research and is not a realistic revision requirement.

3.6 The â€œauxiliary registerâ€ results should be deleted as a theorem package
Without restrictions on admissible encodings, the minimum size of an auxiliary set needed to inject a fibre of size m is m. The sharpness construction uses arbitrary set-theoretic sections. This is fibre counting, not an information-theoretic theorem.
Resolution: replace all register definitions and theorems with one sentence:

Since the quotient fibres are cosets of the kernel, the minimum cardinality of an unrestricted auxiliary set separating each fibre is the kernel cardinality.

If an actual application imposes locality, equivariance, continuity, computability, or common encoder constraints, a nontrivial result could remain. No such constraint is presently present.

3.7 The 48+50-page architecture is still too large
The old 96-page article has been transformed into a 48-page article plus a 50-page supplement, but the mathematical referee burden remains 98 pages. More importantly, the supplement contains the rigidity and realization proofs that should determine acceptance. 
This is not the same presentation defect as the former opaque terminology, but it remains an editorial obstacle.
Resolution: produce a self-contained article of at most about 40 pages for Cahiers:


integrate the full rigidity proof;


integrate the core prescribed-image construction proof;


remove routine semantic and quotient calculations;


retain a technical appendix only for variants and extended examples.


Dividing into two papers is not attractive because the quotient half is too elementary to stand independently.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence â‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter â‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion â‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
âœ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
âŒ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
âœ… Write â†’ Run (pass) â†’ Revert fix â†’ Run (MUST FAIL) â†’ Restore â†’ Run (pass)
âŒ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
âœ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
âŒ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
âœ… Re-read plan â†’ Create checklist â†’ Verify each â†’ Report gaps or completion
âŒ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
âœ… Agent reports success â†’ Check VCS diff â†’ Verify changes â†’ Report actual state
âŒ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion â†’ redirect â†’ rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

# PDF Skill

## When to use
- Read or review PDF content where layout and visuals matter.
- Create PDFs programmatically with reliable formatting.
- Validate final rendering before delivery.

## Workflow
1. Prefer visual review: render PDF pages to PNGs and inspect them.
   - Use `pdftoppm` if available.
   - If unavailable, install Poppler or ask the user to review the output locally.
2. Use `reportlab` to generate PDFs when creating new documents.
3. Use `pdfplumber` (or `pypdf`) for text extraction and quick checks; do not rely on it for layout fidelity.
4. After each meaningful update, re-render pages and verify alignment, spacing, and legibility.

## Temp and output conventions
- Use `tmp/pdfs/` for intermediate files; delete when done.
- Write final artifacts under `output/pdf/` when working in this repo.
- Keep filenames stable and descriptive.

## Dependencies (install if missing)
Prefer `uv` for dependency management.

Python packages:
```
uv pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```
If `uv` is unavailable:
```
python3 -m pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```
System tools (for rendering):
```
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install poppler

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y poppler-utils
```

If installation isn't possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it locally.

## Environment
No required environment variables.

## Rendering command
```
pdftoppm -png $INPUT_PDF $OUTPUT_PREFIX
```

## Quality expectations
- Maintain polished visual design: consistent typography, spacing, margins, and section hierarchy.
- Avoid rendering issues: clipped text, overlapping elements, broken tables, black squares, or unreadable glyphs.
- Charts, tables, and images must be sharp, aligned, and clearly labeled.
- Use ASCII hyphens only. Avoid U+2011 (non-breaking hyphen) and other Unicode dashes.
- Citations and references must be human-readable; never leave tool tokens or placeholder strings.

## Final checks
- Do not deliver until the latest PNG inspection shows zero visual or formatting defects.
- Confirm headers/footers, page numbering, and section transitions look polished.
- Keep intermediate files organized or remove them after final approval.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans â€” one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** â€” never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code â€” the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step â€” if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself â€” not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags â€” any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review â€” just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

\title[Component Gerbes and Homological Quotients]{Component Gerbes and Homological Quotients over Teams and Presheaves}
\author{Haobo Ma}
\address[Haobo Ma]{AELF PTE LTD., \#14-02, Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 1, 8 Marina Blvd, Singapore 018981}
\email[Haobo Ma]{auric@aelf.io}

\author{Wenlin Zhang}
\address[Wenlin Zhang]{National University of Singapore, Singapore}
\email[Wenlin Zhang]{e1327962@u.nus.edu}

\begin{document}

\begin{abstract}
On the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres, a nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups exactly when $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial, and the finite-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models.
\end{abstract}

\keywords{teams, presheaves, sheafification, banded gerbes, homological cokernel, universal coefficient theorem}

\begin{abstract}
This document contains the supporting material relocated from the article:
the presheaf, sheafification, banded-lift, terminal-rigidity, typed-readout,
and lower-fragment packages; the cocycle-coordinate strictification results;
the finite-site constructions realizing prescribed and mixed componentwise
homological images; and the refinement-dynamics and GHZ/Mermin appendices.
The article retains the component-gerbe criterion, intrinsic homological
quotients, aggregation exact sequence, wedge-of-spheres classification, and
empirical-model comparison.  Cross-document citations are descriptive and do
not import either document's auxiliary file.
\end{abstract}

\maketitle

\section*{Dependency and source scope}

The supplement inputs exactly the source units removed from the article.
The initial section develops the set-valued and groupoid-valued local-to-global
machinery.  The next package gives the presentation-level strictification and
the finite-site existence constructions used by the article's intrinsic and
wedge-of-spheres results.  The appendices collect refinement dynamics and the
chosen split GHZ/Mermin lift.

## Summary

The compiled manuscript contains the A/B/C theorem chain: extension-chain forcing, pullback-based local sites and sheafification, terminal-fibre rigidity, lower-fragment separation, component gerbes and gerbe-null semantics, strict and intrinsic visible quotients, pure Ext character blindness, branch-sensitive versus branch-uniform comparison, finite-nerve realization, the torsion-free H2 subgroup classification, bouquet two-branch resolution, the exact obstruction to transferring these results to empirical models, and the split GHZ/Mermin lift.

No required in-scope theorem from the scope contract is completely absent from the compiled manuscript. The main risks are not missing labels but proof-interface sharpness and source hygiene:

- `lem:bouquet-cover-classical-interface` uses `beta` without quantifying it.
- `lem:generated-subsite-model-interface` needs an explicit admissible-model/free-expansion convention.
- `prop:invariance-visible-quotients` must remain groupoid-indexed, not path-independent.
- `sec_forcing_necessity.tex` is an unused stronger draft with duplicate `thm:pointwise-irreducibility` and unresolved references.
- `sequel/` files are out-of-scope split material.
- Several included section files exceed the 800-line discipline.

## Classification Notes

The inventory treats the compiled `main.tex` inputs as the current manuscript. It also scans unused `.tex` files because the Stage A prompt requested all TeX sources. Results in `sequel/` and `sec_forcing_necessity.tex` are therefore classified, but not as part of the compiled article.

Classical material is classified as supporting/background when it is a standard sheaf, stack, gerbe, Cech, UCT, finite abelian duality, or finite group structure fact. The paper-specific contribution is the way these tools are assembled into the state-forcing gluing-obstruction and homological-visibility chain.

The inventory records cross-resolution risks only where a future edit might accidentally convert a stated comparison or monotonicity result into a naive invariant. The current manuscript usually handles this correctly by requiring homology-equivalent refinement, chosen zigzags, Leray/good-cover comparison, or explicit pullback hypotheses.

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
\[
 A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
\]
for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
\[
 d(G)\leq 2\beta
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
\]
Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
arbitrary empirical model.

The standard input is as follows.  We use universal satisfaction on nonempty
teams of assignments, presheaves and their sheafifications, stackification of
categories fibred in groupoids, the classification of banded gerbes by
Giraud's $H^2$, the \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison on the specified Leray
covers, the universal coefficient theorem, and elementary structure theory
and duality for finite abelian groups
\cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}.  Our contributions are the organization
of these inputs into the stated semantic framework; the comparison between
matching families and component gerbes under explicit lift hypotheses; the
presentation-comparison groupoid and the two aggregate quotients; the
component-forgetting exact sequence; the construction of prescribed
componentwise homological images; and the preceding finite-group
classification.

The relation with the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction must be stated
at the outset.  Their obstruction is a relative \v{C}ech class
\[
 \gamma_e(s)\in
 \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0})
\]
of a presheaf, equivalently a torsor class indexed by a chosen local section
\cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}.  Our obstruction is the
derived Giraud class
\[
 \omega_v=[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)
\]
of a gerbe banded by a sheaf, indexed by a global component section.  These
classes do not correspond.  What is functorial is only the support-level
comparison: every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model gives a
canonical split stack whose component gerbes are neutral.  In particular, a
strongly contextual model has no global component section from which our map
could produce its local-section-indexed AMB classes.  Consequently the
condition $d(G)\leq2\beta$ with $G$ not a cyclic $p$-group does not transfer to
bare empirical models; a band and a non-split banded stack lift would have to
be supplied as additional data.  This is proved precisely in
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface,thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}.

We now describe the framework.  An information state
$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is
universal team satisfaction, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or
Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the
team, which immediately gives persistence.  Point assignments enter through
the singleton-state embedding.  The later semantic frameworks add typed data
while preserving the truth of formulas in the reduct; we call these
truth-preserving reduct expansions because consequence conservativity is not asserted without an expansion
theorem for every lower model.

For an admissible parameter $r$ at $p$, the paper specifies a thin
reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$, its base object
$a=[r]_p$, and a presheaf of local sections
$F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.  A matching family
without an element of $F_{p,s}(a)$ is the set-valued failure studied here.
The forward implication from a matching family to a section of the
sheafification is formal; the converse holds when
$F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a}$ is separated
(\suppresult{Existence of a matching family gives a sheafified section} and
\suppresult{Sheafification characterizes existence of a matching family on separated slice sites}).
The predicates expressing a matching family, a global section, and matching
without amalgamation are not definable in the automorphism-invariant,
constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct
(\suppresult{Parameter-free one-reference lower-fragment separation in the constant-free reduct}).

Gerbe-valued obstructions require extra, noncanonical structure.  A
gluing-sensitive banded lift datum consists of a banded groupoid lift of $F$,
its stackification together with an identification of its component sheaf
with $aF$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and a
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis.  A section
$v\in\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong(aF)(a)$ determines a full component gerbe
$\mathfrak G_v$ and hence a Giraud class $\omega_v$.  Under the stated
separatedness, representability, and comparison hypotheses, matching without
amalgamation is equivalent to the existence of global component sections with
all corresponding component gerbes non-neutral
(\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition,thm:gerbe-null-semantics}).  A
strictly pullback-stable representative choice imposes a useful rigidity
condition: together with terminal-fibre essential surjectivity it forces the
sheafification unit to be onto at the terminal object
(\suppresult{Rigidity of representative-rigid lifts over separated slice sites}).

Fix next a global component section, a finite nerve representative, and a
constant finite abelian band $A$.  The universal coefficient map evaluates
the class on second homology,
\[
 \operatorname{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow A.
\]
We write $K_\omega=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ for its
homological image and $Q_\omega=\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)
=A/K_\omega$ for its homological cokernel.  These are invariants of an object
of the presentation-comparison groupoid and transport functorially along the
chosen comparison zigzags; no path independence is claimed.  A class with
zero $H_2$ evaluation is precisely a class in the $\operatorname{Ext}^1$
kernel of the universal coefficient sequence.  This separates the
homology-evaluation quotient from the more presentation-dependent quotient by
the subgroup generated by the coordinates of a chosen cocycle.

For finitely many component sections $v$, put $K_v=\operatorname{Im}
(\operatorname{ev}_{\omega_v})$.  Retaining the component label gives the
label-aware quotient $A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$; retaining only characters that work
for every component gives the common-character quotient
$A/(\sum_vK_v)$.  Their canonical comparison has kernel
\[
 \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}.
\]
The exact sequence and its finite-register interpretation are formal.  The
existence results are not: on the finite intersection site associated to a
connected good-cover nerve with $H_1=0$, we construct typed expansions whose
componentwise evaluation maps have prescribed images, including mixtures of
neutral and non-neutral component gerbes.  If $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong
\mathbb Z^\beta$, the attainable image subgroups are exactly those generated
by at most $\beta$ elements.  The main classification follows by asking when
$G$ decomposes as $K_1\oplus K_2$ with both summands nonzero and each generated
by at most $\beta$ elements.

The paper is organized as follows.  Sections~\ref{sec:preliminaries} and
\ref{sec:information-states} define the semantic frameworks and universal
team satisfaction.  The article then gives the component-gerbe and
Giraud-class results, the finite-presentation and homological quotients, their
aggregation over component sections, the wedge-of-spheres classification, and
the precise empirical-model comparison.  The separately compiled
\suppresult{Presheaves, sheafification, and matching without amalgamation}
contains the full presheaf/sheafification, banded-lift, terminal-rigidity,
typed-readout, null-trichotomy, and lower-fragment separation packages.
It also contains the sections titled ``Cocycle-coordinate and component-image
constructions'' and ``Refinement dynamics,'' which prove the
cocycle-coordinate strictification results, the prescribed and mixed
component-image construction theorems, the refinement-dynamics consequences,
and the chosen GHZ/Mermin lift.

\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}

The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
has been fixed.

\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2em,labelindent=0pt]
\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
satisfaction.
\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
is not part of the definition.
\item[Typed expansion class.]
The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
fixed lower model.
\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
are attached to $r$.
\item[{Base object $a=[r]_p$.}]
The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
specified pretopology and pullbacks.
\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
hypothesis.
\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
\item[Global component section $v$.]
An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
$(aF)(a)$.
\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
zigzags need not give the same comparison.
\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
\item[Label-aware quotient.]
$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
componentwise homological cokernels.
\item[Common-character quotient.]
$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
\item[Typed readout.]
The partial output attached to an admissible parameter: inadmissible if no
typed data are attached, uniquely determined if the sheafified global section
is unique, and non-unique-or-absent otherwise.
\item[Indexed refinement system.]
A family of state-refinement relations indexed by information coordinates,
each monotone for the state preorder and the specified time order.
\item[Information-determining axis set.]
A finite set of refinement coordinates whose information values determine any
decided truth value among the states reachable along those coordinates.
\item[Pairwise commuting refinements and common refinement.]
Refinements for which every indicated finite family has a state refining all
its members.
\item[Readout-preserving rewrite.]
A rewrite between partial outputs that preserves both definedness and value.
\item[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf.]
A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is the
given empirical-model support presheaf and whose automorphism sheaves are the
specified band.
\end{description}

\section{Concluding remarks}\label{sec:conclusion}

The paper separates three stages of the local-to-global problem. At the level
of information states,
\suppresult{Parameter-free one-reference lower-fragment separation in the constant-free reduct}
shows that neither
existence of a matching family nor matching without amalgamation is definable
in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment considered
here. This is not a general expressivity theorem; it identifies the first
point at which the presheaf data exceed the lower language of universal team
satisfaction.

The passage from set-valued to groupoid-valued data necessarily depends on
additional lift data. By
\suppresult{Rigidity of representative-rigid lifts over separated slice sites}, a strictly
pullback-stable representative choice together with essential surjectivity on
the terminal fibre implies that the sheafification unit is surjective there.
Under $H^1$-vanishing and separatedness of the restriction to the slice site,
this is equivalent to the presheaf already satisfying the sheaf condition at
that fibre. For finite empirical models,
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} gives a canonical split banded
stack lift, but every component gerbe is neutral. The AMB obstruction is a
relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section, whereas the
obstruction here is a derived Giraud $H^2$ class indexed by a global component
section. Only the support-level comparison is functorial, and neither class
recovers the other in general.

For a fixed finite nerve representative, the homological image
$K_\omega=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and homological
cokernel $Q_\omega=A/K_\omega$ record the contribution detected on $H_2$.
Across presentations they transport along chosen arrows in the
presentation-comparison groupoid; no independence of the chosen zigzag is
asserted. For several global component sections, the label-aware and
common-character quotients are related by the component-forgetting exact
sequence. Under the fixed finite-nerve, constant-band,
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison, and $H_1=0$ hypotheses, the construction
theorems attain exactly the componentwise image subgroups permitted by
second homology.

When $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, these are precisely
the subgroups generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The chosen open-star good
covers of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres therefore give the exact
classification: the nonzero finite abelian groups occurring as two-component
label-loss kernels with complementary nonzero image subgroups are those with
$d(G)\leq2\beta$ that are not cyclic $p$-groups. This construction does not
transfer to bare empirical models, whose canonical split lift has zero
homological image subgroups.

\begin{remark}[External crossed-module comparison interface]
\label{rem:crossed-module-comparison-interface}
Let
\[
1\longrightarrow Z\longrightarrow \widehat K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow 1
\]
be a central extension, let $K\trianglelefteq G$, put $Q=G/K$, and suppose
that $G\to Q$ admits the local sections required in locally continuous or
locally smooth group cohomology and that the conjugation action lifts so that
$\widehat K\to G$ is a crossed module.  Neeb, Wagemann, and Wockel construct
a \v{C}echization homomorphism
\[
\tau:H^3_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q,Z)\longrightarrow
\check H^2(Q,\underline Z)
\]
and ask whether the image of the crossed-module characteristic class agrees,
up to a convention-dependent sign, with the lifting obstruction of the
principal $K$-bundle $G\to Q$ \cite[Problem~8.1(b)]{NeebWagemannWockel2013}.
The present paper supplies only the downstream analysis of a lifting-gerbe
$H^2$-class after a finite-nerve, constant finite-band presentation and its
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison have been chosen.  It does not supply a chain
model for $H^3_{\mathrm{loc}}$, a representative of the crossed-module
characteristic class, or a chain homotopy comparing that representative with
the triple-overlap defect cocycle.  Consequently, neither the comparison
identity, its sign, nor its asserted naturality follows from the results
proved here.  Establishing such a comparison is an external open interface,
not a theorem or a construction begun in this paper.
\end{remark}

The hypotheses remain explicit throughout: \textup{(RC)} specifies pullbacks
of the presheaf data; \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)} specify the banded lift,
representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison; separatedness is invoked
where global component sections are represented by matching families; and
$H^1$-vanishing is used for terminal-fibre rigidity. The formulation here uses
pullback-based slice sites. Comparisons of finite presentations are therefore
groupoid-indexed and zigzag-dependent, rather than presentation-free choices
of canonical representatives.

 222: \begin{proposition}[No new global objects at $a$]\label{prop:no-new-global-objects}
 223: Assume essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity} for a banded groupoid lift on the pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$. Then
 224: \[
 225: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
 226: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 227: \mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing.
 228: \]
 229: \end{proposition}
 230: 
 231: \begin{proof}
 232: By \Cref{def:existence-levels} and \Cref{def:banded-groupoid-lift}(i),
 233: \[
 234: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
 235: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 236: F_{p,s}(a)\neq\varnothing
 237: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 238: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)\neq\varnothing
 239: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 240: (\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing.
 241: \]
 242: If $(\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing$, choose $y\in (\mathfrak P_r)_a$. Then $\iota_r(y)\in \mathfrak L_r(a)$, so $\mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing$. Conversely, if $x\in \mathfrak L_r(a)$, essential surjectivity of $(\iota_r)_a$ yields $y\in (\mathfrak P_r)_a$ with $\iota_r(y)\cong x$, so $(\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing$.
 243: \end{proof}

 259: \]
 260: is $\sigma$;
 261: \item for every morphism $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C_a$ and every $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(U)$,
 262: \[
 263: f^*s_U(\sigma)=s_V(\res_V^U(\sigma)).
 264: \]
 265: \end{enumerate}
 266: Here \(f^*\) is computed with respect to a fixed split cleavage of the
 267: fibred groupoid \(\mathfrak P_r\), so pullbacks compose on the nose. Thus
 268: the isomorphism classes of lift objects admit a strictly pullback-stable choice
 269: of representatives. This is the condition abbreviated by
 270: \emph{representative-rigid}. Without this split-cleavage convention the same condition
 271: would have to be stated with coherent cartesian isomorphisms, and the proof
 272: of descent below would require the corresponding triple-cocycle coherence
 273: instead of literal equalities of pulled-back representatives.
 274: \end{definition}
 275: 
 276: \begin{lemma}[Where separatedness on the slice enters]\label{lem:unit-equality-on-cover-members}
 277: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with pullbacks of covering families, let \(F\)
 278: be a presheaf of sets, let \(u:F\to aF\) be the sheafification unit, and
 279: let \(X\) be an object. Assume that \(F\) is separated at every object of
 280: the slice \(\mathcal C/X\). If
 281: \[
 282: \{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}
 283: \]
 284: is a covering family, \(\sigma\in F(X)\), and
 285: \(\sigma_i\in F(X_i)\) are sections satisfying
 286: \[
 287: u_{X_i}\bigl(\res_{X_i}^{X}\sigma\bigr)=u_{X_i}(\sigma_i)
 288: \qquad(\forall i),
 289: \]
 290: then
 291: \[
 292: \res_{X_i}^{X}\sigma=\sigma_i
 293: \qquad(\forall i).
 294: \]
 295: \end{lemma}
 296: 
 297: \begin{proof}
 298: Fix \(i\). Equality in \((aF)(X_i)\) is only sheafified equality, so it
 299: does not by itself give equality in \(F(X_i)\). By
 300: \Cref{lem:sheafification-unit-equality-local}, there is a covering family
 301: \(\{Y_{ik}\to X_i\}_k\) such that
 302: \[
 303: \res_{Y_{ik}}^{X}\sigma=\res_{Y_{ik}}^{X_i}\sigma_i
 304: \qquad(\forall k)
 305: \]
 306: in \(F(Y_{ik})\). The object \(X_i\) lies in the slice \(\mathcal C/X\),
 307: and the hypothesis says that \(F\) is separated at this object. Therefore
 308: these equalities after a cover of \(X_i\) force equality over \(X_i\)
 309: itself:
 310: \[
 311: \res_{X_i}^{X}\sigma=\sigma_i.
 312: \]
 313: This proves the assertion for every \(i\).
 314: \end{proof}

 succeeded in 219ms:
   1: \begin{lemma}[Bijective terminal unit and the terminal sheaf axiom]\label{lem:bijective-unit-terminal-sheaf-axiom}
   2: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with pullbacks of covering families, let $F$
   3: be a presheaf of sets, let $X$ be an object, and let
   4: \[
   5: u:F\longrightarrow aF
   6: \]
   7: be the sheafification unit. Assume that \(F\) is separated at every object
   8: of the slice \(\mathcal C/X\). Then the following are equivalent:
   9: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
  10: \item the map \(u_X:F(X)\to(aF)(X)\) is bijective;
  11: \item \(F\) satisfies the sheaf axiom at \(X\): every strict matching
  12: family on every cover of \(X\) has a unique amalgamation in \(F(X)\).
  13: \end{enumerate}
  14: Here separatedness on the whole slice is essential.  In the direction from
  15: bijectivity of \(u_X\) to the sheaf axiom, the chosen preimage of the
  16: glued sheaf section has restrictions which agree with the prescribed
  17: local sections only after applying \(u\) over each cover member.  Equality
  18: in \((aF)(X_i)\) gives equality in \(F\) only after a further cover of
  19: \(X_i\), and separatedness at \(X_i\), not merely at \(X\), is what
  20: descends that refined equality back to \(X_i\).
  21: \end{lemma}
  22: 
  23: \begin{proof}
  24: Separatedness on the slice at \(X\) implies injectivity of \(u_X\). Indeed, if
  25: \(u_X(\sigma)=u_X(\tau)\), then
  26: \Cref{lem:sheafification-unit-equality-local} gives a covering family
  27: \(\{X_i\to X\}_i\) on which the restrictions of \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\)
  28: are equal in \(F(X_i)\), and separatedness at \(X\) forces
  29: \(\sigma=\tau\).
  30: 
  31: Assume first that \(u_X\) is bijective. Let
  32: \[
  33: \bigl(\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I},(\sigma_i)_{i\in I}\bigr)
  34: \]
  35: be a strict \(F\)-matching family. Applying \(u\) to the sections
  36: \(\sigma_i\) gives a matching family in the sheaf \(aF\), hence a unique
  37: section \(\xi\in(aF)(X)\). By surjectivity choose
  38: \(\sigma\in F(X)\) with \(u_X(\sigma)=\xi\). For each \(i\),
  39: \[
  40: u_{X_i}\bigl(\res_{X_i}^{X}\sigma\bigr)=u_{X_i}(\sigma_i)
  41: \]
  42: in \((aF)(X_i)\). This equality is not an equality in \(F(X_i)\). By
  43: \Cref{lem:unit-equality-on-cover-members}, applied to the cover
  44: \(\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}\), these sheafified equalities upgrade to
  45: \[
  46: \res_{X_i}^{X}\sigma=\sigma_i
  47: \qquad(\forall i).
  48: \]
  49: Thus \(\sigma\) is an amalgamation of the original matching family.
  50: Uniqueness of the amalgamation follows again from separatedness at \(X\).
  51: 
  52: Conversely, assume the sheaf axiom at \(X\). Let
  53: \(\xi\in(aF)(X)\). By the plus--plus normal form
  54: \Cref{lem:strict-sheafification-representatives}, \(\xi\) is represented
  55: by a cover \(\{X_i\to X\}_i\) and sections
  56: \(\sigma_i\in F(X_i)\) whose restrictions to each pullback overlap agree
  57: after a further covering of that overlap. Because every such overlap is an
  58: object of \(\mathcal C/X\), \Cref{lem:separated-restriction-refined-equality}
  59: upgrades the refined equalities to a strict \(F\)-matching family. The
  60: sheaf axiom at \(X\) gives an amalgamation \(\sigma\in F(X)\). The
  61: sections \(u_X(\sigma)\) and \(\xi\) restrict to the same sections of
  62: \(aF\) on the cover \(\{X_i\to X\}_i\), so separatedness of the sheaf
  63: \(aF\) gives \(u_X(\sigma)=\xi\). Hence \(u_X\) is surjective, and it is
  64: injective by the first paragraph.
  65: \end{proof}

  67: \begin{lemma}[Isomorphism torsor for a lifted component]\label{lem:canonical-lift-isom-torsor}
  68: Let $\mathfrak P_r$ be a representative-rigid banded groupoid lift with band $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$, let
  69: \[
  70: \iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
  71: \]
  72: be the stackification map, and let $x\in\mathfrak L_r(a)$ and $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(a)$ satisfy
  73: \[
  74: [\iota_r(s_a(\sigma))]=[x]
  75: \quad\text{in}\quad
  76: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a).
  77: \]
  78: Then the sheaf
  79: \[
  80: \mathcal I_{\sigma,x}:=
  81: \underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathfrak L_r}(\iota_r(s_a(\sigma)),x)
  82: \]
  83: is a $\Band$-torsor on $\mathcal C_a$. If $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)=0$, then $\mathcal I_{\sigma,x}$ has a global section, equivalently
  84: \[
  85: \iota_r(s_a(\sigma))\cong x
  86: \quad\text{in}\quad
  87: \mathfrak L_r(a).
  88: \]
  89: \end{lemma}
  90: 
  91: \begin{proof}
  92: Write
  93: \[
  94: y:=s_a(\sigma).
  95: \]
  96: The equality of component classes in the sheaf $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)$ means precisely that the two objects $\iota_r(y)$ and $x$ become isomorphic after passing to a cover of $a$. Hence there is a covering family
  97: \[
  98: \{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
  99: \]
 100: and isomorphisms
 101: \[
 102: \phi_i:\iota_r(y)|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x|_{U_i}.
 103: \]
 104: Thus $\mathcal I_{\sigma,x}$ is locally nonempty.
 105: 
 106: For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and every local isomorphism
 107: \[
 108: \phi:\iota_r(y)|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}x|_U,
 109: \]
 110: right composition gives a simply transitive action of
 111: \[
 112: \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}_{\mathfrak L_r}(\iota_r(y)|_U)
 113: \]
 114: on $\mathcal I_{\sigma,x}(U)$:
 115: \[
 116: \alpha\longmapsto \phi\circ\alpha.
 117: \]
 118: Because $\mathfrak L_r$ is the stackification of a $\Band$-banded prestack, the automorphism sheaf of $\iota_r(y)|_U$ is identified with $\Band|_U$; the band is abelian, so the same torsor is obtained from left composition through the automorphism sheaf of $x|_U$. Therefore $\mathcal I_{\sigma,x}$ is a $\Band$-torsor. This is the usual Isom-torsor construction for a banded stack \cite[Chap.~III]{MacLaneMoerdijk1994}, \cite[Tag 04TU]{StacksProject}.
 119: 
 120: The nonabelian cohomology set $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$ classifies $\Band$-torsors on $\mathcal C_a$ up to isomorphism. Since $\Band$ is here an abelian sheaf, the distinguished point $0\in H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$ is the class of the trivial torsor. If $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)=0$, every $\Band$-torsor is trivial; hence $\mathcal I_{\sigma,x}$ is isomorphic to the trivial torsor $\Band$ and has a global section. Such a section is exactly an isomorphism $\iota_r(y)\cong x$ in the terminal fibre $\mathfrak L_r(a)$.
 121: \end{proof}

 123: \begin{lemma}[Representing component sections by descent]\label{lem:component-section-descent-object}
 124: Let $\mathfrak P_r$ be a representative-rigid banded groupoid lift on
 125: $\mathcal C_a$, assume that $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is
 126: separated on the slice, and let
 127: \[
 128: \iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
 129: \]
 130: be the stackification map. Every section
 131: \[
 132: \xi\in\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)
 133: \]
 134: is represented by an object of the terminal stack fibre $\mathfrak L_r(a)$.
 135: \end{lemma}
 136: 
 137: \begin{proof}
 138: Let
 139: \[
 140: F:=F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
 141: \]
 142: The identification
 143: \[
 144: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
 145: \]
 146: from \Cref{prop:stackification-components} writes $\xi$ as a sheafified
 147: matching datum. We now use the compatible-representative plus--plus normal form
 148: explicitly, because a section of \(aF\) is not, for a general presheaf, a
 149: strict \(F\)-matching family on the first displayed cover. By
 150: \Cref{lem:strictify-component-representatives}, applied in the slice
 151: \(\mathcal C_a\), there is a
 152: covering family
 153: \[
 154: \{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
 155: \]
 156: and sections
 157: \[
 158: \sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(U_i)
 159: \]
 160: such that the sheaf sections \(u_{U_i}(\sigma_i)\) glue to \(\xi\), and
 161: such that for every pair \(i,j\), with
 162: \[
 163: U_{ij}:=U_i\times_a U_j,
 164: \]
 165: the two restrictions agree on the original overlap:
 166: \[
 167: \res_{U_{ij}}^{U_i}(\sigma_i)
 168: =
 169: \res_{U_{ij}}^{U_j}(\sigma_j)
 170: \qquad(\forall i,j),
 171: \]
 172: including the case where \(U_{ij}\) is the formal initial object
 173: representing an empty overlap. The cited choice of compatible representatives lemma is the
 174: point at which separatedness on the slice, rather than separatedness only at
 175: \(a\), is needed: the plus--plus representative first gives equality only
 176: after covers of the \(U_{ij}\), and separatedness at those overlap objects
 177: upgrades it to equality on the original \(U_{ij}\).
 178: Representative-rigidity supplies strict representatives
 179: \[
 180: y_i:=s_{U_i}(\sigma_i)\in\mathfrak P_r(U_i).
 181: \]
 182: On every overlap, strict functoriality gives equality of the restricted
 183: representatives
 184: \[
 185: y_i|_{U_{ij}}=s_{U_{ij}}(\sigma_i|_{U_{ij}})
 186: =s_{U_{ij}}(\sigma_j|_{U_{ij}})=y_j|_{U_{ij}}.
 187: \]
 188: These equalities are equalities in the fibre over the actual pullback
 189: object \(U_{ij}\). They are not merely equalities after a further cover of
 190: \(U_{ij}\). This is why the following identity arrows are legitimate
 191: cover-level descent arrows; without the preceding separatedness and
 192: compatible representatives, identity descent data on the displayed cover would not be
 193: defined.
 194: Taking the identity isomorphism of this common object on each
 195: $U_{ij}$ therefore gives the overlap arrow
 196: \[
 197: \theta_{ij}:y_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}y_j|_{U_{ij}}
 198: \]
 199: inside $\mathfrak L_r(U_{ij})$. On a triple overlap
 200: $U_{ijk}:=U_i\times_aU_j\times_aU_k$, the two composites
 201: \[
 202: \theta_{ik}|_{U_{ijk}},
 203: \qquad
 204: \theta_{jk}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ\theta_{ij}|_{U_{ijk}}
 205: \]
 206: are both the identity of the same restricted object, including when this
 207: triple overlap is the formal initial object. Thus the cocycle condition
 208: for descent is satisfied strictly. Since $\mathfrak L_r$ is a stack,
 209: this descent datum glues to an object
 210: \[
 211: x_\xi\in\mathfrak L_r(a).
 212: \]
 213: By construction, the connected-component class of $x_\xi$ is the original
 214: section $\xi$.
 215: \end{proof}

 217: \begin{theorem}[Rigidity of representative-rigid lifts over slice sites on which the restricted presheaf is separated]\label{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}
 218: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admissible at a state $p$, write
 219: \[
 220: a=[r]_p,
 221: \qquad
 222: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
 223: \]
 224: and let
 225: \[
 226: \mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
 227: \]
 228: be a representative-rigid banded groupoid lift with band $\Band$. Let
 229: \[
 230: u:F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\longrightarrow a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
 231: \]
 232: be the sheafification unit. Assume throughout this theorem that
 233: \[
 234: F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
 235: \]
 236: is separated on the slice in the sense of
 237: \Cref{def:separated-restriction}; equivalently, $F_{p,s}$ is
 238: separated at every object of the slice $\mathcal C_a$, including every
 239: cover member, every pullback overlap, and every refinement occurring below.
 240: Separatedness only at the terminal object $a$ is not sufficient for this
 241: theorem, and no assertion below is made under that weaker hypothesis.
 242: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 243: \item If $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$, then
 244: \[
 245: u_a:F_{p,s}(a)\to \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)
 246: \]
 247: is surjective.
 248: \item If
 249: \[
 250: H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)=0,
 251: \]
 252: then surjectivity of $u_a$ implies that $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially
 253: surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$.
 254: \end{enumerate}
 255: Under the same vanishing hypothesis the following are equivalent:
 256: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
 257: \item $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$;
 258: \item $u_a$ is bijective;
 259: \item $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ satisfies the sheaf gluing condition at
 260: the object $a$, that is, every matching family on every cover of $a$ has
 261: an amalgamation in $F_{p,s}(a)$; uniqueness follows from the standing
 262: separatedness on the slice at $a$.
 263: \end{enumerate}
 264: The last equivalence is not a consequence of separatedness at \(a\) alone.
 265: It uses separatedness at all cover members, pullback overlaps, and their
 266: refinements in the slice \(\mathcal C_a\).
 267: \end{theorem}
 268: 
 269: \begin{proof}
 270: Write
 271: \[
 272: \mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r).
 273: \]
 274: By \Cref{prop:stackification-component-unit-naturality}, the morphism of
 275: component sheaves induced by the stackification map
 276: \[
 277: \iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
 278: \]
 279: identifies with the sheafification unit
 280: \[
 281: u:F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\to a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
 282: \]
 283: 
 284: Assume first that $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$, and let
 285: \[
 286: \xi\in \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a).
 287: \]
 288: By \Cref{lem:component-section-descent-object}, choose an object
 289: \[
 290: x\in \mathfrak L_r(a)
 291: \]
 292: whose connected-component class is $\xi$. The cited lemma uses the
 293: plus--plus normal form of \Cref{lem:strict-sheafification-representatives}:
 294: first one represents $\xi$ by $F_{p,s}$-sections whose overlap equalities
 295: hold after local refinements, then separatedness on the slice upgrades those
 296: refined overlap equalities to a strict matching family, and only then does
 297: effective descent in the stackification produce the terminal object.
 298: Essential surjectivity of
 299: \[
 300: (\iota_r)_a:(\mathfrak P_r)_a\to (\mathfrak L_r)_a
 301: \]
 302: gives an object
 303: \[
 304: y\in \mathfrak P_r(a)
 305: \]
 306: with $\iota_r(y)\cong x$. Let
 307: \[
 308: \sigma:=[y]\in \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)\cong F_{p,s}(a).
 309: \]
 310: Since $u_a$ is the map on connected components induced by $\iota_r$, one has
 311: \[
 312: u_a(\sigma)=[\iota_r(y)]=[x]=\xi.
 313: \]
 314: Thus $u_a$ is surjective.
 315: 
 316: Assume next that $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)=0$ and that $u_a$ is surjective. Let
 317: \[
 318: x\in \mathfrak L_r(a).
 319: \]
 320: Its connected-component class
 321: \[
 322: [x]\in \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)
 323: \]
 324: lies in the image of $u_a$, so choose
 325: \[
 326: \sigma\in F_{p,s}(a)
 327: \]
 328: with
 329: \[
 330: u_a(\sigma)=[x].
 331: \]
 332: Put
 333: \[
 334: y:=s_a(\sigma)\in \mathfrak P_r(a).
 335: \]
 336: By construction, $y$ represents the class $\sigma$ in $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)$, hence
 337: \[
 338: [\iota_r(y)]=u_a(\sigma)=[x]
 339: \]
 340: in $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$. By \Cref{lem:canonical-lift-isom-torsor}, the sheaf
 341: \[
 342: \underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathfrak L_r}(\iota_r(y),x)
 343: \]
 344: is a $\Band$-torsor, and the vanishing of $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$ gives a global section of it. Equivalently, there exists an isomorphism
 345: \[
 346: \iota_r(y)\xrightarrow{\sim} x
 347: \]
 348: in $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Thus every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ is in the essential image of $(\iota_r)_a$, so $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$.
 349: 
 350: The standing separatedness on the slice also gives injectivity of the unit at the
 351: terminal object. If
 352: \[
 353: u_a(\sigma)=u_a(\tau)
 354: \qquad
 355: (\sigma,\tau\in F_{p,s}(a)),
 356: \]
 357: then the two global sections define the same element of the sheafification at $a$.
 358: Applying \Cref{lem:sheafification-unit-equality-local} gives a cover
 359: \[
 360: \{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
 361: \]
 362: such that
 363: \[
 364: \res_{U_i}^a(\sigma)=\res_{U_i}^a(\tau)
 365: \qquad
 366: (\forall i\in I).
 367: \]
 368: Separatedness on the slice applies in particular at the terminal object
 369: $a$, and therefore forces $\sigma=\tau$. Thus $u_a$ is injective.
 370: 
 371: Under $H^1(\mathcal C_a,\Band)=0$, part \textup{(i)} gives
 372: \textup{(a)}$\Rightarrow$\textup{(b)}, and part \textup{(ii)} together
 373: with injectivity gives \textup{(b)}$\Rightarrow$\textup{(a)}. It remains
 374: to identify \textup{(b)} with the terminal sheaf axiom, and we spell this
 375: out because this is the point where separatedness on the slice is
 376: used beyond the terminal object.
 377: 
 378: Assume \textup{(b)}, and let
 379: \[
 380: \{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
 381: \qquad
 382: \sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(U_i)
 383: \]
 384: be a strict matching family on a cover of \(a\). Applying \(u\) to the
 385: \(\sigma_i\) gives a matching family in the sheaf
 386: \(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\), hence a unique section
 387: \[
 388: \xi\in \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)
 389: \]
 390: whose restriction to \(U_i\) is \(u_{U_i}(\sigma_i)\). By surjectivity of
 391: \(u_a\), choose \(\sigma\in F_{p,s}(a)\) with \(u_a(\sigma)=\xi\). For
 392: each \(i\),
 393: \[
 394: u_{U_i}\bigl(\res_{U_i}^{a}\sigma\bigr)=u_{U_i}(\sigma_i)
 395: \]
 396: in \((a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(U_i)\). This equality is not an equality in
 397: \(F_{p,s}(U_i)\). By \Cref{lem:sheafification-unit-equality-local},
 398: there is a covering family
 399: \[
 400: \{V_{ik}\to U_i\}_{k}
 401: \]
 402: such that
 403: \[
 404: \res_{V_{ik}}^{a}\sigma=\res_{V_{ik}}^{U_i}\sigma_i
 405: \qquad(\forall k)
 406: \]
 407: in \(F_{p,s}(V_{ik})\). Since \(U_i\) is an object of the slice
 408: \(\mathcal C_a\) and the standing hypothesis is separatedness on the slice,
 409: \(F_{p,s}\) is separated at \(U_i\). The displayed local equalities over
 410: the cover of \(U_i\) therefore force
 411: \[
 412: \res_{U_i}^{a}\sigma=\sigma_i
 413: \]
 414: in \(F_{p,s}(U_i)\). Thus \(\sigma\) is an amalgamation of the original
 415: matching family. Its uniqueness follows from separatedness at \(a\).
 416: Therefore \textup{(c)} holds.
 417: 
 418: Conversely, assume \textup{(c)} and let
 419: \[
 420: \xi\in \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a).
 421: \]
 422: By the plus--plus normal form of
 423: \Cref{lem:strict-sheafification-representatives}, \(\xi\) is represented
 424: on a cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\) by sections
 425: \(\sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(U_i)\) whose restrictions to each overlap
 426: \[
 427: U_{ij}:=U_i\times_aU_j
 428: \]
 429: agree after a further covering family of \(U_{ij}\). Each \(U_{ij}\) is an
 430: object of the slice \(\mathcal C_a\), so separatedness on the slice and
 431: \Cref{lem:separated-restriction-refined-equality} upgrade these refined
 432: equalities to equalities on the original overlaps. Hence the
 433: \(\sigma_i\) form a strict matching family on the displayed cover. By the
 434: sheaf axiom at \(a\), there is an amalgamation
 435: \(\sigma\in F_{p,s}(a)\). The sections \(u_a(\sigma)\) and \(\xi\) have
 436: the same restrictions to the cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\), so separatedness of
 437: the sheaf \(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\) gives \(u_a(\sigma)=\xi\). Thus \(u_a\) is
 438: surjective, and its injectivity was proved above. Therefore
 439: \textup{(b)} holds.
 440: \end{proof}
 441: 
 442: \begin{corollary}[Matching without amalgamation requires noncanonical lift data]\label{cor:no-rigid-gluing-null}
 443: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admissible at a state $p$, write
 444: \[
 445: a=[r]_p,
 446: \qquad
 447: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
 448: \]
 449: assume that $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is separated on the slice. If
 450: \[
 451: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
 452: \]
 453: then no representative-rigid banded groupoid lift with band $\Band$ can be essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$.
 454: \end{corollary}
 455: 
 456: \begin{proof}
 457: The condition
 458: \[
 459: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
 460: \]
 461: means that $r$ is admissible, that
 462: \[
 463: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r),
 464: \]
 465: and that
 466: \[
 467: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
 468: \]
 469: By \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization},
 470: \[
 471: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\neq\varnothing,
 472: \]
 473: whereas \Cref{def:existence-levels}(iii) gives
 474: \[
 475: F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing.
 476: \]
 477: Hence the unit map
 478: \[
 479: u_a:F_{p,s}(a)\to \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)
 480: \]
 481: cannot be surjective. Since separatedness on the slice is part of the present
 482: hypotheses, the contrapositive of
 483: \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}(i) therefore excludes essential
 484: surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ for every representative-rigid banded groupoid lift
 485: with band $\Band$.
 486: This is not contradicted by the vacuous terminal-fibre essential-surjectivity examples used
 487: later: in those examples the prestack and stack terminal fibres are both
 488: empty. Representative-rigidity is the extra hypothesis that rules out that
 489: vacuous case when a sheafified terminal component exists. Indeed, if such a
 490: prestack were representative-rigid, then
 491: \Cref{lem:component-section-descent-object} would turn the sheafified terminal
 492: component into an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$, contradicting the equality
 493: $\mathfrak P_r(a)=\varnothing=\mathfrak L_r(a)$.
 494: \end{proof}
 495: 
 496: \begin{remark}[What remains conditional]\label{rem:gluing-sensitive-lifts}
 497: \Cref{prop:split-banded-groupoid-lift} constructs a split prestack for every
 498: presheaf \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) and every abelian sheaf \(\Band\).
 499: Separatedness on the slice is needed exactly for this split prestack to be
 500: separated as a prestack in groupoids. The split construction is not
 501: gluing-sensitive: it records the prescribed component presheaf and band, but
 502: it does not by itself supply the additional gerbe data, acyclic-cover
 503: comparisons, or terminal-fibre essential-surjectivity hypotheses used later. The
 504: gerbe-theoretic and homological statements are therefore relative to chosen
 505: banded lift data satisfying those extra hypotheses.
 506: \end{remark}

   1: \begin{theorem}[Typed-expansion construction with neutral and non-neutral component gerbes on a finite intersection site]\label{thm:mixed-component-construction}
   2: Let
   3: \[
   4: \mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
   5: \]
   6: be a finite good-cover presentation in a pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$ whose nonempty \v{C}ech nerve
   7: \[

  14: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}; it contains the strict

  57: \[
