 101: \begin{proof}
 102: Since
 103: \[
 104: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 105: \]
 106: the universal coefficient sequence reduces to an isomorphism
 107: \[
 108: \eta_A:H^2(N,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A).
 109: \]
 110: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, let
 111: \[
 112: \omega_\lambda\in H^2(N,A)
 113: \]
 114: be the unique class satisfying
 115: \[
 116: \eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 117: \]
 118: and choose the normalized representative as follows. If
 119: \(\lambda\in\Lambda_0\), set
 120: \[
 121: \alpha_\lambda:=0\in Z^2(N,A).
 122: \]
 123: If \(\lambda\notin\Lambda_0\), choose any normalized simplicial cocycle
 124: \[
 125: \alpha_\lambda\in Z^2(N,A)
 126: \]
 127: representing \(\omega_\lambda\), with the alternating ordered-triple
 128: extension of \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}. Thus
 129: \[
 130: \lambda\in\Lambda_0
 131: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 132: \omega_\lambda=0,
 133: \]
 134: and, by the normalization just stipulated rather than by an arbitrary choice
 135: of representative, the labels in \(\Lambda_0\) are exactly the labels for
 136: which the construction uses the zero cocycle \(\alpha_\lambda=0\). For
 137: \(\lambda\notin\Lambda_0\) the chosen class is nonzero, so any representing
 138: cocycle is nonzero. No assertion is made that every normalized cocycle
 139: representing the zero cohomology class is itself zero.
 140: 
 141: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(i)--(iv), pass to the
 142: finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ appearing in the statement.
 143: The cover $\mathcal U$, its nerve, and the constant-band finite cochain
 144: data are the same, and Leray comparison identifies
 145: $H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})$ with $H^2(N,A)$. The derived component obstruction class
 146: used below is therefore the actual derived class corresponding to the
 147: chosen finite-nerve cocycle.
 148: 
 149: Define the presheaf of local sections
 150: \[
 151: F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
 152: \]
 153: by
 154: \[
 155: F_{p,s}(U):=\Lambda
 156: \qquad
 157: \text{for every nonempty proper intersection object }U\to a,
 158: \]
 159: \[
 160: F_{p,s}(a):=\Lambda_0,
 161: \]
 162: and
 163: \[
 164: F_{p,s}(\emptyset):=\{\ast\}.
 165: \]
 166: Restrictions between nonempty proper intersection objects are identities,
 167: the restriction maps
 168: \[
 169: F_{p,s}(a)\to F_{p,s}(U)
 170: \]
 171: are the inclusions $\Lambda_0\hookrightarrow \Lambda$, and every
 172: restriction to $\emptyset$ is the unique map.
 173: 
 174: This is the presheaf \(F_{\Lambda_0}\) of
 175: \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification}. That lemma uses the plus--plus
 176: description of sheafification and the strict initial object for empty
 177: pullbacks, so no one-step matching-family description is being assumed.
 178: Since the nonempty nerve is connected, it gives
 179: \[
 180: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 181: \]

 183: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda\setminus\Lambda_0$, define a category fibred in groupoids
 184: \[
 185: \mathfrak P_\lambda\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 186: \]
 187: exactly as in the proof of \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}: on the terminal fibre set
 188: \[

 190: \]

 192: \[

 196: \[

 198: \]

 200: connected nonempty \(W\), and composition twisted by the cocycle
 201: \(\alpha_\lambda\) under this identification. Over $\emptyset$ take the
 202: terminal groupoid, with unique restrictions to it. The argument of
 203: \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction} shows that $\mathfrak P_\lambda$
 204: is a prestack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$, that
 205: \[
 206: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_\lambda)(U)\cong\{ \lambda\}
 207: \]
 208: for every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$, that
 209: \[
 210: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_\lambda)(a)=\varnothing,
 211: \]
 212: that the fibre over $\emptyset$ is terminal, and that the \v{C}ech cocycle
 213: attached to the component is exactly $\alpha_\lambda$. By
 214: \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}, the corresponding
 215: isomorphism and automorphism presheaves on every slice are restrictions of
 216: the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$, so no constant-presheaf
 217: sheaf condition is being assumed.
 218: 
 219: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, define a stack in groupoids
 220: \[
 221: \mathfrak P_\lambda\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 222: \]
 223: by taking, for every nonempty object $U$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, a one-object groupoid with distinguished object $y_U^{(\lambda)}$ and automorphism group $A_{\mathcal U}(U)$, by taking the terminal groupoid over $\emptyset$, and by taking every restriction between nonempty objects to be the restriction map of the genuine constant sheaf on the distinguished object and on automorphisms. Restrictions to $\emptyset$ are unique. By \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}, this neutral one-object prestack is a stack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$: object descent is governed by \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles on slices, and those torsors are trivial because \(H^1(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W,A_{\mathcal U})=0\) for every relevant object \(W\). Thus
 224: \[
 225: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_\lambda)(U)\cong\{\lambda\}
 226: \]
 227: for every nonempty object $U$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, has terminal component set over $\emptyset$, and the \v{C}ech cocycle on the cover $\mathcal U$ is identically zero.
 228: 
 229: Now set
 230: \[
 231: \mathfrak P_r:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
 232: \]
 233: As in \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}, this is the fibrewise
 234: coproduct over nonempty objects with the shared terminal fibre over
 235: $\emptyset$.
 236: By \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}, this coproduct is a prestack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$: the nonzero summands are the twisted groupoids determined by the chosen representatives $\alpha_\lambda$, the neutral summands are indexed by those \(\lambda\in\Lambda_0\) for which we explicitly set \(\alpha_\lambda=0\), the restriction maps are strictly functorial, and the Cech cocycle of the $\lambda$-component is the chosen $\alpha_\lambda$. Since distinct summands have no morphisms between them, its presheaf of isomorphism classes is
 237: \[
 238: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(U)\cong \Lambda
 239: \qquad
 240: \text{for every nonempty proper intersection object }U\to a,
 241: \]

 244: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)\cong \Lambda_0.
 245: \]

 251: \]
 252: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(v)--(vi), the functor

 259: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}, and no independently
 260: restricted semantic model class is being used.
 261: The construction has now supplied the same interfaces as in the prescribed case: admissible parameter $r$, finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$, genuine constant sheaf band $A_{\mathcal U}$, the Leray comparison isomorphism for the cover $\mathcal U$, component sections obtained from sheafified terminal sections, and satisfaction clauses determined by compatible local sections and actual terminal sections.
 262: Applying \Cref{prop:stackification-components} gives
 263: \[
 264: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s},
 265: \]
 266: so
 267: \[
 268: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 269: \]
 270: This proves \textup{(i)}.
 271: 
 272: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda\setminus\Lambda_0$, the same calculation as in \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ has component obstruction class
 273: \[

 275: \]

 277: \[
 278: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=\eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 279: \qquad

 283: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}
 284: shows that the neutral one-object construction is a genuine neutral

 286: $y_{U_i}^{(\lambda)}$ together with the identity isomorphisms on overlaps
 287: yields the zero \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle. Hence
 288: \[
 289: \omega_\lambda=0,
 290: \qquad
 291: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=0=\phi_\lambda,
 292: \qquad
 293: K_\lambda=0=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 294: \]
 295: The neutrality criterion in
 296: \artresult{Derived component classes detect neutrality} therefore gives
 297: \[
 298: \mathfrak G_\lambda\ \text{is neutral}
 299: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 300: \omega_\lambda=0
 301: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 302: \phi_\lambda=0.
 303: \]
 304: This proves \textup{(ii)}.
 305: 
 306: The identity
 307: \[
 308: F_{p,s}(a)=\Lambda_0
 309: \]
 310: immediately gives
 311: \[
 312: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
 313: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 314: \Lambda_0\neq\varnothing.
 315: \]
 316: It remains to prove essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$. If \(\lambda\in\Lambda_0\),
 317: the preceding paragraph and \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1} identify
 318: \(\mathfrak P_\lambda\) with its own stackification on the terminal slice:
 319: every object descent datum has a trivial \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor class, and
 320: morphism descent is the sheaf condition for \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Hence the
 321: restriction of the stackification morphism to the fibre over \(a\) is an
 322: equivalence on that summand. If $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, then
 323: $\phi_\lambda\neq 0$, hence $\omega_\lambda\neq 0$, and
 324: \artresult{Derived component classes detect neutrality} implies that the component gerbe
 325: $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ is non-neutral. Therefore
 326: \[
 327: \mathfrak G_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
 328: \qquad
 329: (\lambda\notin\Lambda_0)
 330: \]
 331: by \artresult{Terminal-fibre nonemptiness and neutrality}. Consequently every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in a neutral component and is therefore in the essential image of $\mathfrak P_r(a)$. Thus $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$. This proves \textup{(iii)}.
 332: 
 333: Since $\Lambda\neq\varnothing$, the identification
 334: \[
 335: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda
 336: \]
 337: shows that
 338: \[

 340: \]

 342: every member $U_i$ of the cover $\mathcal U$. The restriction maps between

 352: \]

 354: \[
 355: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
 356: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad

 358: \]
 359: This proves \textup{(iv)}.

 361: Finally, \textup{(v)} follows by applying

 363: to the family
 364: \[
 365: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)
 366: \qquad

 368: \qedhere

 372: \begin{corollary}[Exact subgroup classification on torsion-free second homology]\label{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification}
 373: Assume the full hypotheses of \Cref{thm:mixed-component-construction}: a
 374: fixed finite nerve $N=N(\mathcal U)$ in the finite intersection site associated to a good-cover nerve,
 375: a trivialized constant finite abelian band $A$, the Leray comparison
 376: isomorphism for the finite-nerve classes, the constructed banded groupoid
 377: lift, and essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre. Assume
 378: in addition that
 379: \[
 380: H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
 381: \]
 382: for some integer $\beta\ge 0$. Let $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be a family of subgroups of $A$. Then the following are equivalent.
 383: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 384: \item There exist a state $p$, an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ on the fixed nerve $N$, and a bijection
 385: \[
 386: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \Lambda
 387: \]
 388: such that the component indexed by $\lambda$ has presentation-relative homological image subgroup
 389: \[
 390: K_\lambda.
 391: \]
 392: \item Every subgroup $K_\lambda$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements.
 393: \end{enumerate}
 394: When these conditions hold,
 395: \[
 396: Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\cong A\Big/\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
 397: \qquad
 398: Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\cong A\Big/\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
 399: \]
 400: and
 401: \[
 402: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
 403: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 404: K_\lambda=0\ \text{for some}\ \lambda\in\Lambda.
 405: \]
 406: In particular, a single component attains surjective homological evaluation
 407: \[
 408: K_\omega=A
 409: \]
 410: if and only if $A$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. For $\beta=1$, the attainable single-component presentation-relative homological image subgroups are exactly the cyclic subgroups of $A$.
 411: \end{corollary}
 412: 
 413: \begin{proof}
 414: Assume \textup{(i)}. For any component on the fixed finite nerve satisfying the
 415: finite-nerve comparison hypotheses, its presentation-relative homological image subgroup is by
 416: definition the image of the homological evaluation map attached to its component section
 417: obstruction class. Since
 418: \[
 419: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 420: \]
 421: the universal coefficient comparison identifies that evaluation map with a
 422: homomorphism from $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)$ to $A$. Thus, for each $\lambda$, there
 423: exists a homomorphism
 424: \[
 425: \phi_\lambda:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
 426: \]
 427: with
 428: \[
 429: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 430: \]
 431: After choosing an identification
 432: \[
 433: H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta,
 434: \]
 435: the image of $\phi_\lambda$ is generated by the images of the $\beta$ standard basis vectors. Hence $K_\lambda$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. Therefore \textup{(ii)} holds.
 436: 
 437: Assume conversely that \textup{(ii)} holds. For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose generators
 438: \[
 439: k_{\lambda,1},\dots,k_{\lambda,\beta}\in K_\lambda
 440: \]
 441: of $K_\lambda$, allowing repetitions and zeros when fewer than $\beta$ generators are needed. Define
 442: \[
 443: \phi_\lambda:\mathbb Z^\beta\to A,
 444: \qquad
 445: (n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto \sum_{j=1}^{\beta} n_j k_{\lambda,j}.
 446: \]
 447: Then
 448: \[
 449: \operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)=K_\lambda.
 450: \]
 451: Transporting these maps across the chosen isomorphism
 452: \[
 453: H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
 454: \]
 455: and applying \Cref{thm:mixed-component-construction} yields the required state $p$, admissible parameter $r$, and family of component sections. Hence \textup{(i)} holds.
 456: 
 457: The quotient formulas are those of \Cref{thm:mixed-component-construction}(v). The global-section criterion follows from \Cref{thm:mixed-component-construction}(iii), because
 458: \[
 459: K_\lambda=0
 460: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 461: \operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)=0
 462: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 463: \phi_\lambda=0.
 464: \]
 465: For the surjective-evaluation claim, take $\Lambda$ to be a singleton and $K_\omega=A$. Then the equivalence between \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} says exactly that such a component exists if and only if $A$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The final sentence is the case $\beta=1$.
 466: \end{proof}

 succeeded in 218ms:
   1: \begin{lemma}[$2$-cocycle-defined banded prestack for one component]\label{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}
   2: Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite cover whose nerve $N$ is connected, let $A$ be a finite abelian group, let $\Lambda$ be a finite nonempty label set, and let
   3: \[
   4: \alpha_\lambda\in Z^2(N,A)
   5: \qquad
   6: (\lambda\in\Lambda)
   7: \]
   8: be normalized simplicial cocycles. Assume also that
   9: \[
  10: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0.
  11: \]
  12: We use their alternating extension to all
  13: ordered triples of indices: for pairwise distinct indices, permuting an
  14: ordered simplex multiplies the value by the sign of the permutation, and any
  15: triple with a repeated index has value $0$. Let
  16: \[
  17: A_{\mathcal U}
  18: \]
  19: denote the genuine constant sheaf on $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, i.e. the
  20: sheaf of locally constant $A$-valued functions on the chosen good-cover
  21: geometric realization restricted to the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve. Hence
  22: $A_{\mathcal U}(U_J)=A$ for each nonempty basic intersection and
  23: $A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0$.
  24: Let
  25: \[
  26: \Lambda_0:=\{\lambda\in\Lambda\mid \alpha_\lambda=0\}.
  27: \]
  28: On the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, define $F$ by
  29: \[
  30: F(W)=
  31: \begin{cases}
  32: \Lambda,& W\to a\text{ a nonempty proper formal intersection object},\\
  33: \Lambda_0,& W=a,\\
  34: \{\ast\},& W=\emptyset,
  35: \end{cases}
  36: \]
  37: with identity restrictions among nonempty proper intersection objects,
  38: inclusions $\Lambda_0\hookrightarrow\Lambda$ from $a$ to nonempty proper
  39: intersections, and the unique restriction map to $F(\emptyset)$. For each
  40: $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, define a fibred groupoid $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ by
  41: \[
  42: \mathfrak P_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
  43: \]
  44: and, for every nonempty proper object $W$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, put
  45: \[
  46: I(W):=\{i\in I\mid W\to U_i\text{ in }\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\}.
  47: \]
  48: Thus $I(U_J)=J$ for a formal intersection object. Define objects
  49: \[
  50: x_i^{(\lambda,W)}\qquad (i\in I(W))
  51: \]
  52: and morphism sets
  53: \[
  54: \mathrm{Hom}\bigl(x_i^{(\lambda,W)},x_j^{(\lambda,W)}\bigr)
  55: =A_{\mathcal U}(W),
  56: \]
  57: which is identified with \(A\) because \(W\) is a connected nonempty
  58: basic intersection. With this identification, write morphisms as
  59: \((a,i,j)\) with \(a\in A\), and define composition by
  60: \[
  61: (b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)=(a+b+\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,k).
  62: \]
  63: For a morphism $V\to W$, one has $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, because a map
  64: $W\to U_i$ composes with $V\to W$. Restrictions therefore send
  65: $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ to $x_i^{(\lambda,V)}$ and $(a,i,j)$ to the same
  66: coefficient-labelled morphism after applying the restriction map of
  67: \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Over $\emptyset$ take the terminal groupoid and let
  68: every restriction to $\emptyset$ be the unique functor. For each
  69: $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, let $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ be the neutral stack with
  70: one object over every object and automorphism group
  71: \(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\) over \(W\), so the fibre over \(\emptyset\) is
  72: terminal because \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). Restrictions are exactly
  73: the restriction maps of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Its stack property is
  74: the \(H^1\)-vanishing criterion of
  75: \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}: object descent data are
  76: \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles on slices, and those torsors are
  77: trivial on the formal good-cover slices used here. Its automorphism sheaf is
  78: therefore the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$. Set
  79: \[
  80: \mathfrak P:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
  81: \]
  82: This denotes the fibrewise coproduct over every nonempty object, while over
  83: $\emptyset$ the summands share the single terminal fibre and all
  84: restrictions to $\emptyset$ are the unique functor. The band used below is
  85: the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ on the finite intersection site, not the
  86: identity-restriction constant presheaf.
  87: Then:
  88: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  89: \item each nonzero summand $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ is a category fibred in groupoids, and the pullback functors are strictly functorial;
  90: \item the identity, inverse, and associativity laws in each twisted fibre are respectively the normalized identities
  91: \[
  92: \alpha_{\lambda,iij}=\alpha_{\lambda,ijj}=0,
  93: \qquad
  94: \alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0,
  95: \]
  96: and the cocycle identity
  97: \[
  98: \alpha_{\lambda,jkl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
  99: +\alpha_{\lambda,ijl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}=0;
 100: \]
 101: \item $\mathfrak P$ is a prestack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$;
 102: \item its presheaf of connected components is $F$;
 103: \item after stackification, the components over $a$ are naturally indexed by $\Lambda$, and the component indexed by $\lambda$ has \v{C}ech cocycle $\alpha_\lambda$ on $\mathcal U$.
 104: \end{enumerate}
 105: \end{lemma}
 106: 
 107: \begin{proof}
 108: The sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ is fixed as part of the finite intersection site interface in
 109: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iii)--(iv). Since every
 110: nonempty object of the finite intersection site is represented by a connected
 111: contractible intersection of the good cover, locally constant
 112: $A$-valued functions on it are exactly constant functions with value in
 113: $A$; the strict initial object has only the zero section. Thus the
 114: coefficient notation $A$ below is shorthand for the actual sheaf sections
 115: $A_{\mathcal U}(W)$ on nonempty basic objects, not for the
 116: identity-restriction constant presheaf on an arbitrary site; equivalently,
 117: we are using \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding} throughout.
 118: In particular, whenever an isomorphism or automorphism presheaf below is
 119: written as \(A\) on nonempty objects and \(0\) on \(\emptyset\), it is
 120: defined by the displayed identification with
 121: \(A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}\). The prestack condition is
 122: therefore a sheaf condition for a genuine sheaf on each slice, not a
 123: claim that the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the index
 124: category is already a sheaf.
 125: 
 126: For a nonempty proper formal intersection object $W$ and a fixed
 127: $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, the displayed formula makes every morphism
 128: invertible. The identity at $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ is $(0,i,i)$ because the
 129: cocycle is normalized on repeated indices. The inverse of $(a,i,j)$ is
 130: $(-a,j,i)$, again because the repeated-index normalization gives
 131: $\alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0$. Associativity of
 132: \[
 133: (c,k,l)\circ\bigl((b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)\bigr)
 134: \quad\text{and}\quad
 135: \bigl((c,k,l)\circ(b,j,k)\bigr)\circ(a,i,j)
 136: \]
 137: is equivalent, after cancelling $a+b+c$, to
 138: \[
 139: \alpha_{\lambda,ijk}+\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
 140: =
 141: \alpha_{\lambda,jkl}+\alpha_{\lambda,ijl},
 142: \]
 143: which is the displayed cocycle identity, interpreted under the alternating
 144: ordered-triple convention just fixed. This proves that each fibre is a
 145: groupoid. If $V\to W$, then $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, so every object and
 146: morphism named over $W$ has the same name over $V$. The restriction maps
 147: therefore preserve labels and restrict coefficients through the map
 148: \(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\to A_{\mathcal U}(V)\). Under the connected
 149: intersection identifications these coefficient restrictions are the
 150: identity maps \(A\to A\) on nonempty objects; for restrictions to
 151: \(\emptyset\) they are the unique maps to \(0\). Thus the same ordered
 152: simplex indices are used wherever a nonempty coefficient is present, so
 153: restrictions preserve identities, inverses, and composition. Since
 154: inclusions \(I(W)\subseteq I(V)\) are transitive and
 155: \(A_{\mathcal U}\) is a sheaf with functorial restrictions, restrictions
 156: compose strictly. This proves \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}.
 157: 
 158: For each pair of objects in a twisted fibre over a nonempty object $W$, the
 159: isomorphism presheaf on the slice \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W\) is defined
 160: objectwise by
 161: \[
 162: V\longmapsto A_{\mathcal U}(V),
 163: \]
 164: with restrictions those of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\), whenever the two
 165: restricted labels are both defined; over \(\emptyset\) this gives the
 166: single section of \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). On connected nonempty
 167: basic intersections this is the coefficient notation \(A\), but the
 168: presheaf itself is the restriction of the genuine constant sheaf
 169: \(A_{\mathcal U}\), not the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the
 170: index category. By
 171: \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}, it is therefore a sheaf.
 172: The same argument applies to automorphisms,
 173: where the distinguished zero coefficient gives a canonical identification
 174: \[
 175: \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(x_i^{(\lambda,W)})
 176: \cong A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}.
 177: \]
 178: Thus the prestack condition and the banding use the genuine constant sheaf
 179: $A_{\mathcal U}$. The neutral summands indexed by \(\Lambda_0\) are stacks by
 180: \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}. This invokes object descent, not
 181: only morphism descent: a one-object \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-banded prestack has
 182: descent data classified by \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles, and those
 183: torsors are trivial on every relevant slice. Taking the finite coproduct
 184: over nonempty objects and the shared terminal fibre over $\emptyset$ preserves the prestack
 185: condition: over nonempty objects this is the usual finite coproduct of
 186: prestacks in groupoids, while the strict initial object has only the unique
 187: matching datum. This proves \textup{(iii)} without any appeal to a
 188: constant presheaf sheaf condition.
 189: 
 190: For every nonempty proper intersection object, each twisted summand is
 191: connected and each neutral summand is one connected component; there are no
 192: morphisms between distinct summands. Over $\emptyset$ the shared terminal
 193: fibre has the unique lift object over the empty intersection, matching $F(\emptyset)=\{\ast\}$.
 194: Hence
 195: \[
 196: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(U)\cong\Lambda
 197: \]
 198: for every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$. Over $a$, the
 199: nonzero summands have empty fibre and the neutral summands indexed by
 200: \(\Lambda_0\) have one object, so
 201: \[
 202: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong\Lambda_0.
 203: \]
 204: These identifications are compatible with the restriction maps, giving \textup{(iv)}.
 205: 
 206: By \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification}, applied to the displayed
 207: presheaf \(F\) and the subset \(\Lambda_0\subseteq\Lambda\), the
 208: sheafification of \(F\) has terminal sections indexed by \(\Lambda\). By
 209: \Cref{prop:stackification-components}, stackification identifies
 210: \[
 211: \pi_0(a(\mathfrak P))\cong aF,
 212: \]
 213: so the components over $a$ are indexed by $\Lambda$.
 214: 
 215: For a fixed $\lambda$, take on $U_i$ the object $x_i^{(\lambda,U_i)}$ if $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$ and the distinguished constant object if $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$. On $U_{ij}$ take the morphism $(0,i,j)$ in the nonzero case and the identity in the zero case. The triple defect is
 216: \[
 217: (0,i,k)^{-1}\circ(0,j,k)\circ(0,i,j)
 218: =
 219: (\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,i)
 220: \]
 221: in the twisted case and is $0$ in the constant case. Under the band identification this is exactly $\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}$. Thus the Cech obstruction cocycle of the $\lambda$-component is $\alpha_\lambda$, proving \textup{(v)}.
 222: \end{proof}
 223: 
 224: \begin{theorem}[Construction with prescribed componentwise homological image subgroups]\label{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}
 225: Let
 226: \[
 227: \mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
 228: \]
 229: be a finite good-cover presentation in a pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$ whose nonempty \v{C}ech nerve
 230: \[
 231: N:=N(\mathcal U)
 232: \]
 233: is connected. Equivalently, the geometric realization of the cover nerve is a
 234: paracompact space homotopy equivalent to $|N|$ and all nonempty finite
 235: intersections of members of $\mathcal U$ are acyclic for constant
 236: coefficients. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ be the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve of
 237: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}; it includes the strict
 238: initial object $\emptyset$ for all empty intersections, so disjoint cover
 239: members have a pullback in the site even though they do not contribute a
 240: nonzero finite-nerve cochain. Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, and let
 241: $A_{\mathcal U}$ denote the genuine constant sheaf on
 242: $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ whose value on each nonempty basic intersection
 243: is identified with $A$. View $A_{\mathcal U}$ as the automorphism band of
 244: the banded groupoid lift constructed below, and assume
 245: \[
 246: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0.
 247: \]
 248: Use the Leray comparison isomorphism of
 249: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv). Let $\Lambda$ be a finite nonempty set, and let
 250: \[
 251: \phi_\lambda:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
 252: \]
 253: be a nonzero homomorphism for each $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then, in the
 254: typed-expansion model class generated by
 255: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}, the following typed data
 256: define a one-state $\mathbb L_2/\mathbb L_3$ model \(M\): the one-state
 257: \(\mathbb L_1\)-reduct, the finite intersection site \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), the
 258: presheaf of local sections \(F_{p,s}\) constructed below, and the banded groupoid lift
 259: prestack
 260: \[
 261: \mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 262: \]
 263: with band \(A_{\mathcal U}\). In that generated model there are a state
 264: \(p\) and a distinguished admissible parameter \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\) with
 265: \([r]_p=a\), local slice site \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), and
 266: \(\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)\), such that the following hold:
 267: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 268: \item
 269: \[
 270: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \Lambda;
 271: \]
 272: \item under the identification in \textup{(i)}, for each $\lambda\in\Lambda$ the corresponding component gerbe $\mathfrak G_\lambda\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ has component obstruction class
 273: \[
 274: \omega_\lambda\in H^2(N,A)
 275: \]
 276: satisfying
 277: \[
 278: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=\phi_\lambda,
 279: \qquad
 280: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda);
 281: \]
 282: \item $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ by the vacuous terminal-fibre case
 283: \[
 284: \mathfrak P_r(a)=\varnothing=\mathfrak L_r(a),
 285: \]
 286: and
 287: \[
 288: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r);
 289: \]
 290: \item the aggregate quotients satisfy
 291: \[
 292: Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\cong A\Big/\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda),
 293: \qquad
 294: Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\cong A\Big/\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 295: \]
 296: \end{enumerate}
 297: In particular, within the fixed finite-nerve and typed-expansion
 298: framework above, every finite family of subgroups of $A$ arising as images of homomorphisms
 299: \[
 300: H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
 301: \]
 302: is attained as the family of presentation-relative homological image subgroups of the global component sections of one admissible parameter.
 303: \end{theorem}
 304: 
 305: \begin{proof}
 306: Since
 307: \[
 308: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 309: \]
 310: the universal coefficient sequence reduces to an isomorphism
 311: \[
 312: \eta_A:H^2(N,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A).
 313: \]
 314: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose the unique class
 315: \[
 316: \omega_\lambda\in H^2(N,A)
 317: \]
 318: with
 319: \[
 320: \eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 321: \]
 322: and choose a normalized simplicial cocycle
 323: \[
 324: \alpha_\lambda\in Z^2(N,A)
 325: \]
 326: representing $\omega_\lambda$, with the alternating ordered-triple extension
 327: of \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}.
 328: 
 329: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(i)--(iv), pass to the
 330: finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ appearing in the statement.
 331: The cover $\mathcal U$, its nerve, and the constant-band finite cochain
 332: data are the same, and Leray comparison identifies
 333: $H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})$ with $H^2(N,A)$. The derived component obstruction class
 334: used below is therefore the actual derived class corresponding to the
 335: chosen finite-nerve cocycle.
 336: 
 337: Define the presheaf of local sections
 338: \[
 339: F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
 340: \]
 341: by
 342: \[
 343: F_{p,s}(U):=\Lambda
 344: \qquad
 345: \text{for every nonempty proper intersection object }U\to a,
 346: \]
 347: \[
 348: F_{p,s}(a):=\varnothing,
 349: \]
 350: and
 351: \[
 352: F_{p,s}(\emptyset):=\{\ast\}.
 353: \]
 354: Restrictions between nonempty proper intersection objects are identities,
 355: and every restriction to $\emptyset$ is the unique map. This is the
 356: presheaf \(F_{\Lambda_0}\) of
 357: \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification} with \(\Lambda_0=\varnothing\).
 358: That lemma uses the plus--plus description of sheafification, not a
 359: one-step matching-family replacement, and it treats pullbacks equal to
 360: \(\emptyset\) as strict initial objects carrying only the unique section.
 361: Since the nonempty nerve is connected, it gives
 362: \[
 363: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 364: \]
 365: 
 366: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, define a category fibred in groupoids
 367: \[
 368: \mathfrak P_\lambda\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 369: \]
 370: by the nonzero-summand construction of
 371: \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}. Thus
 372: $\mathfrak P_\lambda(a)=\varnothing$; over every nonempty proper formal
 373: intersection object $W$ its objects are
 374: $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ for $i\in I(W):=\{i\in I\mid W\to U_i\}$; its morphism
 375: sets are the sheaf sections $A_{\mathcal U}(W)$, identified with \(A\) on
 376: connected nonempty \(W\); and composition is twisted by the normalized
 377: cocycle $\alpha_\lambda$ under this identification. Over $\emptyset$ the
 378: fibre is terminal because \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). The groupoid
 379: laws, strict functoriality, prestack
 380: condition, and genuine constant-band automorphism-sheaf condition are
 381: exactly \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}(i)--(iii), whose banding
 382: uses \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}.
 383: 
 384: Let
 385: \[
 386: \mathfrak P_r:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
 387: \]
 388: As in \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}, this is the fibrewise
 389: coproduct over nonempty objects with the shared terminal fibre over
 390: $\emptyset$.
 391: The verification that this is a fibred prestack, that its restrictions are strictly functorial, that its automorphism sheaves are the genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$, and that the normalized cocycle identities give the groupoid laws is precisely \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model} with $\Lambda_0=\varnothing$. On every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$, each summand $\mathfrak P_\lambda(U)$ is connected, while there are no morphisms between distinct summands. Consequently,
 392: \[
 393: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(U)\cong \Lambda
 394: \qquad
 395: \text{for every nonempty proper }U\to a,
 396: \]
 397: and
 398: \[
 399: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)=\varnothing.
 400: \]
 401: Over $\emptyset$ the shared terminal fibre gives
 402: $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(\emptyset)\cong\{\ast\}=F_{p,s}(\emptyset)$.
 403: Hence
 404: \[
 405: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}.
 406: \]
 407: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(v)--(vi), the functor
 408: $F_{p,s}$ and the prestack $\mathfrak P_r$ determine a one-state semantic
 409: model $M$ with admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at its unique state $p$,
 410: with base object $[r]_p=a$, local slice site $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$,
 411: presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$, and banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r$ with
 412: genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$. This admissibility is exactly the expansion convention of
 413: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}; no additional semantic
 414: closure axiom for freely adjoining presheaf or prestack data is being used.
 415: At this point all semantic interfaces required by the statement have been checked: the admissible parameter is $r$; the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve is $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$; the presheaf of local sections is the displayed $F_{p,s}$; the prestack band is the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$; the cover $\mathcal U$ is compared with derived cohomology by the Leray isomorphism of \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv); the global component sections are the sheafified terminal sections of $F_{p,s}$; and the satisfaction clauses for $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\NoAmalg_s$ are read from these matching-family and terminal-section data.
 416: By \Cref{prop:stackification-components},
 417: \[
 418: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s},
 419: \]
 420: so the sheafified global sections at $a$ are exactly
 421: \[
 422: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 423: \]
 424: This proves \textup{(i)}.
 425: 
 426: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, let $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ be the full substack of $\mathfrak L_r$ determined by the global component section $\lambda$. On the cover $\mathcal U$, take the lift objects
 427: \[
 428: x_i^{(\lambda)}:=x_i^{(\lambda,U_i)}
 429: \]
 430: and, on each overlap $U_{ij}$, take the distinguished isomorphism
 431: \[
 432: \phi_{ij}^{(\lambda)}:=(0,i,j):x_i^{(\lambda)}|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j^{(\lambda)}|_{U_{ij}}.
 433: \]
 434: Then on every triple overlap $U_{ijk}$,
 435: \[
 436: \bigl(\phi_{ik}^{(\lambda)}\bigr)^{-1}\circ
 437: \phi_{jk}^{(\lambda)}\circ
 438: \phi_{ij}^{(\lambda)}
 439: =
 440: (\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,i),
 441: \]
 442: which identifies with $\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}\in A$ under the automorphism-band identification. Therefore the \v{C}ech cocycle produced by
 443: \artresult{\v{C}ech obstruction of a component gerbe on an acyclic cover}
 444: is exactly $\alpha_\lambda$, and the component obstruction class of $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ is
 445: \[
 446: \omega_\lambda=[\alpha_\lambda].
 447: \]
 448: This is the stackification-component compatibility clause of \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model} written on the cover $\mathcal U$.
 449: Thus the finite-nerve comparison uses exactly the fixed good cover
 450: $\mathcal U$, the constant band $A$, and the normalized cocycle
 451: $\alpha_\lambda$ supplied by the homomorphism $\phi_\lambda$; the passage
 452: to derived $H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})$ is the Leray comparison of
 453: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv).
 454: Since
 455: \[
 456: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=\eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 457: \]
 458: one gets
 459: \[
 460: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 461: \]
 462: This proves \textup{(ii)}.
 463: 
 464: Because each $\phi_\lambda$ is nonzero and $\eta_A$ is an isomorphism, each class $\omega_\lambda$ is nonzero. By
 465: \artresult{Derived component classes detect neutrality}, every component
 466: gerbe $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ is therefore non-neutral, and
 467: \artresult{Terminal-fibre nonemptiness and neutrality} gives
 468: \[
 469: \mathfrak G_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
 470: \qquad
 471: (\forall \lambda\in\Lambda).
 472: \]
 473: Hence
 474: \[
 475: \mathfrak L_r(a)=\varnothing.
 476: \]
 477: Since also
 478: \[
 479: \mathfrak P_r(a)=\varnothing,
 480: \]
 481: the stackification functor on the terminal fibre is
 482: \[
 483: (\iota_r)_a:\mathfrak P_r(a)\to \mathfrak L_r(a),
 484: \]
 485: that is, the empty functor $\varnothing\to\varnothing$, and it is essentially surjective. Thus $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$.
 486: 
 487: Moreover,
 488: \[
 489: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda\neq\varnothing,
 490: \]
 491: and the cover $\mathcal U$ carries an explicit strict matching family:
 492: choose any $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and put the section $\lambda\in
 493: F_{p,s}(U_i)=\Lambda$ on every member $U_i$. Restrictions between
 494: nonempty proper intersections are identities, and restrictions to
 495: $\emptyset$ are unique, so the family agrees on every pullback overlap.
 496: Hence \Cref{def:existence-levels}(ii) gives
 497: \[
 498: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
 499: \]
 500: On the other hand,
 501: \[
 502: F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing,
 503: \]
 504: so
 505: \[
 506: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
 507: \]
 508: Since $r$ is admissible by construction, it follows that
 509: \[
 510: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
 511: \]
 512: This proves \textup{(iii)}.
 513: 
 514: Finally, \textup{(iv)} follows by applying
 515: \artresult{Label-aware quotient} and \artresult{Common-character quotient}
 516: to the family
 517: \[
 518: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)
 519: \qquad
 520: (\lambda\in\Lambda).
 521: \]
 522: The last sentence is the same statement rewritten in terms of the images of the chosen homomorphisms.
 523: \end{proof}
 524: 
 525: The preceding construction theorem makes every component gerbe non-neutral. The next theorem removes that restriction and identifies the neutral component gerbes exactly with the zero homomorphisms.

   5: The construction proofs use the following explicit typed-expansion
   6: interface. The site is not an arbitrary full subcategory of intersections.
   7: It is the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve of a finite good-cover presentation, so that
   8: the cohomological comparison used later is an actual Leray comparison rather

  11: \begin{lemma}[Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion]\label{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}
  12: Let
  13: \[
  14: \mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
  15: \]
  16: be a finite cover whose nerve $N=N(\mathcal U)$ is the nerve of a good cover
  17: of a paracompact space $X\simeq |N|$. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ be the
  18: finite intersection site associated to this chosen good-cover model, defined
  19: as follows. Its objects are $a$, one strict initial object $\emptyset$, and
  20: one object $U_J$ for each nonempty simplex $J\in N$. A geometric-realization functor
  21: from this formal category to open subsets of \(X\) sends \(a\) to \(X\),
  22: \(\emptyset\) to the empty open set, and \(U_J\) to the corresponding
  23: nonempty good-cover intersection. This is a pullback-complete finite intersection site,
  24: not the full subcategory on only nonempty intersections. The same strict
  25: initial object represents every empty finite intersection. Thus the only
  26: finite subsets represented by named non-initial objects are the simplices
  27: of \(N\), but a finite subset \(J\subseteq I\) which is not a simplex is
  28: not discarded from the site-level pullback calculus; whenever such a
  29: subset arises as a pullback intersection, the pullback is the
  30: distinguished object \(\emptyset\). In formulas
  31: we write
  32: \[
  33: \widetilde U_J:=
  34: \begin{cases}
  35: U_J,& J\in N,\\
  36: \emptyset,& J\notin N.
  37: \end{cases}
  38: \]
  39: Thus empty intersections are not omitted from the site: all of them are
  40: identified with the same strict initial pullback object $\emptyset$, and
  41: the open set corresponding to \(\widetilde U_J\) is the actual intersection
  42: \(\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j\), possibly empty. The order is generated by
  43: \[
  44: \emptyset\to U_J\to U_K\to a
  45: \qquad (K\subseteq J,\; J,K\in N).
  46: \]
  47: There is a unique arrow \(\emptyset\to W\) for every object \(W\), and no
  48: non-initial object maps to \(\emptyset\).
  49: For any two arrows $U_J\to U_L$ and $U_K\to U_L$ with
  50: $L\subseteq J\cap K$, their fibre product is
  51: \[
  52: U_J\times_{U_L}U_K=\widetilde U_{J\cup K}.
  53: \]
  54: If $J\cup K\notin N$, this means that the fibre product is the strict
  55: initial object $\emptyset$. Any fibre product in which one factor is
  56: $\emptyset$ is also $\emptyset$. The pretopology is the smallest
  57: pretopology for which the vertex cover \(\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\), all of
  58: its pullbacks along arrows of the formal category, all identity covers,
  59: and the empty cover of \(\emptyset\) are covers. Equivalently, it is
  60: obtained by repeatedly applying pullback stability and transitivity to
  61: the vertex cover inside the formal category just described. For example,
  62: the pullback of the vertex cover along \(U_J\to a\) is the family of
  63: arrows
  64: \[
  65: \{\widetilde U_{J\cup\{i\}}\to U_J\}_{i\in I},
  66: \]
  67: with the terms for non-simplices equal to \(\emptyset\). Repeated
  68: occurrences of \(\emptyset\) in such a pulled-back family may be
  69: identified with the same initial object. They are harmless in matching
  70: conditions because the coefficient sheaves used below have zero value at
  71: \(\emptyset\), but the corresponding pullback object is still present in
  72: the site. In particular, disjoint cover members \(U_i,U_j\to a\) have the
  73: pullback \(U_i\times_aU_j=\emptyset\) in the site. The empty object is
  74: omitted only from the nonempty \v{C}ech nerve and from the displayed
  75: nonzero cochain groups, never from the local-reference-site structure.
  76: Every pullback demanded by \Cref{def:local-reference-frame} is therefore
  77: an object of \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), including the empty pullback
  78: objects produced by disjoint members of a covering family.
  79: Thus closure under the pretopology axioms is part of the definition, not a
  80: consequence of omitting any empty pullback object. Then:
  81: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  82: \item $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ is a pullback-based reference-refinement site
  83: with terminal object $a$; in particular, for every pair of cover members
  84: $U_i,U_j\to a$, the fibre product is the formal object $U_{\{i,j\}}$ if
  85: $\{i,j\}\in N$ and is the strict initial object $\emptyset$ otherwise;
  86: \item the cover $\mathcal U$ remains a cover of $a$ in
  87: $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, all pullbacks of members of this cover exist
  88: there, and its nonempty \v{C}ech nerve is the finite simplicial complex
  89: $N$;
  90: \item for every abelian group $A$, let $A_{\mathcal U}$ denote the genuine
  91: constant sheaf
  92: on \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\)
  93: \[
  94: A_{\mathcal U}(W)=\operatorname{LC}(|W|,A),
  95: \]
  96: where \(|W|\subseteq X\) is the open set represented by \(W\). This is the
  97: restriction of the genuine constant sheaf of locally constant
  98: \(A\)-valued functions on the chosen good-cover space. It is this
  99: sheaf, not the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the abstract
 100: index category, that is used as the band. With these coefficients the
 101: \v{C}ech cochain complex of
 102: $\mathcal U$ with coefficients in $A_{\mathcal U}$ and the finite nerve
 103: presentation of any class in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ are the same finite
 104: cochain data after replacing $\mathcal C_a$ with
 105: $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$. This is a cochain-level identification because
 106: the cover is a chosen good cover: on connected nonempty basic
 107: intersections \(A_{\mathcal U}\) has value \(A\), while on the strict
 108: initial object it has value \(0\);
 109: \item on the slice

 111: object, every cover of a nonempty object contains an identity, while the
 112: empty cover forces every abelian sheaf to take value \(0\) at the strict
 113: initial object. Consequently the abelian sheaf category on the slice is
 114: equivalent to the presheaf category on its full nonempty subcategory.
 115: Evaluation at the terminal object is therefore exact and
 116: \[

 119: \]
 120: Thus the vertex cover is \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-Leray for an entirely internal
 121: finite-site reason, and the Cech-to-derived comparison gives a natural

 123: \[

 125: \]

 153: \begin{proof}
 154: The formal index category is thin and has terminal object $a$. We first
 155: verify the pullbacks, since they are part of the local-reference-site
 156: structure and not merely a convention about the \v{C}ech cochain complex.
 157: Suppose that \(U_J\to U_L\) and \(U_K\to U_L\) are two maps, so
 158: \(L\subseteq J\cap K\). If \(J\cup K\in N\), then \(U_{J\cup K}\) maps to
 159: both \(U_J\) and \(U_K\), and any object mapping to both over \(U_L\) is
 160: indexed by a simplex containing \(J\cup K\), hence factors uniquely through
 161: \(U_{J\cup K}\). If \(J\cup K\notin N\), no nonempty simplex can contain the
 162: union, so the only object mapping to both over \(U_L\) is the strict initial
 163: object \(\emptyset\). Pullbacks involving \(\emptyset\) are \(\emptyset\) by
 164: strict initiality. Therefore every fibre product required by
 165: \Cref{def:local-reference-frame} is an object of \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\).
 166: In particular, for every pair in the covering family \(\{U_i\to a\}\) the
 167: pullback is \(U_{\{i,j\}}\) when \(\{i,j\}\in N\) and is \(\emptyset\)
 168: otherwise. This proves the pullback-object clause in \textup{(i)}; the
 169: identity, pullback-stability, and transitivity pretopology axioms hold by
 170: construction of the generated pretopology.
 171: 
 172: The covering family $\mathcal U$ is one of the generators of the
 173: pretopology on $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$. A finite set $J\subseteq I$
 174: spans a simplex precisely when the iterated pullback of the corresponding
 175: $U_i$ is a nonempty object $U_J$ rather than $\emptyset$. Hence the
 176: \v{C}ech nerve of the cover is $N$, proving \textup{(ii)}.
 177: 
 178: The sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\) is defined by restricting the genuine
 179: constant sheaf of locally constant \(A\)-valued functions on \(X\) along
 180: the geometric-realization functor \(W\mapsto |W|\). Equivalently,
 181: \(A_{\mathcal U}(W)=\operatorname{LC}(|W|,A)\), with the usual sheaf
 182: restriction maps for locally constant functions. Since every nonempty
 183: formal intersection \(U_J\) is contractible, hence connected, its sections
 184: are \(A\); over the strict initial object the section group is \(0\). This
 185: is a sheaf before it is used as a band: no sheaf condition is being
 186: inferred from the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the formal
 187: index category. More explicitly, if a generated cover of an object \(W\)
 188: contains several nonempty pieces, a matching family is a family of locally
 189: constant functions on the corresponding open subsets which agree on the
 190: nonempty geometric overlaps and impose no condition on empty pullbacks,
 191: where the coefficient group is \(0\). These functions glue uniquely to a
 192: locally constant function on \(|W|\) because they are sections of the
 193: ambient constant sheaf restricted to the cover.
 194: Hence the \v{C}ech $n$-cochains on
 195: $\mathcal U$ are exactly functions from the set of nonempty
 196: $(n+1)$-fold intersections to $A$; empty pullback terms contribute only
 197: zero sections. Thus empty intersections are present as pullback objects
 198: in $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, but their coefficient group is
 199: $A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0$, so omitting them from the finite cochain
 200: display changes neither cochains nor coboundaries. The preceding
 201: paragraph identifies that nonzero indexing set before and after passing
 202: to $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, and the alternating coboundary is the same.
 203: Hence the \v{C}ech cochain complex, the simplicial cochain complex of
 204: $N(\mathcal U)$, and the
 205: universal-coefficient data used in the finite nerve representative are
 206: identical. This proves \textup{(iii)}.
 207: 
 208: For \textup{(iv)}, fix a nonempty proper intersection object \(U_J\), and
 209: consider any nonempty object \(U_K\to U_J\) of its slice. The pullback of the
 210: vertex cover along \(U_K\to a\) is
 211: \[
 212: \{\widetilde U_{K\cup\{i\}}\to U_K\}_{i\in I}.
 213: \]
 214: For every \(k\in K\), its \(k\)-term is the identity
 215: \(U_K=U_{K\cup\{k\}}\to U_K\). Hence this pulled-back generating cover
 216: contains an identity. The same is true of identity covers and is preserved
 217: under pullback and transitivity: pulling back an identity gives an identity,
 218: and, when covers each containing an identity are composed, the composite
 219: family again contains an identity. Induction over the generation of the
 220: pretopology therefore shows that every covering family of every nonempty
 221: object \(U_K\to U_J\) contains \(\operatorname{id}_{U_K}\). Equivalently,
 222: the topology on the full nonempty subcategory of
 223: \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/U_J\) is trivial.
 224: 
 225: The only remaining object is the strict initial object \(\emptyset\to U_J\).
 226: Its empty covering family forces an abelian sheaf to take the value \(0\)
 227: there. Restrictions to that object are then unique. Thus restriction to the
 228: full nonempty subcategory is an equivalence from abelian sheaves on the slice
 229: to presheaves of abelian groups on that subcategory. Since \(U_J\to U_J\) is
 230: terminal, the global section functor is evaluation there, which is exact
 231: because kernels and epimorphisms in a presheaf category are computed
 232: objectwise. Therefore
 233: \[
 234: H^q(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/U_J,A_{\mathcal U})=0
 235: \qquad(q>0).
 236: \]
 237: The slice over the empty intersection is also acyclic: the empty cover forces
 238: every sheaf of abelian groups to have zero value there. Thus all finite
 239: intersections of members of the vertex cover are acyclic. This proves the
 240: Leray hypothesis
 241: directly inside the finite intersection site; contractibility of their ambient
 242: good-cover models is used in \textup{(iii)} to identify coefficient
 243: groups with \(A\), but not to infer this derived acyclicity.
 244: 
 245: Applying that Leray theorem to the vertex cover of the terminal object \(a\)
 246: identifies the derived sheaf cohomology on the generated finite site with the
 247: \v{C}ech cohomology of this cover. By \textup{(iii)}, the resulting Cech
 248: cochain complex is the simplicial cochain complex of the nonempty nerve
 249: \(N\) with coefficients in \(A\): nonempty intersections contribute one copy
 250: of \(A\), and empty intersections contribute \(0\). Hence
 251: \[
 252: H^n(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})
 253: \cong \check H^n(\mathcal U,A_{\mathcal U})
 254: \cong H^n(N,A)
 255: \]
 256: naturally in \(A\). Under this comparison a vertex-cover \v{C}ech
 257: \(2\)-cocycle represents exactly the corresponding derived class in
 258: \(H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})\). The argument uses only the
 259: generated finite cover-basis condition just stated; it does not assert an
 260: equivalence of topoi between \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\) and the open-set
 261: site of \(X\).
 262: 
 263: For \textup{(v)}, build the lower structure explicitly. Let the state set be
 264: the singleton $\{p\}$. For each object $U$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, take a
 265: reference element $r_U$ of sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$, interpret $\Adm_s$ at $p$ as
 266: the set of all these elements, and put $[r_U]_p=U$. This gives a surjective
 267: reference-class assignment onto the object set of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$.
 268: Let $r:=r_a$ be the distinguished terminal reference. The refinement relation
 269: and pretopology on these base objects are those of

 271: pullback-object clauses were verified in \textup{(i)}. Thus the slice site over
 272: $[r]_p=a$ is exactly $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$. For parameter sorts not used in
 273: the construction, take empty reference sets or the inherited background
 274: interpretation. Assign the given functor $F$ as the presheaf of local sections on
 275: that slice site. These data are exactly the semantic data required by
 276: \Cref{def:reference-classes,def:local-reference-frame,def:local-object-functor};
 277: the lower $\mathbb L_1$-reduct is the same one-state information model with
 278: the added site and local-section symbols forgotten. Hence they define the
 279: claimed $\mathbb L_2$-model by the presheaf expansion case of
 280: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}. Thus the existence
 281: assertions in this subsection are relative to the deliberately broad

 284:

 290: gives clause \textup{(ii)}. Thus $\mathfrak P$ is a banded groupoid lift for

 293: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain} and

   1: The preceding corollary classifies the componentwise homological image subgroups that can occur on a fixed finite nerve with $H_2\cong \mathbb Z^\beta$. The next theorem replaces that abstract nerve by an explicitly chosen wedge-of-spheres good-cover family and classifies, inside that family and with the stated lift data, the finite abelian groups that occur as two-component label-loss kernels with complementary nonzero image subgroups.

   9: \begin{lemma}[Wedge-of-spheres good-cover and finite-abelian interfaces]\label{lem:wedge-sphere-cover-interface}
  10: Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ be the open-star cover of $\operatorname{Sd}^m K$ on $|K|$. Then:
  11: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  12: \item every nonempty finite intersection of members of $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ is contractible, and $N(\mathcal U^{(m)})$ is canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sd}^mK$;
  13: \item the covers $\mathcal U^{(m+1)}$ refine $\mathcal U^{(m)}$, and in the pullback site generated by all such open stars, their nonempty intersections, and a strict initial object for empty intersections, the family $(\mathcal U^{(m)})_{m\ge0}$ is filtered and cofinal;
  14: \item for every constant finite abelian group $G$, the Leray--\v{C}ech comparison identifies
  15: \[
  16: \varinjlim_m\check H^2(\mathcal U^{(m)},G)
  17: \cong
  18: H^2(|K|,G),
  19: \]
  20: and the comparison is compatible with the simplicial cohomology of the nerves;
  21: \item for every integer $\beta\ge 1$ and every nonzero finite abelian group $G$, the
  22: group $G$ admits a decomposition
  23: \[
  24: G=G_1\oplus G_2
  25: \]
  26: with $G_1,G_2$ nonzero and $d(G_i)\le\beta$ for $i=1,2$ if and only if $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.
  27: \end{enumerate}
  28: \end{lemma}
  29: 
  30: \begin{proof}
  31: For \textup{(i)}, the open star of a vertex of a barycentric subdivision is contractible, and a nonempty finite intersection of such open stars is the open star of the simplex spanned by the corresponding vertices. This is contractible. The nerve of the open-star cover of a barycentric subdivision is the subdivision itself; this is the standard nerve computation for open stars in a simplicial complex \cite[Secs.~2.1, 4G]{Hatcher2002}.
  32: 
  33: For \textup{(ii)}, barycentric subdivision gives a simplicial refinement of the previous subdivision, and each open star in $\operatorname{Sd}^{m+1}K$ lies in an open star of $\operatorname{Sd}^{m}K$. The generated site used here includes a strict initial object $\emptyset$ and declares the pullback of two disjoint members to be $\emptyset$; nonempty pullbacks are the corresponding finite intersections. Thus every pullback demanded by the reference-refinement-site axioms is represented in the site, while the \v{C}ech cochains still ignore empty intersections because the constant sheaf has only the zero section on $\emptyset$. The pretopology is generated by these covers, their pullbacks, identity covers, and the empty cover of $\emptyset$, so any covering family in the generated site is refined by a common later barycentric open-star cover. This proves filteredness and cofinality.
  34: 
  35: For \textup{(iii)}, the contractibility in \textup{(i)} makes each $\mathcal U^{(m)}$ a Leray cover for the genuine constant sheaf $G$ on the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve. Empty pullback objects contribute no cochains. The Leray theorem for \v{C}ech cohomology therefore identifies the \v{C}ech cohomology of these covers with the sheaf cohomology of $|K|$, and the nerve identification in \textup{(i)} identifies the same groups with simplicial cohomology of $\operatorname{Sd}^mK$ \cite[Chap.~III, Sec.~4]{Bredon1997}, \cite[Sec.~4G]{Hatcher2002}. The refinement maps are the usual subdivision maps, hence induce cohomology isomorphisms.
  36: 
  37: For \textup{(iv)}, fix an integer $\beta\ge1$. The standing nonzero hypothesis removes the trivial group from the classification; here a cyclic $p$-group means a cyclic group of order $p^n$ with $n\ge1$. First suppose such a decomposition exists. Then $G$ is a direct sum of two nonzero groups, so it is decomposable. The finite abelian indecomposable groups are exactly the cyclic groups of prime-power order \cite[Chap.~12]{DummitFoote2004}. Also
  38: \[
  39: d(G)\le d(G_1)+d(G_2)\le 2\beta.
  40: \]
  41: Conversely, assume $d(G)\le2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. There are two cases: either the minimal number of generators is $m\ge2$, or $m=1$ and the cyclic group has non-prime-power order. If $d(G)=m\ge2$, write an invariant-factor decomposition
  42: \[
  43: G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_m},
  44: \qquad
  45: n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_m.
  46: \]
  47: With $t=\min\{\beta,m-1\}$, the two sums
  48: \[
  49: G_1=C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_t},
  50: \qquad
  51: G_2=C_{n_{t+1}}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_m}
  52: \]
  53: are nonzero and satisfy $d(G_1)\le\beta$ and $d(G_2)=m-t\le\beta$. If $d(G)=1$, then $G$ is cyclic. Since it is not a cyclic $p$-group, its order has at least two coprime factors $a,b>1$, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives
  54: \[
  55: G\cong \mathbb Z/a\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/b\mathbb Z,
  56: \]
  57: with both summands nonzero and singly generated. This proves the equivalence.
  58: \end{proof}

  60: \begin{lemma}[Wedge-of-spheres mixed-component construction transfer]\label{lem:wedge-sphere-mixed-component-transfer}
  61: Fix $\beta\ge 1$ and the open-star good-cover intersection site $\mathcal C_a$ built from
  62: $K_\beta$ and the open-star covers $\mathcal U_\beta^{(m)}$ as in
  63: \Cref{thm:wedge-sphere-two-component-label-loss}. Let $G$ be a finite abelian
  64: group, and let $G_1,G_2\le G$ be nonzero subgroups satisfying
  65: \[
  66: d(G_i)\le \beta\qquad(i=1,2).
  67: \]
  68: Then there exist a state $p$, an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$
  69: inside a model $M$ with $a=[r]_p$, a presheaf of local sections on
  70: $\mathcal C_a$, and a banded groupoid lift with constant band $G$ such
  71: that
  72: \[
  73: \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v_1,v_2\},
  74: \qquad
  75: K_{v_i}=G_i\quad(i=1,2).
  76: \]
  77: Both component gerbes are non-neutral. If, moreover,
  78: \[
  79: G_1\cap G_2=0,\qquad G_1+G_2=G,
  80: \]
  81: then
  82: \[
  83: Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\cong K_{\mathrm{forg}}(r)\cong G,
  84: \qquad
  85: Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)=0,
  86: \qquad
  87: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
  88: \]
  89: \end{lemma}
  90: 
  91: \begin{proof}
  92: By \Cref{lem:wedge-sphere-cover-interface}(i)--(iii), the cover
  93: $\mathcal U_\beta^{(0)}$ is a finite good cover whose nerve is
  94: $K_\beta$, all finite intersections are contractible, the constant band
  95: $G$ is trivial on the cover, and the generated filtered family satisfies
  96: \textup{(H4)}. Since $K_\beta\simeq\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, we have
  97: \[

 101: \]

 637: \begin{proposition}[Derived component classes detect neutrality]\label{prop:derived-branch-classification}
 638: Assume \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)}. For every global component section $v$,
 639: \[
 640: \omega_v=0\ \text{in}\ H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
 641: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 642: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is neutral}.
 643: \]

 693: \begin{proposition}[Global sections versus neutral component gerbes]\label{prop:global-sections-vs-neutral-components}

 696: \[
 697: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)

 702: \end{proposition}

 712:

 716: \begin{theorem}[Component-gerbe criterion for matching without amalgamation]\label{thm:gerbe-null-semantics}
 717: Assume \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H3)} for an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$, and assume in addition that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice. Then matching without amalgamation is equivalent to the existence of at least one global component section and the non-neutrality of every component gerbe:
 718: \[
 719: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
 720: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 721: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing
 722: \ \text{and}\
 723: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is non-neutral for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r).
 724: \]
 725: If, in addition, \textup{(H4)} holds, then this is equivalently
 726: \[
 727: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
 728: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 729: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing
 730: \ \text{and}\
 731: \omega_v\neq 0\ \text{in }H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
 732: \text{ for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r).
 733: \]
 734: The companion theorem \cite[Theorem~5.20]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} is the meet-semilattice analogue of this pullback-site formulation.
 735: \end{theorem}
 736: 
 737: \begin{proof}
 738: Because $r$ is admissible, the definition of matching without amalgamation gives
 739: \[
 740: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
 741: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 742: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)\ \text{and}\ M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
 743: \]
 744: By \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches}, the compatible-local clause is equivalent to
 745: \[
 746: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing.
 747: \]
 748: By \Cref{prop:global-sections-vs-neutral-components}, using essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ from \textup{(H3)}, the global-section clause is equivalent to the existence of a global component section $v$ with
 749: \[
 750: \mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
 751: \]
 752: By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this is equivalent to the existence of a neutral component gerbe. Therefore
 753: \[
 754: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r)
 755: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 756: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is non-neutral for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r),
 757: \]
 758: provided the compatible-local clause has supplied at least one global component section. Combining these two equivalences proves the first displayed characterization.
 759: 
 760: Assume now also \textup{(H4)}. For each global component section $v$, \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} gives
 761: \[
 762: \omega_v=0
 763: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 764: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is neutral}.
 765: \]
 766: Thus non-neutrality of every component gerbe is equivalent to nonvanishing of every derived component class $\omega_v$, and the second displayed characterization follows.
 767: \end{proof}

 110: \begin{definition}[Banded stack lift of the component sheaf]\label{def:banded-stack-lift}
 111: For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, abbreviate
 112: \[
 113: a=[r]_p,
 114: \qquad
 115: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
 116: \]
 117: and fix an abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$. Let $\mathfrak E_r$ be a
 118: $\Band$-banded stack in groupoids on $\mathcal C_a$. A
 119: \emph{$\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf} is a pair
 120: \[
 121: (\mathfrak E_r,\epsilon_r)
 122: \]
 123: consisting of such a stack together with an isomorphism of sheaves
 124: \[
 125: \epsilon_r:\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)\xrightarrow{\sim} a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
 126: \]
 127: on $\mathcal C_a$.
 128: 
 129: For a sheafified global section
 130: \[
 131: v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a),
 132: \]
 133: the \emph{$v$-component substack} of $\mathfrak E_r$ is the full substack
 134: \[
 135: \mathfrak E_r[v](U):=
 136: \bigl\{x\in \mathfrak E_r(U)\mid \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U\bigr\}
 137: \]
 138: for objects $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, where $\epsilon_{r,U}$ denotes the component of $\epsilon_r$ at $U$.
 139: \end{definition}

 141: \begin{lemma}[Equivalence data and component transport]\label{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport}
 142: Let
 143: \[
 144: (\mathfrak E_r,\Band,\epsilon_r),
 145: \qquad
 146: (\mathfrak E'_r,\Band',\epsilon'_r)
 147: \]
 148: be banded stack lifts of the component sheaf on $\mathcal C_a$. Suppose an equivalence of stacks
 149: \[
 150: \Phi:\mathfrak E_r\to\mathfrak E'_r
 151: \]
 152: comes with a band isomorphism $\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'$ and satisfies
 153: \[
 154: \epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r.
 155: \]
 156: Then, for every sheafified global section $v$, $\Phi$ restricts to an equivalence of full component substacks
 157: \[
 158: \Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak E'_r[v],
 159: \]
 160: and this restricted equivalence is banded by $\theta$.
 161: \end{lemma}
 162: 
 163: \begin{proof}
 164: Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C_a$ and let $x\in\mathfrak E_r[v](U)$. By definition,
 165: \[
 166: \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U.
 167: \]
 168: The compatibility condition gives
 169: \[
 170: \epsilon'_{r,U}([\Phi(x)])
 171: =
 172: (\epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi))_U([x])
 173: =
 174: \epsilon_{r,U}([x])
 175: =
 176: v|_U.
 177: \]
 178: Thus $\Phi(x)\in\mathfrak E'_r[v](U)$, so $\Phi$ restricts to a functor
 179: \[
 180: \Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\to\mathfrak E'_r[v].
 181: \]
 182: Since both component substacks are full, $\Phi_v$ is fully faithful because $\Phi$ is. For local essential surjectivity, take $z\in\mathfrak E'_r[v](U)$. A quasi-inverse $\Psi$ to $\Phi$ gives, after possibly refining $U$, an object $y\in\mathfrak E_r(U)$ with $\Phi(y)\cong z$. Applying $\epsilon'_r$ to this local isomorphism gives
 183: \[
 184: \epsilon_{r,U}([y])
 185: =
 186: \epsilon'_{r,U}([\Phi(y)])
 187: =
 188: \epsilon'_{r,U}([z])
 189: =
 190: v|_U,
 191: \]
 192: so $y$ lies locally in $\mathfrak E_r[v]$. Hence $\Phi_v$ is an equivalence of stacks. The automorphism-sheaf maps of $\Phi_v$ are the restrictions of the automorphism-sheaf maps of $\Phi$, so the band is transported by the same isomorphism $\theta$.
 193: \end{proof}

 195: \begin{lemma}[Transport of Giraud classes under banded equivalence]\label{lem:giraud-class-transport}
 196: Let $\mathfrak G$ be a $\Band$-banded gerbe and let $\mathfrak G'$ be a $\Band'$-banded gerbe on the same site $\mathcal C$. Suppose
 197: \[
 198: \Phi:\mathfrak G\to\mathfrak G'
 199: \]
 200: is an equivalence of stacks whose induced maps on automorphism sheaves identify the bands through an isomorphism
 201: \[
 202: \theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'.
 203: \]
 204: Then
 205: \[
 206: \theta_*[\mathfrak G]=[\mathfrak G']
 207: \qquad\text{in}\qquad
 208: H^2(\mathcal C,\Band').
 209: \]
 210: \end{lemma}
 211: 
 212: \begin{proof}
 213: Choose a cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ which locally trivializes $\mathfrak G$, objects $x_i\in\mathfrak G(U_i)$, and descent isomorphisms
 214: \[
 215: \varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.
 216: \]
 217: The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
 218: \[
 219: \varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
 220: \]
 221: Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
 222: \[
 223: \Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
 224: =
 225: \Phi(c_{ijk}),
 226: \]
 227: which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
 228: 
 229: The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
 230: \[
 231: (\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
 232: \]
 233: is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
 234: \end{proof}
