 236: \begin{theorem}[Canonical component-section obstruction map under banded stack lifts]\label{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension}
 237: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admissible at a state $p$, write
 238: \[
 239: a=[r]_p,
 240: \qquad
 241: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
 242: \]
 243: and let
 244: \[
 245: (\mathfrak E_r,\Band,\epsilon_r)
 246: \]
 247: be a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf in the sense of \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}. Then the assignment
 248: \[
 249: \delta_{\mathfrak E_r}:\Vis_{p,s}(r)\longrightarrow H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band),
 250: \qquad
 251: v\longmapsto [\mathfrak E_r[v]]
 252: \]
 253: is canonically defined, where $[\mathfrak E_r[v]]$ denotes the Giraud class of the $v$-component substack. More precisely:
 254: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 255: \item for every sheafified global section $v$, the full substack $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is a $\Band$-banded gerbe on $\mathcal C_a$;
 256: \item for every sheafified global section $v$,
 257: \[
 258: \delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=0
 259: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 260: \mathfrak E_r[v]\ \text{is neutral}
 261: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 262: \mathfrak E_r[v](a)\neq\varnothing;
 263: \]
 264: \item if
 265: \[
 266: (\mathfrak E'_r,\Band',\epsilon'_r)
 267: \]
 268: is another banded stack lift of the component sheaf and
 269: \[
 270: \Phi:\mathfrak E_r\to \mathfrak E'_r
 271: \]
 272: is an equivalence of stacks whose induced map on automorphism sheaves identifies the bands through an isomorphism
 273: \[
 274: \theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'
 275: \]
 276: and whose map on connected components satisfies
 277: \[
 278: \epsilon'_r\circ \pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r,
 279: \]
 280: then for every sheafified global section $v$ the functor $\Phi$ restricts to an equivalence
 281: \[
 282: \mathfrak E_r[v]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak E'_r[v]
 283: \]
 284: and
 285: \[
 286: \theta_*\bigl(\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)\bigr)=\delta_{\mathfrak E'_r}(v)
 287: \quad\text{in}\quad
 288: H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band');
 289: \]
 290: \item if $r$ admits a gluing-sensitive banded lift datum and
 291: \[
 292: \mathfrak E_r=\mathfrak L_r=a(\mathfrak P_r)
 293: \]
 294: is its stackification, then
 295: \[
 296: \delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=\omega_v
 297: \]
 298: for every global component section $v$ for which \textup{(H4)} holds.
 299: \end{enumerate}
 300: \end{theorem}
 301: 
 302: \begin{proof}
 303: Fix a sheafified global section
 304: \[
 305: v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a).
 306: \]
 307: Since $\mathfrak E_r$ is a stack in groupoids and $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is a full substack, $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is again a stack in groupoids.
 308: 
 309: Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C_a$. The section
 310: \[
 311: v|_U\in \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(U)\cong \pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)(U)
 312: \]
 313: is, by definition of the sheaf of connected components, locally represented by objects of $\mathfrak E_r$. Hence there exists a cover
 314: \[
 315: \{U_i\to U\}
 316: \]
 317: and objects
 318: \[
 319: x_i\in \mathfrak E_r(U_i)
 320: \]
 321: with
 322: \[
 323: \epsilon_{r,U_i}([x_i])=v|_{U_i}.
 324: \]
 325: Therefore
 326: \[
 327: (\mathfrak E_r[v])(U_i)\neq\varnothing
 328: \]
 329: for every $i$, so $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is locally nonempty.
 330: 
 331: Now let
 332: \[
 333: x,y\in \mathfrak E_r[v](U).
 334: \]
 335: Then
 336: \[
 337: \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=\epsilon_{r,U}([y])=v|_U.
 338: \]
 339: Because $\epsilon_{r,U}$ is an isomorphism, the connected-component classes $[x]$ and $[y]$ in $\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)(U)$ coincide. By the definition of $\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)$, there exists a cover
 340: \[
 341: \{U_i\to U\}
 342: \]
 343: such that
 344: \[
 345: x|_{U_i}\cong y|_{U_i}
 346: \qquad
 347: (\forall i).
 348: \]
 349: Thus any two objects of $\mathfrak E_r[v](U)$ are locally isomorphic. The full substack $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is therefore a gerbe \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Since it is full inside the $\Band$-banded stack $\mathfrak E_r$, the automorphism sheaf of every object in $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is still identified with $\Band$.
 350: 
 351: The preceding sentence is the band-preservation lemma used in this
 352: argument: if \(P\) is \(\Band\)-banded and \(L=a(P)\), every object of \(L\)
 353: is locally in the essential image of \(P\), and the automorphism sheaf of
 354: that local representative is \(\Band\). Because automorphism presheaves are
 355: sheafified in the stackification and the band identifications are compatible
 356: with restriction, these local identifications descend and glue on overlaps.
 357: Consequently every object of \(L\), and every object of a full component
 358: substack, has automorphism sheaf locally identified with \(\Band\) in a way
 359: compatible with descent. This proves \textup{(i)}.
 360: 
 361: Clause \textup{(i)} identifies $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ as a $\Band$-banded gerbe, so its Giraud class
 362: \[
 363: [\mathfrak E_r[v]]\in H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
 364: \]
 365: is defined canonically \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. By the classification of banded gerbes, this class vanishes if and only if the gerbe is neutral. Since $a$ is the terminal object of the slice site $\mathcal C_a$, neutrality is equivalent to the existence of an object over $a$, namely
 366: \[
 367: \mathfrak E_r[v](a)\neq\varnothing.
 368: \]
 369: This proves \textup{(ii)}.
 370: 
 371: Assume now that $\Phi$ is an equivalence as in \textup{(iii)}. The compatibility condition
 372: \[
 373: \epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r
 374: \]
 375: first fixes the component on which the equivalence is allowed to act: an object whose component is $v|_U$ is sent to an object whose component is again $v|_U$. Hence \Cref{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport} gives a restricted equivalence
 376: \[
 377: \Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\to \mathfrak E'_r[v]
 378: \]
 379: of the two $v$-component gerbes. This equivalence is not merely an abstract equivalence of stacks: on every lift object $x$ the induced map
 380: \[
 381: \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathfrak E_r[v]}(x)\longrightarrow
 382: \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathfrak E'_r[v]}(\Phi_v x)
 383: \]
 384: is the band map $\theta:\Band\to\Band'$. Therefore the local-trivialization cocycle defining the Giraud class of $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ is transported termwise by $\theta$ to the cocycle defining the class of $\mathfrak E'_r[v]$. By the band-functorial classification recalled in \Cref{lem:giraud-class-transport},
 385: \[
 386: \theta_*\bigl([\mathfrak E_r[v]]\bigr)=[\mathfrak E'_r[v]]
 387: \]
 388: in $H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band')$. This is exactly the displayed identity in \textup{(iii)}.
 389: 
 390: For \textup{(iv)}, let $\mathfrak E_r=\mathfrak L_r=a(\mathfrak P_r)$. By \suppresult{Components of the stackification}, the stackification carries a canonical identification
 391: \[
 392: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a},
 393: \]
 394: so $\mathfrak L_r$ is a banded stack lift of the component sheaf. The $v$-component substack defined above is then exactly the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}. On every cover
 395: \[
 396: \mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a),
 397: \]
 398: \Cref{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction} constructs the \v{C}ech class of this gerbe. The filtered colimit of those \v{C}ech classes is, by the standard classification of banded gerbes, the Giraud class of $\mathfrak G_v$, and hypothesis \textup{(H4)} identifies that colimit with the derived cohomology group
 399: \[
 400: H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band).
 401: \]
 402: By \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}, the image of that same filtered system is precisely $\omega_v$. Therefore
 403: \[
 404: \delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=[\mathfrak G_v]=\omega_v.
 405: \]
 406: \end{proof}
 407: 
 408: \begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}
 409: In the pullback-based setting of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}, and using only the banded groupoid lift and component data fixed there, every global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ determines a full substack $\mathfrak G_v\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ that is a banded $\Band$-gerbe over $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. In particular, neither essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ nor the derived comparison hypothesis \textup{(H4)} is used here.
 410: \end{theorem}
 411: 
 412: \begin{proof}
 413: By \suppresult{Components of the stackification}, the stackification
 414: \[
 415: \mathfrak E_r:=\mathfrak L_r
 416: \]
 417: is a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf of
 418: $a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$. The global component section $v$ is a section of
 419: \[
 420: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong (a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(a),
 421: \]
 422: and the full substack
 423: \[
 424: \mathfrak G_v(U)=
 425: \{x\in\mathfrak L_r(U)\mid [x]\ \text{restricts to}\ v|_U\}
 426: \]
 427: is therefore exactly the $v$-component substack
 428: $\mathfrak E_r[v]$ of \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}.
 429: 
 430: We recall why this is a gerbe. Because $\mathfrak L_r$ is a stack in
 431: groupoids, every descent datum for objects whose component lies over
 432: $v$ glues to an object whose component still lies over $v$; hence
 433: $\mathfrak G_v$ is a full substack. Local nonemptiness follows from the
 434: definition of a global component section as a section of the sheaf of connected
 435: components: after passing to a cover of any object $U$, the section
 436: $v|_U$ is represented by objects of $\mathfrak L_r$. Local connectedness
 437: is the local form of equality in the component sheaf: if two objects of
 438: $\mathfrak G_v(U)$ have component $v|_U$, then they become isomorphic
 439: after a cover of $U$. Fullness is built into the definition of
 440: $\mathfrak G_v$, so no morphisms between objects in the component are
 441: discarded. Finally, for every object $x$ of $\mathfrak G_v(U)$, the
 442: automorphism sheaf of $x$ inside $\mathfrak G_v$ is the same as its
 443: automorphism sheaf inside $\mathfrak L_r$, and this sheaf is identified
 444: with $\Band|_{\mathcal C_a/U}$ by the banding of the groupoid lift
 445: prestack and its stackification. Thus $\mathfrak G_v$ is a
 446: $\Band$-banded gerbe.
 447: 
 448: This argument uses only the banded groupoid lift, its stackification, and
 449: the component identification. Essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre concerns
 450: whether terminal stack objects come from terminal prestack objects, and
 451: \textup{(H4)} concerns promotion of cover-level \v{C}ech classes to
 452: derived cohomology; neither condition enters the gerbe construction
 453: itself.
 454: \end{proof}

   1: \subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}
   2: 
   3: Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
   4: reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
   5: degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
   6: trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
   7: Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
   8: scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
   9: isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
  10: \cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
  11: or a banded stack lift in the sense of
  12: \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}. The following comparison locates the
  13: gap precisely.
  14: 
  15: Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
  16: nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
  17: \(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
  18: \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
  19: the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
  20: equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
  21: terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
  22: \(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
  23: \[
  24: e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
  25: \]
  26: is a compatible family of probability distributions on
  27: \(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
  28: \[
  29: S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
  30: \qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
  31: \]
  32: where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
  33: context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
  34: terminal object we take the right Kan extension
  35: \[
  36: \widehat S_e(X):=
  37: \varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
  38: \]
  39: Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
  40: of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
  41: this terminally augmented presheaf.
  42: 
  43: A \emph{context refinement} used below is a refinement
  44: \(\rho:\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\) on the same measurements and outcomes,
  45: with \(C'\subseteq\rho(C')\), for which marginalization defines the refined
  46: model \(\rho^*e\). The inclusion of downward-closed context categories induces
  47: a functor
  48: \[
  49: u_\rho:\mathcal D_{\mathcal M'}\hookrightarrow
  50: \mathcal D_{\mathcal M}
  51: \]
  52: which is required to be continuous for the two generated cover topologies and
  53: to extend to their terminal augmentations. We also require the natural
  54: base-change isomorphism
  55: \[
  56: S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e.
  57: \]
  58: This includes ordinary iterated refinements which are covering refinements
  59: for the generated topology. No
  60: claim is made here for resource-theoretic simulations which change the
  61: measurement or outcome sets.
  62: 
  63: \begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
  64: For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
  65: bijection:
  66: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  67: \item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
  68:       \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
  69: \item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
  70:       \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
  71: \item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
  72:       Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
  73: \item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
  74:       \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
  75: \end{enumerate}
  76: Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
  77: from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
  78: \[
  79: M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
  80: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  81: M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
  82: \]
  83: In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
  84: set-valued level; it is not the matching-without-amalgamation case
  85: \(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
  86: \end{proposition}
  87: 
  88: \begin{proof}
  89: The event presheaf
  90: \(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf. Hence a compatible family
  91: \((s_C)\) glues uniquely to a global assignment \(s\), and its restrictions
  92: remain in the prescribed supports. Conversely, restriction of such an
  93: assignment gives a compatible supported family. This proves the first three
  94: identifications. The fourth is the defining limit formula for
  95: \(\widehat S_e(X)\); the plus construction for the cover
  96: \(\mathcal M\to X\) gives the same set in the sheafification. The displayed
  97: equivalence follows immediately.
  98: \end{proof}
  99: 
 100: \begin{remark}[Support versus probabilistic contextuality]\label{rem:support-vs-probabilistic-contextuality}
 101: The proposition concerns the possibilistic support of \(e\). Probabilistic
 102: noncontextuality asks instead for a distribution on
 103: \(\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) whose marginals are the given distributions \(e_C\).
 104: That is a fibre-extension problem for the distribution presheaf, and is not
 105: determined by \(S_e\): empirical models with the same support can have
 106: different probabilistic noncontextuality behaviour.
 107: \end{remark}
 108: 
 109: \begin{theorem}[Canonical split stack and the degree obstruction]\label{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}
 110: Let \(e\) be a finite empirical model on the context site above.
 111: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 112: \item There is a canonical banded stack lift with zero band,
 113: \[
 114: \mathfrak E_e^0:=\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e),
 115: \qquad
 116: \pi_0(\mathfrak E_e^0)\cong aS_e.
 117: \]
 118: Here \(\operatorname{Disc}\) regards a sheaf of sets as a stack of discrete
 119: groupoids.
 120: \item More generally, after an abelian sheaf \(\Band\) has been supplied,
 121: there is a canonical split \(\Band\)-banded stack lift
 122: \[
 123: \mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}:=
 124: \operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\Band.
 125: \]
 126: Every component gerbe of this lift is neutral, and therefore every
 127: Giraud class supplied by
 128: \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is zero.
 129: \item The assignments in \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are pseudonatural
 130: under context refinements: there are coherent banded equivalences
 131: \[
 132: u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^0\simeq
 133: \mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^0,
 134: \qquad
 135: u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}\simeq
 136: \mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^{\mathrm{spl}}
 137: \]
 138: in the second formula whenever the supplied bands are identified under
 139: pullback.
 140: \item The AB and AMB constructions do not produce the non-split degree-two
 141: data required by this paper. More precisely, fix
 142: \(C_0\in\mathcal M\) and \(s\in S_e(C_0)\).
 143: Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa form the free-abelian presheaf
 144: \(\mathcal F_e=\mathbb Z[S_e]\), its relative kernel
 145: \(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\), and a class
 146: \[
 147: \gamma_e(s)\in
 148: \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}).
 149: \]
 150: This is relative \v{C}ech cohomology of a presheaf, and the class is the
 151: isomorphism class of an
 152: \(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\)-torsor trivialized by
 153: \(\mathcal M\). It is not a derived \(H^2\) Giraud class for a sheaf band
 154: \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}.
 155: \item There is no comparison which recovers these AMB classes, for all finite
 156: empirical models, from the component-section obstruction map of any banded stack lift
 157: whose component sheaf is \(aS_e\). Indeed, if \(e\) is strongly contextual,
 158: then
 159: \[
 160: (aS_e)(X)=\varnothing,
 161: \]
 162: so the component-section obstruction map
 163: \[
 164: \delta_{\mathfrak E_e}:(aS_e)(X)\longrightarrow
 165: H^2(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M},\Band)
 166: \]
 167: has empty domain, whereas AMB classes are defined for the local sections
 168: \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) and can be nonzero, as in their GHZ and
 169: Kochen--Specker examples.
 170: \end{enumerate}
 171: In \textup{(i)}, \emph{canonical} means that the construction is the
 172: composite of the universal sheafification functor and the discrete-stack
 173: functor, with no choices, and that the displayed refinement equivalences
 174: satisfy the usual pseudofunctor coherence. It does not mean that all
 175: banded stack lifts of \(S_e\) are equivalent.
 176: \end{theorem}
 177: 
 178: \begin{proof}
 179: The discrete groupoid construction preserves descent, so
 180: \(\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\) is a stack and its connected-component sheaf is
 181: exactly \(aS_e\). Its automorphism sheaves are zero, proving \textup{(i)}.
 182: The classifying stack \(\mathsf B\Band\) has one local component and
 183: automorphism sheaf \(\Band\). Taking its product with the discrete stack
 184: therefore proves the band and component assertions in \textup{(ii)}. The
 185: global object represented by the identity \(\Band\)-torsor neutralizes each
 186: component gerbe, so its Giraud class vanishes.
 187: 
 188: Inverse image for the morphism of context sites commutes, up to its canonical
 189: isomorphism, with associated sheaves, discrete stacks, products, and
 190: classifying stacks. Together with
 191: \(S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e\), this gives the equivalences and their
 192: coherence in \textup{(iii)}.
 193: 
 194: The construction of \(\gamma_e(s)\) and its degree are those of
 195: \cite[Sec.~4]{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}. The torsor
 196: classification is \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}, proving \textup{(iv)}. Finally,
 197: \Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation} identifies strong contextuality with
 198: emptiness of \((aS_e)(X)\). The component-section obstruction map of
 199: \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is indexed by precisely
 200: that set, while \(\gamma_e(s)\) is indexed by a local section. This proves
 201: the asserted failure in \textup{(v)}.
 202: \end{proof}
 203: 
 204: \begin{corollary}[Exact limit of transfer to empirical models]\label{thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}
 205: For finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models, the set-valued
 206: local-to-global statements of \Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
 207: transfer functorially. The later banded and homological theorems transfer
 208: only after a band and a non-split banded stack lift have been
 209: supplied as additional data. In particular:
 210: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 211: \item the canonical split lift gives only zero Giraud classes and zero
 212: homological image subgroups;
 213: \item the characterization
 214: \[
 215: d(G)\le 2\beta
 216: \quad\text{and}\quad
 217: G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}
 218: \]
 219: remains a construction theorem for the chosen wedge-of-spheres good-cover, band, and
 220: two-component cocycle data of
 221: \Cref{thm:wedge-sphere-two-component-label-loss}; it is not a characterization of
 222: groups canonically attached to empirical models;
 223: \item without an additional degree-shifting construction, the Giraud
 224: \(H^2\)-class neither recovers nor refines the AMB relative
 225: \(\check H^1\)-obstruction.
 226: \end{enumerate}
 227: \end{corollary}
 228: 
 229: \begin{proof}
 230: The first and third assertions are
 231: \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}(ii),(iv)--(v). The wedge-of-spheres theorem
 232: starts from a prescribed finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and
 233: chosen componentwise homomorphisms
 234: \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\). None of those data is selected by a bare empirical
 235: model, so its group classification cannot be transported through the split
 236: construction. This proves the second assertion.
 237: \end{proof}

  36: \]
  37: with identity restrictions among nonempty proper intersection objects,
  38: inclusions $\Lambda_0\hookrightarrow\Lambda$ from $a$ to nonempty proper
  39: intersections, and the unique restriction map to $F(\emptyset)$. For each
  40: $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, define a fibred groupoid $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ by
  41: \[
  42: \mathfrak P_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
  43: \]
  44: and, for every nonempty proper object $W$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, put
  45: \[
  46: I(W):=\{i\in I\mid W\to U_i\text{ in }\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\}.
  47: \]
  48: Thus $I(U_J)=J$ for a formal intersection object. Define objects
  49: \[
  50: x_i^{(\lambda,W)}\qquad (i\in I(W))
  51: \]
  52: and morphism sets
  53: \[
  54: \mathrm{Hom}\bigl(x_i^{(\lambda,W)},x_j^{(\lambda,W)}\bigr)
  55: =A_{\mathcal U}(W),
  56: \]
  57: which is identified with \(A\) because \(W\) is a connected nonempty
  58: basic intersection. With this identification, write morphisms as
  59: \((a,i,j)\) with \(a\in A\), and define composition by
  60: \[
  61: (b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)=(a+b+\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,k).
  62: \]
  63: For a morphism $V\to W$, one has $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, because a map
  64: $W\to U_i$ composes with $V\to W$. Restrictions therefore send
  65: $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ to $x_i^{(\lambda,V)}$ and $(a,i,j)$ to the same
  66: coefficient-labelled morphism after applying the restriction map of
  67: \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Over $\emptyset$ take the terminal groupoid and let
  68: every restriction to $\emptyset$ be the unique functor. For each
  69: $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, let $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ be the neutral stack with
  70: one object over every object and automorphism group
  71: \(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\) over \(W\), so the fibre over \(\emptyset\) is
  72: terminal because \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). Restrictions are exactly
  73: the restriction maps of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Its stack property is
  74: the \(H^1\)-vanishing criterion of
  75: \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}: object descent data are
  76: \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles on slices, and those torsors are
  77: trivial on the formal good-cover slices used here. Its automorphism sheaf is
  78: therefore the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$. Set
  79: \[
  80: \mathfrak P:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
  81: \]
  82: This denotes the fibrewise coproduct over every nonempty object, while over
  83: $\emptyset$ the summands share the single terminal fibre and all
  84: restrictions to $\emptyset$ are the unique functor. The band used below is
  85: the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ on the finite intersection site, not the
  86: identity-restriction constant presheaf.
  87: Then:
  88: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  89: \item each nonzero summand $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ is a category fibred in groupoids, and the pullback functors are strictly functorial;
  90: \item the identity, inverse, and associativity laws in each twisted fibre are respectively the normalized identities
  91: \[
  92: \alpha_{\lambda,iij}=\alpha_{\lambda,ijj}=0,
  93: \qquad
  94: \alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0,
  95: \]
  96: and the cocycle identity
  97: \[
  98: \alpha_{\lambda,jkl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
  99: +\alpha_{\lambda,ijl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}=0;
 100: \]
 101: \item $\mathfrak P$ is a prestack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$;
 102: \item its presheaf of connected components is $F$;
 103: \item after stackification, the components over $a$ are naturally indexed by $\Lambda$, and the component indexed by $\lambda$ has \v{C}ech cocycle $\alpha_\lambda$ on $\mathcal U$.
 104: \end{enumerate}
 105: \end{lemma}
 106: 
 107: \begin{proof}
 108: The sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ is fixed as part of the finite intersection site interface in
 109: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iii)--(iv). Since every
 110: nonempty object of the finite intersection site is represented by a connected
 111: contractible intersection of the good cover, locally constant
 112: $A$-valued functions on it are exactly constant functions with value in
 113: $A$; the strict initial object has only the zero section. Thus the
 114: coefficient notation $A$ below is shorthand for the actual sheaf sections
 115: $A_{\mathcal U}(W)$ on nonempty basic objects, not for the
 116: identity-restriction constant presheaf on an arbitrary site; equivalently,
 117: we are using \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding} throughout.
 118: In particular, whenever an isomorphism or automorphism presheaf below is
 119: written as \(A\) on nonempty objects and \(0\) on \(\emptyset\), it is
 120: defined by the displayed identification with
 121: \(A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}\). The prestack condition is
 122: therefore a sheaf condition for a genuine sheaf on each slice, not a
 123: claim that the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the index
 124: category is already a sheaf.
 125: 
 126: For a nonempty proper formal intersection object $W$ and a fixed
 127: $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, the displayed formula makes every morphism
 128: invertible. The identity at $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ is $(0,i,i)$ because the
 129: cocycle is normalized on repeated indices. The inverse of $(a,i,j)$ is
 130: $(-a,j,i)$, again because the repeated-index normalization gives
 131: $\alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0$. Associativity of
 132: \[
 133: (c,k,l)\circ\bigl((b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)\bigr)
 134: \quad\text{and}\quad
 135: \bigl((c,k,l)\circ(b,j,k)\bigr)\circ(a,i,j)
 136: \]
 137: is equivalent, after cancelling $a+b+c$, to
 138: \[
 139: \alpha_{\lambda,ijk}+\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
 140: =
 141: \alpha_{\lambda,jkl}+\alpha_{\lambda,ijl},
 142: \]
 143: which is the displayed cocycle identity, interpreted under the alternating
 144: ordered-triple convention just fixed. This proves that each fibre is a
 145: groupoid. If $V\to W$, then $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, so every object and
 146: morphism named over $W$ has the same name over $V$. The restriction maps
 147: therefore preserve labels and restrict coefficients through the map
 148: \(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\to A_{\mathcal U}(V)\). Under the connected
 149: intersection identifications these coefficient restrictions are the
 150: identity maps \(A\to A\) on nonempty objects; for restrictions to
 151: \(\emptyset\) they are the unique maps to \(0\). Thus the same ordered
 152: simplex indices are used wherever a nonempty coefficient is present, so
 153: restrictions preserve identities, inverses, and composition. Since
 154: inclusions \(I(W)\subseteq I(V)\) are transitive and
 155: \(A_{\mathcal U}\) is a sheaf with functorial restrictions, restrictions
 156: compose strictly. This proves \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}.
 157: 
 158: For each pair of objects in a twisted fibre over a nonempty object $W$, the
 159: isomorphism presheaf on the slice \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W\) is defined
 160: objectwise by
 161: \[
 162: V\longmapsto A_{\mathcal U}(V),
 163: \]
 164: with restrictions those of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\), whenever the two
 165: restricted labels are both defined; over \(\emptyset\) this gives the
 166: single section of \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). On connected nonempty
 167: basic intersections this is the coefficient notation \(A\), but the
 168: presheaf itself is the restriction of the genuine constant sheaf
 169: \(A_{\mathcal U}\), not the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the
 170: index category. By
 171: \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}, it is therefore a sheaf.
 172: The same argument applies to automorphisms,
 173: where the distinguished zero coefficient gives a canonical identification
 174: \[
 175: \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(x_i^{(\lambda,W)})
 176: \cong A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}.
 177: \]
 178: Thus the prestack condition and the banding use the genuine constant sheaf
 179: $A_{\mathcal U}$. The neutral summands indexed by \(\Lambda_0\) are stacks by
 180: \Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}. This invokes object descent, not
 181: only morphism descent: a one-object \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-banded prestack has
 182: descent data classified by \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles, and those
 183: torsors are trivial on every relevant slice. Taking the finite coproduct
 184: over nonempty objects and the shared terminal fibre over $\emptyset$ preserves the prestack
 185: condition: over nonempty objects this is the usual finite coproduct of
 186: prestacks in groupoids, while the strict initial object has only the unique
 187: matching datum. This proves \textup{(iii)} without any appeal to a
 188: constant presheaf sheaf condition.
 189: 
 190: For every nonempty proper intersection object, each twisted summand is
 191: connected and each neutral summand is one connected component; there are no
 192: morphisms between distinct summands. Over $\emptyset$ the shared terminal
 193: fibre has the unique lift object over the empty intersection, matching $F(\emptyset)=\{\ast\}$.
 194: Hence
 195: \[
 196: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(U)\cong\Lambda
 197: \]
 198: for every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$. Over $a$, the
 199: nonzero summands have empty fibre and the neutral summands indexed by
 200: \(\Lambda_0\) have one object, so
 201: \[
 202: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong\Lambda_0.
 203: \]
 204: These identifications are compatible with the restriction maps, giving \textup{(iv)}.
 205: 
 206: By \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification}, applied to the displayed
 207: presheaf \(F\) and the subset \(\Lambda_0\subseteq\Lambda\), the
 208: sheafification of \(F\) has terminal sections indexed by \(\Lambda\). By
 209: \Cref{prop:stackification-components}, stackification identifies
 210: \[
 211: \pi_0(a(\mathfrak P))\cong aF,
 212: \]
 213: so the components over $a$ are indexed by $\Lambda$.
 214: 
 215: For a fixed $\lambda$, take on $U_i$ the object $x_i^{(\lambda,U_i)}$ if $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$ and the distinguished constant object if $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$. On $U_{ij}$ take the morphism $(0,i,j)$ in the nonzero case and the identity in the zero case. The triple defect is
 216: \[
 217: (0,i,k)^{-1}\circ(0,j,k)\circ(0,i,j)
 218: =
 219: (\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,i)
 220: \]
 221: in the twisted case and is $0$ in the constant case. Under the band identification this is exactly $\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}$. Thus the Cech obstruction cocycle of the $\lambda$-component is $\alpha_\lambda$, proving \textup{(v)}.
 222: \end{proof}
 223: 
 224: \begin{theorem}[Construction with prescribed componentwise homological image subgroups]\label{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}
 225: Let
 226: \[
 227: \mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
 228: \]
 229: be a finite good-cover presentation in a pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$ whose nonempty \v{C}ech nerve
 230: \[
 231: N:=N(\mathcal U)
 232: \]
 233: is connected. Equivalently, the geometric realization of the cover nerve is a
 234: paracompact space homotopy equivalent to $|N|$ and all nonempty finite
 235: intersections of members of $\mathcal U$ are acyclic for constant
 236: coefficients. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ be the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve of
 237: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}; it includes the strict
 238: initial object $\emptyset$ for all empty intersections, so disjoint cover
 239: members have a pullback in the site even though they do not contribute a
 240: nonzero finite-nerve cochain. Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, and let
 241: $A_{\mathcal U}$ denote the genuine constant sheaf on
 242: $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ whose value on each nonempty basic intersection
 243: is identified with $A$. View $A_{\mathcal U}$ as the automorphism band of
 244: the banded groupoid lift constructed below, and assume
 245: \[
 246: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0.
 247: \]
 248: Use the Leray comparison isomorphism of
 249: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv). Let $\Lambda$ be a finite nonempty set, and let
 250: \[
 251: \phi_\lambda:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
 252: \]
 253: be a nonzero homomorphism for each $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then, in the
 254: typed-expansion model class generated by
 255: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}, the following typed data
 256: define a one-state $\mathbb L_2/\mathbb L_3$ model \(M\): the one-state
 257: \(\mathbb L_1\)-reduct, the finite intersection site \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), the
 258: presheaf of local sections \(F_{p,s}\) constructed below, and the banded groupoid lift
 259: prestack
 260: \[
 261: \mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 262: \]
 263: with band \(A_{\mathcal U}\). In that generated model there are a state
 264: \(p\) and a distinguished admissible parameter \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\) with
 265: \([r]_p=a\), local slice site \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), and
 266: \(\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)\), such that the following hold:
 267: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 268: \item
 269: \[
 270: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \Lambda;
 271: \]
 272: \item under the identification in \textup{(i)}, for each $\lambda\in\Lambda$ the corresponding component gerbe $\mathfrak G_\lambda\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ has component obstruction class
 273: \[
 274: \omega_\lambda\in H^2(N,A)
 275: \]
 276: satisfying
 277: \[
 278: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=\phi_\lambda,
 279: \qquad
 280: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda);
 281: \]
 282: \item $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ by the vacuous terminal-fibre case
 283: \[
 284: \mathfrak P_r(a)=\varnothing=\mathfrak L_r(a),
 285: \]
 286: and
 287: \[
 288: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r);
 289: \]
 290: \item the aggregate quotients satisfy
 291: \[
 292: Q_{\mathrm{lab}}(r)\cong A\Big/\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda),
 293: \qquad
 294: Q_{\mathrm{com}}(r)\cong A\Big/\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 295: \]
 296: \end{enumerate}
 297: In particular, within the fixed finite-nerve and typed-expansion
 298: framework above, every finite family of subgroups of $A$ arising as images of homomorphisms
 299: \[
 300: H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
 301: \]
 302: is attained as the family of presentation-relative homological image subgroups of the global component sections of one admissible parameter.
 303: \end{theorem}
 304: 
 305: \begin{proof}
 306: Since
 307: \[
 308: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 309: \]
 310: the universal coefficient sequence reduces to an isomorphism

 305: \begin{proof}
 306: Since
 307: \[
 308: H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 309: \]
 310: the universal coefficient sequence reduces to an isomorphism
 311: \[
 312: \eta_A:H^2(N,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A).
 313: \]
 314: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose the unique class
 315: \[
 316: \omega_\lambda\in H^2(N,A)
 317: \]
 318: with
 319: \[
 320: \eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 321: \]
 322: and choose a normalized simplicial cocycle
 323: \[
 324: \alpha_\lambda\in Z^2(N,A)
 325: \]
 326: representing $\omega_\lambda$, with the alternating ordered-triple extension
 327: of \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}.
 328: 
 329: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(i)--(iv), pass to the
 330: finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ appearing in the statement.
 331: The cover $\mathcal U$, its nerve, and the constant-band finite cochain
 332: data are the same, and Leray comparison identifies
 333: $H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})$ with $H^2(N,A)$. The derived component obstruction class
 334: used below is therefore the actual derived class corresponding to the
 335: chosen finite-nerve cocycle.
 336: 
 337: Define the presheaf of local sections
 338: \[
 339: F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
 340: \]
 341: by
 342: \[
 343: F_{p,s}(U):=\Lambda
 344: \qquad
 345: \text{for every nonempty proper intersection object }U\to a,
 346: \]
 347: \[
 348: F_{p,s}(a):=\varnothing,
 349: \]
 350: and
 351: \[
 352: F_{p,s}(\emptyset):=\{\ast\}.
 353: \]
 354: Restrictions between nonempty proper intersection objects are identities,
 355: and every restriction to $\emptyset$ is the unique map. This is the
 356: presheaf \(F_{\Lambda_0}\) of
 357: \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification} with \(\Lambda_0=\varnothing\).
 358: That lemma uses the plus--plus description of sheafification, not a
 359: one-step matching-family replacement, and it treats pullbacks equal to
 360: \(\emptyset\) as strict initial objects carrying only the unique section.
 361: Since the nonempty nerve is connected, it gives
 362: \[
 363: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 364: \]
 365: 
 366: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, define a category fibred in groupoids
 367: \[
 368: \mathfrak P_\lambda\to \mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
 369: \]
 370: by the nonzero-summand construction of
 371: \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}. Thus
 372: $\mathfrak P_\lambda(a)=\varnothing$; over every nonempty proper formal
 373: intersection object $W$ its objects are
 374: $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ for $i\in I(W):=\{i\in I\mid W\to U_i\}$; its morphism
 375: sets are the sheaf sections $A_{\mathcal U}(W)$, identified with \(A\) on
 376: connected nonempty \(W\); and composition is twisted by the normalized
 377: cocycle $\alpha_\lambda$ under this identification. Over $\emptyset$ the
 378: fibre is terminal because \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). The groupoid
 379: laws, strict functoriality, prestack
 380: condition, and genuine constant-band automorphism-sheaf condition are
 381: exactly \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}(i)--(iii), whose banding
 382: uses \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}.
 383: 
 384: Let
 385: \[
 386: \mathfrak P_r:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
 387: \]
 388: As in \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}, this is the fibrewise
 389: coproduct over nonempty objects with the shared terminal fibre over
 390: $\emptyset$.
 391: The verification that this is a fibred prestack, that its restrictions are strictly functorial, that its automorphism sheaves are the genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$, and that the normalized cocycle identities give the groupoid laws is precisely \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model} with $\Lambda_0=\varnothing$. On every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$, each summand $\mathfrak P_\lambda(U)$ is connected, while there are no morphisms between distinct summands. Consequently,
 392: \[
 393: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(U)\cong \Lambda
 394: \qquad
 395: \text{for every nonempty proper }U\to a,
 396: \]
 397: and
 398: \[
 399: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)=\varnothing.
 400: \]
 401: Over $\emptyset$ the shared terminal fibre gives
 402: $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(\emptyset)\cong\{\ast\}=F_{p,s}(\emptyset)$.
 403: Hence
 404: \[
 405: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}.
 406: \]
 407: By \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(v)--(vi), the functor
 408: $F_{p,s}$ and the prestack $\mathfrak P_r$ determine a one-state semantic
 409: model $M$ with admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at its unique state $p$,
 410: with base object $[r]_p=a$, local slice site $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$,
 411: presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$, and banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r$ with
 412: genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$. This admissibility is exactly the expansion convention of
 413: \artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain}; no additional semantic
 414: closure axiom for freely adjoining presheaf or prestack data is being used.
 415: At this point all semantic interfaces required by the statement have been checked: the admissible parameter is $r$; the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve is $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$; the presheaf of local sections is the displayed $F_{p,s}$; the prestack band is the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$; the cover $\mathcal U$ is compared with derived cohomology by the Leray isomorphism of \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv); the global component sections are the sheafified terminal sections of $F_{p,s}$; and the satisfaction clauses for $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\NoAmalg_s$ are read from these matching-family and terminal-section data.
 416: By \Cref{prop:stackification-components},
 417: \[
 418: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s},
 419: \]
 420: so the sheafified global sections at $a$ are exactly
 421: \[
 422: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda.
 423: \]
 424: This proves \textup{(i)}.
 425: 
 426: For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, let $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ be the full substack of $\mathfrak L_r$ determined by the global component section $\lambda$. On the cover $\mathcal U$, take the lift objects
 427: \[
 428: x_i^{(\lambda)}:=x_i^{(\lambda,U_i)}
 429: \]
 430: and, on each overlap $U_{ij}$, take the distinguished isomorphism
 431: \[
 432: \phi_{ij}^{(\lambda)}:=(0,i,j):x_i^{(\lambda)}|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j^{(\lambda)}|_{U_{ij}}.
 433: \]
 434: Then on every triple overlap $U_{ijk}$,
 435: \[
 436: \bigl(\phi_{ik}^{(\lambda)}\bigr)^{-1}\circ
 437: \phi_{jk}^{(\lambda)}\circ
 438: \phi_{ij}^{(\lambda)}
 439: =
 440: (\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,i),
 441: \]
 442: which identifies with $\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}\in A$ under the automorphism-band identification. Therefore the \v{C}ech cocycle produced by
 443: \artresult{\v{C}ech obstruction of a component gerbe on an acyclic cover}
 444: is exactly $\alpha_\lambda$, and the component obstruction class of $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ is
 445: \[
 446: \omega_\lambda=[\alpha_\lambda].
 447: \]
 448: This is the stackification-component compatibility clause of \Cref{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model} written on the cover $\mathcal U$.
 449: Thus the finite-nerve comparison uses exactly the fixed good cover
 450: $\mathcal U$, the constant band $A$, and the normalized cocycle
 451: $\alpha_\lambda$ supplied by the homomorphism $\phi_\lambda$; the passage
 452: to derived $H^2(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})$ is the Leray comparison of
 453: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iv).
 454: Since
 455: \[
 456: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_\lambda}=\eta_A(\omega_\lambda)=\phi_\lambda,
 457: \]
 458: one gets
 459: \[
 460: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
 461: \]
 462: This proves \textup{(ii)}.
 463: 
 464: Because each $\phi_\lambda$ is nonzero and $\eta_A$ is an isomorphism, each class $\omega_\lambda$ is nonzero. By
 465: \artresult{Derived component classes detect neutrality}, every component
 466: gerbe $\mathfrak G_\lambda$ is therefore non-neutral, and
 467: \artresult{Terminal-fibre nonemptiness and neutrality} gives
 468: \[
 469: \mathfrak G_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
 470: \qquad
 471: (\forall \lambda\in\Lambda).
 472: \]
 473: Hence
 474: \[
 475: \mathfrak L_r(a)=\varnothing.
 476: \]
 477: Since also
 478: \[
 479: \mathfrak P_r(a)=\varnothing,
 480: \]
 481: the stackification functor on the terminal fibre is
 482: \[
 483: (\iota_r)_a:\mathfrak P_r(a)\to \mathfrak L_r(a),
 484: \]
 485: that is, the empty functor $\varnothing\to\varnothing$, and it is essentially surjective. Thus $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$.
 486: 
 487: Moreover,
 488: \[
 489: \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a)\cong \Lambda\neq\varnothing,
 490: \]
 491: and the cover $\mathcal U$ carries an explicit strict matching family:
 492: choose any $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and put the section $\lambda\in
 493: F_{p,s}(U_i)=\Lambda$ on every member $U_i$. Restrictions between
 494: nonempty proper intersections are identities, and restrictions to
 495: $\emptyset$ are unique, so the family agrees on every pullback overlap.
 496: Hence \Cref{def:existence-levels}(ii) gives
 497: \[
 498: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
 499: \]
 500: On the other hand,
 501: \[
 502: F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing,
 503: \]
 504: so
 505: \[
 506: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
 507: \]
 508: Since $r$ is admissible by construction, it follows that
 509: \[
 510: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
 511: \]
 512: This proves \textup{(iii)}.
 513: 
 514: Finally, \textup{(iv)} follows by applying
 515: \artresult{Label-aware quotient} and \artresult{Common-character quotient}
 516: to the family
 517: \[
 518: K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)
 519: \qquad
 520: (\lambda\in\Lambda).
 521: \]
 522: The last sentence is the same statement rewritten in terms of the images of the chosen homomorphisms.
 523: \end{proof}
 524: 
 525: The preceding construction theorem makes every component gerbe non-neutral. The next theorem removes that restriction and identifies the neutral component gerbes exactly with the zero homomorphisms.

+\section{The finite-site interface}\label{sec:preliminaries}
 
-We fix the semantic framework used throughout. In particular, we distinguish truth-preserving reduct expansion from the weaker singleton embedding that links the pointwise layer to universal team satisfaction.

-\subsection*{Standing notation}
-States are denoted by $p,q,u$, and admissible parameters by $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ with associated base object $a=[r]_p$. The reference-refinement site at a state and sort is $\mathcal C_{p,s}$, the presheaf of local sections is $F_{p,s}$, the set of global component sections is $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$, and component obstruction classes are denoted by $\omega$ or $\omega_v$.
+The results use a site, a presheaf, and a banded prestack as input.  No
+semantic construction of these data is assumed.  This section records the
+small interface needed later and fixes the distinction between a matching
+family and an amalgamation.

-\begin{proposition}[Concrete instantiation of the finite chain]\label{prop:chain-instantiation}
-The chain
-\[
-\mathbb L_0\xhookrightarrow{\iota} \mathbb L_1\preceq \mathbb L_2\preceq \mathbb L_3\preceq \mathbb L_4
-\]
-is instantiated as follows.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=3em]
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb L_1$ (pointwise states to information states: singleton-state embedding).}
-The language embedding
-\[
-e_{0,1}:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow \Sigma_1
-\]
-is the inclusion of the underlying many-sorted symbols. In addition, $\Sigma_1$ contains the parameter sorts $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ (one for each designated sort $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$) together with their equality; no geometric predicates or site structure is imposed at this step. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{1,0}:\Mod_1\to\Mod_0
-\]
-forgets the information-state presentation and the reference carrier sets, remembering only the underlying many-sorted structure of $\Sigma_0$. A pointwise state $\rho$ in $\mathbb L_0$ is represented inside $\mathbb L_1$ by the singleton information state
-\[
-\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho):=(\Gamma,\{\rho\}).
-\]
-By \Cref{prop:singleton-conservativity},
-\[
-M,\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{1,0}(M),\rho\Vdash_0\varphi
-\]
-for every $\mathbb L_0$-formula $\varphi$. This is a singleton-state embedding in the sense of \Cref{def:singleton-semantic-embedding}: it preserves satisfaction of $\mathbb L_0$-formulas on the canonical singleton image but does not provide a state projection from arbitrary $\mathbb L_1$-states back to $\mathbb L_0$-states.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_1\leadsto\mathbb L_2$ (information states to presheaves of local sections).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{1,2}:\Sigma_1\hookrightarrow \Sigma_2
-\]
-adjoins the admissibility predicates, the local-section predicates $\LocSec_s$, $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, the site-structure symbols (covers, refinement preorder, pullbacks), and the associated geometric notation. The parameter sorts $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and their equality are already present in $\Sigma_1$; the step from $\mathbb L_1$ to $\mathbb L_2$ equips admissible parameters with the geometric structure needed to state local-to-global questions. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{2,1}:\Mod_2\to\Mod_1
-\]
-forgets the reference-refinement sites, covers, and presheaves of local sections but retains the parameter sorts and their carrier sets. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{2,1}:\St_2(M)\to \St_1(U_{2,1}(M))
-\]
-is the identity on the underlying information state $(\Gamma_p,R_p)$. Since the satisfaction clauses for formulas already in $\mathrm{Form}_1$ never inspect the added presheaf data, one has
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_2\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{2,1}(M),\pi^M_{2,1}(p)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_1$.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_2\leadsto\mathbb L_3$ (presheaves to obstruction data).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{2,3}:\Sigma_2\hookrightarrow \Sigma_3
-\]
-adjoins the predicates and symbols used to talk about structural absence, global component sections, component gerbes, and obstruction classes. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{3,2}:\Mod_3\to\Mod_2
-\]
-drops the banded groupoid lift, band, component-gerbe, and obstruction data. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{3,2}:\St_3(M)\to \St_2(U_{3,2}(M))
-\]
-again leaves the underlying state unchanged. Formulas from $\mathrm{Form}_2$ are evaluated exactly as before, so
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_3\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{3,2}(M),\pi^M_{3,2}(p)\Vdash_2\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_2$.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_3\leadsto\mathbb L_4$ (obstruction data to refinement dynamics).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{3,4}:\Sigma_3\hookrightarrow \Sigma_4
-\]
-adjoins the update relations, axis indices, support notions, and rewrite language of the refinement layer. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{4,3}:\Mod_4\to\Mod_3
-\]
-forgets the dynamic axes, update structure, and rewrite operations. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{4,3}:\St_4(M)\to \St_3(U_{4,3}(M))
-\]
-forgets only the new dynamic bookkeeping. Because the satisfaction clauses for $\mathrm{Form}_3$ do not depend on that added bookkeeping, one has
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_4\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{4,3}(M),\pi^M_{4,3}(p)\Vdash_3\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_3$.
+\item a strict matching family determines a section of \((aF)(a)\); if
+      \(F\) is separated on the slice over \(a\), every section of
+      \((aF)(a)\) is represented by a strict matching family on a cover of
+      \(a\).  Hence, under this separatedness hypothesis,
+      \[

+\item under separatedness on the slice and terminal essential surjectivity,
+      \(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\) holds exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is
+      nonempty and \(\mathfrak L(a)\) is empty.
 \end{enumerate}
-The base boundary $\mathbb L_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb L_1$ is a singleton-state embedding: pointwise states embed faithfully into information states, preserving satisfaction of all $\mathbb L_0$-formulas on that canonical image. -\begin{proposition}[Concrete instantiation of the finite chain]\label{prop:chain-instantiation}

-\[

-for every $\mathbb L_0$-formula $\varphi$. -forgets only the new dynamic bookkeeping. Because the satisfaction clauses for $\mathrm{Form}_3$ do not depend on that added bookkeeping, one has
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_4\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{4,3}(M),\pi^M_{4,3}(p)\Vdash_3\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_3$.
+\item a strict matching family determines a section of \((aF)(a)\); if
+      \(F\) is separated on the slice over \(a\), every section of
+      \((aF)(a)\) is represented by a strict matching family on a cover of
+      \(a\).  Hence, under this separatedness hypothesis,
+      \[
+      \operatorname{Match}(F,a)
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      (aF)(a)\ne\varnothing;
+      \]
+\item \(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\).
+      If \(\iota\) is terminally essentially surjective, these are also
+      equivalent to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\);
+\item under separatedness on the slice and terminal essential surjectivity,
+      \(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\) holds exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is
+      nonempty and \(\mathfrak L(a)\) is empty.
 \end{enumerate}
-The base boundary $\mathbb L_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb L_1$ is a singleton-state embedding: pointwise states embed faithfully into information states, preserving satisfaction of all $\mathbb L_0$-formulas on that canonical image. The three higher boundaries $\mathbb L_1\preceq\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3\preceq\mathbb L_4$ are truth-preserving reduct expansions in the sense of \Cref{def:conservative-extension}, each with an explicit forgetful functor and state projection.
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For the first boundary, the data displayed in \textup{(i)} give the language embedding
-\[
-e_{0,1}:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow\Sigma_1,
-\]
-the forgetful functor $U_{1,0}$, and for each pointwise state $\rho$ the canonical singleton information state
-\[
-\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)=(\Gamma,\{\rho\}).
-\]
-\Cref{prop:singleton-conservativity} gives, for every $\mathbb L_0$-formula $\varphi$,
+Applying \(u\) to a strict matching family gives a matching family in the
+sheaf \(aF\), which has a unique amalgamation in \((aF)(a)\).  Conversely,
+let \(\xi\in(aF)(a)\).  The plus--plus description of sheafification gives
+a cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\) and sections \(s_i\in F(U_i)\) representing
+\(\xi|_{U_i}\), with the following local equality on each overlap: there is
+a cover \(\{V_{ijk}\to U_{ij}\}_k\) such that
 \[
-M,\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{1,0}(M),\rho\Vdash_0\varphi.
+ s_i|_{V_{ijk}}=s_j|_{V_{ijk}}.
 \]
-These are exactly the three pieces of structure and the preservation condition required in \Cref{def:singleton-semantic-embedding}. Notice that the verification uses only singleton information states; it does not assert a projection from arbitrary $\mathbb L_1$-states to pointwise states.
+Every \(U_{ij}\to a\) is an object of the slice.  Separatedness there turns
+these locally witnessed equalities into
+\(s_i|_{U_{ij}}=s_j|_{U_{ij}}\).  The \(s_i\) therefore form a strict
+matching family.  This proves (i).
 
-For $\mathbb L_1\preceq\mathbb L_2$, the displayed clauses fix the object language of the expansion: $\Sigma_2$ is the disjoint expansion of $\Sigma_1$ by the local-section and site symbols listed in \textup{(ii)}, $\Mod_2$ is the class of $\Sigma_2$-expansions whose $\Sigma_1$-reduct is obtained by $U_{2,1}$, and $\pi^M_{2,1}$ is the identity on the underlying information state. Equivalently, this is the presheaf instance of the typed-expansion interface of \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. Atomic $\Sigma_1$-formulas use only symbols retained by $U_{2,1}$. Thus \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} gives, for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_1$,
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_2\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{2,1}(M),\pi^M_{2,1}(p)\Vdash_1\varphi,
-\]
-which is \Cref{def:conservative-extension}.
-
-The same lemma applies to $\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3$. Here $\Sigma_3$ is the disjoint expansion of $\Sigma_2$ by the banded-groupoid-lift, band, component-gerbe, matching-without-amalgamation, and obstruction-class symbols listed in \textup{(iii)}. The admissible models are precisely the corresponding well-typed expansions singled out in \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. The functor $U_{3,2}$ forgets precisely those symbols, while $\pi^M_{3,2}$ leaves the underlying state unchanged. Atomic $\Sigma_2$-formulas contain no symbols for the forgotten gerbe or obstruction data, so \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_3\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{3,2}(M),\pi^M_{3,2}(p)\Vdash_2\varphi
-\qquad(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_2).
-\]
-Thus $\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3$.
-
-Finally, $\Sigma_4$ is obtained from $\Sigma_3$ by adjoining only the refinement-dynamic axes, update structure, support notions, and rewrite operations listed in \textup{(iv)}. This is the refinement-dynamic instance of \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. The functor $U_{4,3}$ forgets exactly that dynamic structure, and $\pi^M_{4,3}$ forgets only the corresponding state bookkeeping. Atomic $\Sigma_3$-formulas are interpreted through the reduct, so \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} yields
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_4\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{4,3}(M),\pi^M_{4,3}(p)\Vdash_3\varphi
-\qquad(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_3).
-\]
-Consequently the three upper steps are truth-preserving reduct expansions, and the displayed finite chain has exactly the asserted form.
+The isomorphism \(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong F(a)\) proves
+the first equivalence in (ii).  The forward implication from
+\(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\) is
+given by \(\iota\), and the converse is terminal essential surjectivity.
+Finally, (iii) is obtained by combining (i), (ii), and the definition of
+\(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\).
 \end{proof}
 
-Hence the truth-preserving-reduct part of the chain begins at $\mathbb L_1$.
+The article treats \((\mathcal C,F,\mathfrak P,\mathscr A)\) as supplied
+finite-site lift data.  In particular, the realization theorem below is not
+derived from a lower team-semantic model.  A narrow lower-language separation
+example and the presentation bookkeeping removed from the core argument are
+given in the technical appendix
+\cite[Appendix~B]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} only as context; they
+do not generate the lift.

-\begin{corollary}[Finite-chain invariance]\label{cor:whole-chain-invariance}
-If
+Let \(\mathscr A\) be an abelian sheaf on \(\mathcal C\).  An

-Precisely, an expansion from $\mathbb L_m$ to $\mathbb L_n$ is admissible when

-Accordingly, the construction theorems in later sections are internal

-\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)} \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band),

-\begin{remark}[Relation to the companion paper]

-\begin{definition}[Banded stack lift of the component sheaf]\label{def:banded-stack-lift}
-For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, abbreviate

-\qquad

-For a sheafified global section

-\]
-the \emph{$v$-component substack} of $\mathfrak E_r$ is the full substack

-\]
-for objects $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, where $\epsilon_{r,U}$ denotes the component of $\epsilon_r$ at $U$.

-\begin{lemma}[Equivalence data and component transport]\label{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport}
-Let
-\[
-(\mathfrak E_r,\Band,\epsilon_r),
-\qquad
-(\mathfrak E'_r,\Band',\epsilon'_r)

-\Phi:\mathfrak E_r\to\mathfrak E'_r

-\[
-\epsilon'_r\circ\pi_0(\Phi)=\epsilon_r.
-\]
-Then, for every sheafified global section $v$, $\Phi$ restricts to an equivalence of full component substacks
-\[
-\Phi_v:\mathfrak E_r[v]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak E'_r[v],
-\]
-and this restricted equivalence is banded by $\theta$.
-\end{lemma}
+\end{proposition}

-The compatibility condition gives

-=

-=
-\epsilon_{r,U}([x])
-=

-Thus $\Phi(x)\in\mathfrak E'_r[v](U)$, so $\Phi$ restricts to a functor

-=

-\]

+Clause (i) is precisely the component-gerbe construction of
+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  Concretely, \(v|_X\) is locally

-\begin{lemma}[Transport of Giraud classes under banded equivalence]\label{lem:giraud-class-transport}
-Let $\mathfrak G$ be a $\Band$-banded gerbe and let $\mathfrak G'$ be a $\Band'$-banded gerbe on the same site $\mathcal C$. Suppose
-\[
-\Phi:\mathfrak G\to\mathfrak G'
-\]
-is an equivalence of stacks whose induced maps on automorphism sheaves identify the bands through an isomorphism
-\[
-\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-\theta_*[\mathfrak G]=[\mathfrak G']
-\qquad\text{in}\qquad
-H^2(\mathcal C,\Band').
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Choose a cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ which locally trivializes $\mathfrak G$, objects $x_i\in\mathfrak G(U_i)$, and descent isomorphisms
-\[
-\varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.
-\]
-The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
-\[
-\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
-\]
-Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
-\[
-\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
-=
-\Phi(c_{ijk}),
-\]
-which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
-
-The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
-\[
-(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
-\]
-is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
+The classification of abelian-banded gerbes identifies equivalence classes
+with \(H^2\), with the neutral gerbes representing zero
+\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}.  On a site with terminal object \(a\), neutrality
+is exactly existence of an object over \(a\), proving (ii).  For (iii), the
+component compatibility makes \(\Phi\) restrict to the full component
+substacks.  Applying \(\Phi\) to local objects and overlap arrows applies
+\(\theta\) to their triple-overlap defect cocycle.  This is the standard
+naturality of Giraud classification under a banded equivalence
+\cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Presheaf-to-component-gerbe comparison criterion]
+\label{thm:gerbe-null-semantics}
+Let \(F\) be separated on the slice over \(a\), and let
+\(\mathfrak P\) be an abelian-banded prestack lift whose stackification map
+is terminally essentially surjective.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:matching-gerbe-criterion}
+ \operatorname{MWA}(F,a)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ (aF)(a)\ne\varnothing
+ \ \text{and}\ 
+ \mathfrak G_v\text{ is non-neutral for every }v\in(aF)(a).
+\end{equation}
+Equivalently, every \(\omega_v\) is nonzero.  The dependencies are
 \[
-\delta_{\mathfrak E_r}(v)=[\mathfrak G_v]=\omega_v.
+\begin{array}{c@{\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad}c}
+ \operatorname{Match}(F,a)&(aF)(a)\ne\varnothing
+ \quad\text{(slice separatedness)},\\[2mm]
+ v\in(aF)(a)&\mathfrak G_v\text{ a component gerbe}
+ \quad\text{(Giraud III.2.1.5.3)},\\[2mm]
+ F(a)\ne\varnothing&\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing
+ \quad\text{(terminal essential surjectivity)},\\[2mm]
+ \mathfrak G_v(a)\ne\varnothing&\mathfrak G_v\text{ neutral}
+ \quad\text{(Giraud classification)}.
+\end{array}
 \]

-\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}
-In the pullback-based setting of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}, and using only the banded groupoid lift and component data fixed there, every global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ determines a full substack $\mathfrak G_v\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ that is a banded $\Band$-gerbe over $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. In particular, neither essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ nor the derived comparison hypothesis \textup{(H4)} is used here.
 \end{theorem}
 
 \begin{proof}
-By \suppresult{Components of the stackification}, the stackification
-\[
-\mathfrak E_r:=\mathfrak L_r
-\]
-is a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf of
-$a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$. The global component section $v$ is a section of
-\[
-\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong (a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(a),
-\]
-and the full substack
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v(U)=
-\{x\in\mathfrak L_r(U)\mid [x]\ \text{restricts to}\ v|_U\}
-\]
-is therefore exactly the $v$-component substack
-$\mathfrak E_r[v]$ of \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}.
+By \Cref{prop:finite-site-semantic-interface}(i), matching is equivalent to
+\((aF)(a)\ne\varnothing\).  By clause (ii) of that proposition and terminal
+essential surjectivity, \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\) is equivalent to
+\(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\).  The latter holds exactly when one of the
+full components \(\mathfrak G_v\) contains an object over \(a\).  By
+\Cref{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package}(ii), this is equivalent to
+neutrality of at least one component gerbe.  Negating that statement while
+retaining nonemptiness of \((aF)(a)\) proves
+\eqref{eq:matching-gerbe-criterion}; the cohomological form follows from the
+same standard package.
+\end{proof}
 
-We recall why this is a gerbe. Because $\mathfrak L_r$ is a stack in
-groupoids, every descent datum for objects whose component lies over
-$v$ glues to an object whose component still lies over $v$; hence
-$\mathfrak G_v$ is a full substack. Local nonemptiness follows from the
-definition of a global component section as a section of the sheaf of connected
-components: after passing to a cover of any object $U$, the section

-is the local form of equality in the component sheaf: if two objects of
-$\mathfrak G_v(U)$ have component $v|_U$, then they become isomorphic
-after a cover of $U$. Fullness is built into the definition of
-$\mathfrak G_v$, so no morphisms between objects in the component are
-discarded. Finally, for every object $x$ of $\mathfrak G_v(U)$, the
-automorphism sheaf of $x$ inside $\mathfrak G_v$ is the same as its
-automorphism sheaf inside $\mathfrak L_r$, and this sheaf is identified
-with $\Band|_{\mathcal C_a/U}$ by the banding of the groupoid lift
-prestack and its stackification. Thus $\mathfrak G_v$ is a
-$\Band$-banded gerbe.
+The criterion is a site-theoretic reformulation of the meet-semilattice
+comparison in the companion manuscript

-\begin{theorem}[\v{C}ech obstruction of a component gerbe on an acyclic cover]\label{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction}
-Assume that $\mathfrak G_v$ is a banded component gerbe with band $\Band$ in the sense of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}. Using only this gerbe and a single acyclic cover of $a$, let
-\[
-\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in \Cov_{p,s}(a)
-\]

-\[

-\]
-for the corresponding simplices. Assume that the component gerbe is locally nonempty on the cover, so that objects
-\[
-x_i\in \mathfrak G_v(U_i)
-\]
-exist for all $i$, and assume
-\[
-H^1(U_{i_0\cdots i_n},\Band)=0
-\]
-for every nonempty intersection used below, including all members, pairwise overlaps, triple overlaps, and quadruple overlaps appearing in the descent calculation.
+\begin{theorem}[Terminal rigidity for representative-rigid lifts]
+\label{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}
+Let \(F\) be separated on the slice over \(a\), and let \(\mathfrak P\) be a
+representative-rigid \(\mathscr A\)-banded prestack lift of \(F\).  Write
+\(u:F\to aF\) and \(\iota:\mathfrak P\to\mathfrak L=a(\mathfrak P)\).
 Then:
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item for every pair $(i,j)$ there exists an isomorphism
-\[
-\theta_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim} x_j|_{U_{ij}};
-\]
-\item on each triple overlap $U_{ijk}$, the element
-\[
-c_{ijk}:=\theta_{ik}^{-1}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ \theta_{jk}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ \theta_{ij}|_{U_{ijk}}
-\in \Band(U_{ijk})
-\]
-defines a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle $c=(c_{ijk})\in \check Z^2(\mathcal U,\Band)$;
-\item the class $[c]\in \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)$ depends only on the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and the chosen cover: changing the local lift objects or the comparison isomorphisms changes $c$ by a \v{C}ech coboundary, and refinements of acyclic covers pull this class back functorially;
-\item the class $[c]$ vanishes if and only if the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral over $a$.
+\item terminal essential surjectivity of \(\iota\) implies that
+      \(u_a:F(a)\to(aF)(a)\) is surjective;
+\item if \(H^1(\mathcal C,\mathscr A)=0\), surjectivity of \(u_a\) implies
+      terminal essential surjectivity of \(\iota\).
 \end{enumerate}
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By local nonemptiness, fix objects $x_i\in \mathfrak G_v(U_i)$. For every pair $(i,j)$, the sheaf
-\[
-\mathrm{Isom}(x_i|_{U_{ij}},x_j|_{U_{ij}})
-\]
-is a $\Band|_{U_{ij}}$-torsor. The vanishing
-\[
-H^1(U_{ij},\Band)=0
-\]

-\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\subseteq \Cov_{p,s}(a)
-\]
-such that every cover \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}\) in the family has a
-\v{C}ech nerve in the slice site, trivializes the band on all intersections
-used in degrees \(0,1,2\), and satisfies the following comparison condition:
-the canonical refinement map
-\[
-\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)}
-\check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)
-\longrightarrow
-H^2(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,\Band)
-\]
-is an isomorphism. One way to verify this condition is the usual Leray
-hypothesis: all nonempty finite intersections appearing in the family are
-\(\Band\)-acyclic in every positive degree needed for the derived
-comparison. The definition itself, however, records the comparison
-isomorphism as the required assumption; the later theorems do not silently
-infer derived \(H^2\) from a single \v{C}ech cocycle unless this hypothesis, or
-the explicit finite good-cover Leray theorem of
-\suppresult{Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion}, is in force.
-\end{definition}
+The exact ancestry of this construction is classical.  Giraud proves that
+the projection of a stack to its sheaf of connected components is a gerbe
+over that sheaf, and that pullback along a component section gives the
+corresponding maximal subgerbe
+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  The next proposition records this
+standard construction and the two compatibilities used later.  It is an
+input, not an originality claim.
 
-\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},nosep]
-\item\label{hyp:admitted-prestack} An admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$ with $a=[r]_p$, equipped with a banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r \to \mathcal C_a$ and band $\Band$ in the sense of \suppresult{Banded groupoid lift and stackification}.
-\item\label{hyp:band-identification} The band $\Band$ is identified with a fixed abelian sheaf on the slice site $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$.
-\item\label{hyp:global-conservativity} The banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \suppresult{Essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre}.
-\item\label{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted} For every global component section \(v\), a
-\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis in the sense of
-\Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package} has been fixed.
+\begin{proposition}[Standard component-gerbe package]
+\label{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package}
+Let \(\mathfrak E\) be a stack in groupoids on \(\mathcal C\), and let
+\(v\in\pi_0(\mathfrak E)(a)\).
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item The full substack \(\mathfrak E[v]\) is the maximal gerbe over the
+      section \(v\).  If \(\mathfrak E\) is banded by an abelian sheaf
+      \(\mathscr A\), then \(\mathfrak E[v]\) has the restricted
+      \(\mathscr A\)-banding.
+\item Its Giraud class satisfies
+      \[
+      [\mathfrak E[v]]=0\text{ in }H^2(\mathcal C,\mathscr A)
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v]\text{ is neutral}
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v](a)\ne\varnothing.
+      \]
+\item Suppose \(\Phi:\mathfrak E\to\mathfrak E'\) is a banded equivalence,
+      its band map is \(\theta:\mathscr A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr A'\),
+      and its component map carries \(v\) to \(v'\).  Then \(\Phi\)
+      restricts to a banded equivalence
+      \(\mathfrak E[v]\simeq\mathfrak E'[v']\), and
+      \[
+      \theta_*[\mathfrak E[v]]=[\mathfrak E'[v']].
+      \]
 \end{enumerate}
-
-When a statement compares global component sections with the strict predicate
-\(\CompSec_s\), or with \(\NoAmalg_s\) through that predicate,
-it separately assumes that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice.
-Without this separatedness assumption global component sections are only
-sheafified sections, and no strict compatible family is asserted.

-\begin{remark}[\v{C}ech versus derived cohomology]\label{rem:cech-vs-derived}
-Hypothesis \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, equivalently the hypothesis of
-\Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}, is the precise comparison
-assumption governing the passage between \v{C}ech and derived $H^2$. It
-requires the comparison isomorphism itself; acyclicity in positive degrees is
-one standard sufficient Leray condition, not an unstated assumption unless
-explicitly invoked. Without this hypothesis, the component obstruction class lives in
-the filtered colimit
-\[
-\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)} \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band),
-\]
-and the non-neutrality statement in \Cref{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction} is purely \v{C}ech-theoretic. With \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, this colimit is canonically identified with the derived $H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$, and the obstruction class $\omega_v$ is an element of derived cohomology. All theorems in this subsection state explicitly whether they use only the \v{C}ech-level data or additionally require the comparison isomorphism.
-\end{remark}

-\begin{remark}[Relation to the companion paper]
-The companion paper \cite{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} formulates component obstructions relative to a chosen gluing-sensitive banded groupoid lift and its stackification. The present section isolates the three constructions needed later: the promotion of cover-relative \v{C}ech classes to derived classes $\omega_v$ under \textup{(H4)}, the reformulation of the obstruction theory for arbitrary banded stack lifts of the component sheaf of the sheafified presheaf of local sections, and the componentwise neutrality criteria stated directly in terms of component gerbes.
-\end{remark}

-\begin{definition}[Component gerbes and component obstruction classes]\label{def:component-gerbes}\label{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}
-Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, write
-\[
-a=[r]_p,
-\]

-Assume moreover that \textup{(H4)} holds. For each global component section $v$ and each cover

-Refinement compatibility identifies these classes in the filtered system, and the comparison isomorphism in \textup{(H4)} therefore determines a unique derived class
-\[

-\begin{definition}[Banded stack lift of the component sheaf]\label{def:banded-stack-lift}
-For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, abbreviate
-\[
-a=[r]_p,
-\qquad

-\]
-and fix an abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$. Let $\mathfrak E_r$ be a

-\[

-consisting of such a stack together with an isomorphism of sheaves
-\[
-\epsilon_r:\pi_0(\mathfrak E_r)\xrightarrow{\sim} a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
-\]
-on $\mathcal C_a$.
-
-For a sheafified global section
-\[
-v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a),
-\]
-the \emph{$v$-component substack} of $\mathfrak E_r$ is the full substack
-\[
-\mathfrak E_r[v](U):=
-\bigl\{x\in \mathfrak E_r(U)\mid \epsilon_{r,U}([x])=v|_U\bigr\}
-\]
-for objects $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, where $\epsilon_{r,U}$ denotes the component of $\epsilon_r$ at $U$.
-\end{definition}
