\appendix

We collect two auxiliary topics. The first concerns the refinement-dynamic extension together with finite-state complexity bounds for the associated information-determination notions. The second gives the GHZ/Mermin banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf mentioned in the introduction.
\section{Finite-state complexity bounds}\label{sec:appendix-complexity}

We record the finite-state upper bounds for the information-determination notions attached to the refinement-dynamic extension of the semantics.

For this appendix, assume that the indexed refinement system is finite and that a distinguished formula $\chi$ is part of the input together with polynomial-time decidable tables for the relations
\[
q\mapsto (M,q\Vdash\chi),
\qquad
q\mapsto (M,q\Vdash\neg\chi),
\qquad
q\mapsto (\mathrm{info}_j(q))_{j\in J}.
\]
The finite information maps for refinement axes $\mathrm{info}_j$ of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps} are assumed to be part of the input model; agreement of $K$-information between two states is checked by comparing $\mathrm{info}_j(q)=\mathrm{info}_j(r)$ for each $j\in K$. This is the natural finite encoding once the underlying semantic state graph has already been computed and the information-determination problems are asked over that graph. No matching lower bounds are claimed here.

We consider the decision problems \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, and \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} associated with \Cref{def:axis-support,def:axis-indispensability}. For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} we use the standard class $\mathrm{D}^P$ in the sense of Papadimitriou and Yannakakis \cite{PapadimitriouYannakakis1984}.

\begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.

For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.

For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
\end{proof}

\section{Refinement dynamics}\label{sec:appendix-dynamics}

This section contains the formal refinement-dynamic material.

\subsection{Refinement dynamics and information determination}\label{sec:appendix-multiaxis-refinement}

The previous sections analyzed satisfaction at a fixed state. We now treat refinement itself as a dynamics: the satisfaction clause stays unchanged, but the set of assignments may shrink along different axes of information. The results apply to model classes in which refinement induces morphisms of slice sites and compatible maps of finite nerves.

\subsubsection{Dynamic refinement}

\begin{definition}[Indexed refinement system]\label{def:multi-axis-dynamic-structure}
Fix a model $M$. A \emph{indexed refinement system} on $M$ is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak{D}=\bigl(\St(M),\le,\tau,J,\{\rightsquigarrow_j\}_{j\in J}\bigr),
\]
where $J$ is an axis set, each $\rightsquigarrow_j$ is a single-axis refinement relation satisfying
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow q\le p,
\]
and $\tau:\St(M)\to T$ maps states to a linearly ordered set $T$ such that
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow \tau(q)\ge \tau(p).
\]
For finite $K\subseteq J$, write $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$ if $q$ is reachable from $p$ by a finite chain of refinements using only axes in $K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Updates preserve satisfaction]\label{prop:updates-preserve-forcing}
If $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$ and $M,p\Vdash\varphi$, then $M,q\Vdash\varphi^\uparrow$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every indexed step is a refinement by \Cref{def:multi-axis-dynamic-structure}, so $q\le p$. The claim is therefore immediate from
\artresult{Persistence of universal team satisfaction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Delayed decidability]\label{def:delayed-decidability}
Let $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$. We say that $\varphi$ undergoes \emph{delayed decidability} from $p$ to $q$ if
\[
M,p\nVdash\varphi,\qquad
M,p\nVdash\neg\varphi,\qquad
\text{but}\qquad
M,q\Downarrow\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Delayed decidability does not create truth]\label{prop:delayed-no-new-truth}
If $\varphi$ undergoes delayed decidability in a transition $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$, then the passage from $p$ to $q$ acts by eliminating assignments from $R_p$ rather than by changing the truth conditions of $\varphi$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ or $M,p\Vdash\neg\varphi$ already held, then \Cref{prop:updates-preserve-forcing} would preserve that judgment at $q$. Hence delayed decidability can occur only because the refinement $q\le p$ has discarded assignments that formerly gave incompatible outcomes. The semantic clause for $\varphi$ itself has not changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Delayed classification is non-retrocausal]\label{prop:nonretrocausal-delayed-classification}
Let $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$, and suppose that $q$ is $\tau$-minimal among the $K$-reachable states that decide $\varphi$. Then every $u$ with
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K u
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\tau(u)<\tau(q)
\]
is still undecided on $\varphi$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If some earlier $u$ with $\tau(u)<\tau(q)$ already decided $\varphi$, then $q$ would not be $\tau$-minimal among the deciding states reachable from $p$. Thus no earlier stage carries the later decision. The decision at $q$ records newly available discriminatory power at $q$, not a change in the past.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Information determination and explicit lifting}

\begin{definition}[Finite information maps for refinement axes]\label{def:axis-information-maps}
Fix an indexed refinement system $\mathfrak{D}$ on a model $M$. For each axis $j\in J$, assume there is a finite set $I_j$ and a map
\[
\mathrm{info}_j:\{q\in\St(M)\mid p\rightsquigarrow_K q\text{ for some finite }K\ni j\}\longrightarrow I_j.
\]
For states $q$ and $r$ reachable from $p$ via $K$-refinements and a subset $L\subseteq K$, we say that $q$ and $r$ \emph{agree on $L$-information} if
\[
\mathrm{info}_j(q)=\mathrm{info}_j(r)
\qquad
\text{for every }j\in L.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Information-determining axis sets and minimality]\label{def:axis-support}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite. We say that $K$ \emph{determines} a formula $\varphi$ at $p$, written $K\triangleright_p\varphi$, if whenever
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
and both $q$ and $r$ decide $\varphi$, agreement of the $K$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}) implies agreement of the decision. An information-determining set $K$ is \emph{minimal} if no proper subset of $K$ still determines $\varphi$ at $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Necessity of a refinement axis]\label{def:axis-indispensability}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite and let $j\in K$. We say that $j$ is \emph{necessary relative to $K$} for $\varphi$ at $p$ if there exist states $q$ and $r$ with
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
such that $q$ and $r$ agree on $(K\setminus\{j\})$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}), while
\[
M,q\Vdash\varphi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M,r\Vdash\neg\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Necessity of a refinement axis implies minimality]\label{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}
If $K\triangleright_p\varphi$ and every $j\in K$ is necessary relative to $K$ for $\varphi$ at $p$, then $K$ is a minimal information-determining axis set for $\varphi$ at $p$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Assume that a proper subset $L\subsetneq K$ still determined $\varphi$, and choose $j\in K\setminus L$. Any two states that agree on all axes in $K\setminus\{j\}$ automatically agree on all axes in $L$, contradicting the necessity of the refinement axis $j$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Pairwise commuting refinements]\label{def:axis-orthogonality}
Two axes $j,k\in J$ are \emph{pairwise commuting at $p$} if whenever
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_k r,
\]
there exists a state $u$ such that
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_{\{j,k\}} u,
\qquad
u\le q,
\qquad
u\le r.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Common refinements and completeness]\label{def:fusion-state}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite, and suppose that for each $j\in K$ there is a single-axis refinement $p\rightsquigarrow_j q_j$. A state $u$ is a \emph{common refinement} for the family $(q_j)_{j\in K}$ if
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K u
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
u\le q_j\ \text{for every }j\in K.
\]
The indexed refinement system \emph{admits all required common refinements} if every finite pairwise commuting family of single-axis refinements admits a common refinement.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit lifting principle]\label{cor:explicit-lifting}
Assume that all required common refinements exist. Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite, and for each $j\in K$ let
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q_j
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Read_{q_j,s_j}(r_j)=v_j\neq \Indet.
\]
If the single-axis refinements are pairwise commuting at $p$, then there exists a common refinement $u$ such that
\[
\Read_{u,s_j}(r_j)=v_j
\qquad
(\forall j\in K).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By the common-refinement hypothesis there exists a common refinement $u$ with $u\le q_j$ for all $j\in K$. Since each $q_j$ carries a determined typed readout, \Cref{prop:typed-readout-persistence} transports that readout to the common refinement $u$. Thus all axis-wise readout judgments hold simultaneously at one state.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Componentwise obstruction monotonicity}

The obstruction theory of \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} becomes dynamic once global component sections and their component gerbes are transported along refinement. In the model classes just described, the basic structural fact is that refinement can only shrink the homological image subgroup and enlarge its cokernel.

\begin{proposition}[Refinement monotonicity of componentwise homological cokernels]\label{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}
Let $q\le p$, let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admissible at both states, and write
\[
a_p=[r]_p,
\qquad
a_q=[r]_q.
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item there is a morphism of slice sites
\[
f_{q,p}:\mathcal C_{q,s}/a_q\to \mathcal C_{p,s}/a_p;
\]
\item the banded groupoid lift at $q$ is equivalent to the pullback of the banded groupoid lift at $p$ along $f_{q,p}$;
\item global component sections pull back along refinement, and for a component section $w\in \Vis_{q,s}(r)$ lying above $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ the corresponding component gerbes satisfy
\[
\mathfrak G_w\simeq f_{q,p}^*(\mathfrak G_v);
\]
\item compatible finite nerve representatives have been chosen together with a simplicial refinement map
\[
N(f_{q,p}):N(\mathcal U_q)\to N(\mathcal U_p)
\]
such that the induced component obstruction classes satisfy
\[
\omega_w=N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)
\]
with the same finite abelian band $A$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
X_v\subseteq X_w,
\qquad
K_w\subseteq K_v,
\qquad
Q_w\twoheadrightarrow Q_v,
\qquad
|K_w|\le |K_v|.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The pullback of gerbes is again a gerbe, and the induced cohomology class is the pullback of the original one \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}, \cite[Theorem~3.11]{BerghSchnurer2021}. Naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the simplicial refinement map $N(f_{q,p})$ gives the cohomological compatibility needed below. Let $\chi\in X_v$. Then
\[
\chi_*(\omega_v)=0.
\]
Applying the pullback $N(f_{q,p})^*$ gives
\[
\chi_*(\omega_w)=\chi_*\bigl(N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)\bigr)=N(f_{q,p})^*\bigl(\chi_*(\omega_v)\bigr)=0,
\]
so $\chi\in X_w$. Hence $X_v\subseteq X_w$.

By \artresult{Character-theoretic detection of the homological cokernel},
\[
K_v=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_v}\ker\chi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
K_w=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_w}\ker\chi.
\]
Since $X_v\subseteq X_w$, intersecting over the larger family gives the smaller subgroup, so $K_w\subseteq K_v$. Therefore the quotient map $A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v$ factors through $A/K_w$, yielding a surjection
\[
Q_w=A/K_w\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v=Q_v.
\]
For finite groups, $K_w\subseteq K_v$ implies $|K_w|\le |K_v|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[A strict drop under refinement]\label{ex:refinement-drop}
Let $A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, and let $r$ be admissible at $q\le p$.
Assume that at $p$ there is one global component section $v$ and a component obstruction class
\[
\omega_v\in H^2(N(\mathcal U_p),A)
\]
with
\[
K_v=\langle 2\rangle\subseteq A.
\]
Hence
\[
Q_v=A/K_v\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
\]

Suppose $r$ has a unique component section $w$ above $v$ at the refinement $q$, and the induced pullback class
\[
\omega_w=f_{q,p}^*(\omega_v)
\]
is trivial in $H^2(N(\mathcal U_q),A)$. Then
\[
K_w=\{0\},\qquad Q_w=A/K_w\cong A.
\]
By \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, the map
\[
Q_w\longrightarrow Q_v
\]
is the quotient mod~$2$, so $|K_w|<|K_v|$ and the logarithmic fibre cardinality decreases strictly under this refinement.
\end{example}

\begin{corollary}[Refinement decreases presentation-relative logarithmic fibre cardinality]\label{cor:branch-budget-monotonicity}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, refinement can only enlarge the quotient and can never increase the presentation-relative minimum auxiliary register size of the componentwise quotient map:
\[
\log_2|K_w|\le \log_2|K_v|.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the last clause of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity} rewritten on a logarithmic scale.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Readout-preserving rewrites}

\begin{definition}[Readout-preserving rewrite]\label{def:value-preserving-rewrite}
A \emph{readout expression} is any term whose semantic role at a state is determined by a typed readout. A rewrite
\[
E\leadsto E'
\]
between readout expressions is \emph{value preserving} if for every state $p$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\Read_p(E)$ is defined if and only if $\Read_p(E')$ is defined,
\item whenever defined, $\Read_p(E)=\Read_p(E')$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Readout-preserving rewrites do not create facts]\label{prop:value-preserving-no-creation}
If $E\leadsto E'$ is value preserving and
\[
\Read_p(E')=v
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
v\neq \Indet,
\]
then
\[
\Read_p(E)=v.
\]
In particular, a readout-preserving rewrite cannot turn an inadmissible or non-unique-or-absent expression into a genuinely new value claim.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:value-preserving-rewrite}, definedness is preserved in both directions, and whenever the readouts are defined they agree. Hence the determined readout of $E'$ gives the same determined readout for $E$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalization does not create facts]\label{cor:normalization-no-fact-creation}
Let
\[
E=E_0\leadsto E_1\leadsto\cdots\leadsto E_n=E'
\]
be a finite sequence of readout-preserving rewrites. If $\Read_p(E')=v\neq \Indet$, then $\Read_p(E)=v$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{prop:value-preserving-no-creation} inductively along the rewrite sequence.
\end{proof}

\section{A split GHZ/Mermin banded groupoid lift}\label{sec:appendix-ghz}

The GHZ/Mermin model provides a convenient illustration of the split lift in
\artresult{Canonical split stack and the degree obstruction}. The role of this section is
correspondingly limited: it records chosen representatives for that split
lift, not a constructed non-split finite-nerve GHZ example. In particular, it
does not supply a canonical finite nerve, a normalized $2$-cocycle, a
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison map, or a nonzero value of $K_\omega$ for GHZ.

Let $e_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model obtained from the GHZ state \cite{GreenbergerHorneZeilinger1989,Mermin1990,AbramskyBrandenburger2011}, situated in the Kochen--Specker tradition \cite{KochenSpecker1967}. Related topological and cohomological treatments of contextuality include \cite{OkayRaussendorf2016,OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017,OkayTyhurstRaussendorf2018,Aasnaess2022}. The measurement cover consists of the four contexts
\[
C_{XXX},\ C_{XYY},\ C_{YXY},\ C_{YYX},
\]
where, for instance, $C_{XYY}$ records the joint measurement in which the first observer measures $X$ and the other two measure $Y$. Each context carries outcomes in $\{\pm 1\}^3$, and the GHZ support presheaf $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ selects exactly the assignments whose parity matches the GHZ constraints: $+1$ on $XXX$ and $-1$ on the three $XYY$-type contexts.

\begin{definition}[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf]\label{def:amplitude-lift}
Let $S_e$ be the support presheaf of a finite empirical model on a measurement-cover site $\mathcal C_a$. An \emph{banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf} of $S_e$ with band $\Band$ is a banded groupoid lift
\[
\mathfrak P_e\to \mathcal C_a
\]
together with an identification
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_e)\cong S_e.
\]
Equivalently, such a lift is a choice of lift objects and transition
isomorphisms whose isomorphism classes recover the supported local assignments.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Support data versus a non-split banded groupoid lift]\label{rem:amplitude-lift-choice}
The support presheaf canonically determines the split lift of
\artresult{Canonical split stack and the degree obstruction}, but that lift has only neutral
component gerbes. It does not determine a non-split banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf, a
nonzero component obstruction class, or a nonzero value of $K_\omega$. Such claims
for empirical support presheaves are therefore relative to additional lift
data.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Chosen GHZ phase-line lift]\label{lem:ghz-prestack}
Let $a=[r]_p$ be the GHZ base object and $\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. Fix, for each object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and each supported local assignment $s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$, a one-dimensional complex line $L_{U,s}$ generated by a chosen local GHZ amplitude, together with restriction isomorphisms compatible with restriction of assignments. Let $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$ be the groupoid whose objects are the pairs
\[
(s,L_{U,s}),
\qquad
s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U),
\]
and whose automorphisms are the signs $\{\pm 1\}\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ acting on the chosen line. Then $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}\to\mathcal C_a$ is a banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ with band $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Its stackification is bandedly equivalent to
\[
\operatorname{Disc}(aS_{\mathrm{GHZ}})
\times\mathsf B(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z),
\]
so every component gerbe is neutral.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By construction, restriction along $V\to U$ sends $(s,L_{U,s})$ to the restricted supported assignment together with the chosen restricted line, so the fibres form a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C_a$. The automorphism sheaf of every object is the constant sheaf $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, acting by sign changes on the one-dimensional line. Forgetting the line remembers only the supported assignment, and two objects are isomorphic exactly when they have the same supported assignment. Hence
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})\cong S_{\mathrm{GHZ}},
\]
so \Cref{def:amplitude-lift} is satisfied.
The compatible choice of one line for every supported assignment gives an
equivalence with the split prestack having those assignments as components
and $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ as each automorphism sheaf. Stackification
therefore gives the displayed split stack, whose identity torsor supplies a
global object in each component.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Limit of the chosen GHZ/Mermin lift]\label{thm:ghz-lift-limit}
Let $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the GHZ support presheaf, and fix the chosen banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ of \Cref{lem:ghz-prestack}. Suppose, in addition, that one has chosen a stackification
\[
\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}}:=a(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})
\]
and a cofinal family of covers
\[
\Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)
\]
such that the terminal-fibre essential-surjectivity and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison clauses of \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-banded-lift} hold for this chosen lift. Then
\[
(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}})
\]
is a gluing-sensitive banded lift datum for the chosen split GHZ banded
groupoid lift, but every Giraud class furnished by its component gerbes is zero. In
particular, it does not recover the nonzero relative degree-one classes of
\cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}, and it yields no nonzero value of
$K_\omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{lem:ghz-prestack} identifies the stackification as a split banded lift.
The additional assumptions are exactly the remaining clauses in
\Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-banded-lift}. The general theorems therefore
apply, but neutrality of every component gerbe forces all resulting Giraud
classes, homological evaluation maps, and homological image subgroups to vanish.
\end{proof}


 succeeded in 180ms:
\section{The finite-site interface}\label{sec:preliminaries}

The results use a site, a presheaf, and a banded prestack as input.  No
semantic construction of these data is assumed.  This section records the
small interface needed later and fixes the distinction between a matching
family and an amalgamation.

Let \(\mathcal C\) be a small site with pullbacks of covering families and
terminal object \(a\), and let
\[
 F:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\mathbf {Set}
\]
be a presheaf.  If \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\) is a cover, write
\(U_{ij}=U_i\times_aU_j\).  A \emph{strict matching family} on
\(\mathcal U\) is a family \(s_i\in F(U_i)\) satisfying
\[
 s_i|_{U_{ij}}=s_j|_{U_{ij}}
 \qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
It is an \emph{amalgamation} if there is \(s\in F(a)\) with
\(s|_{U_i}=s_i\) for every \(i\).  We use the abbreviations
\[
 \operatorname{Match}(F,a),\qquad
 \operatorname{Glob}(F,a),\qquad
 \operatorname{MWA}(F,a)
\]
for, respectively, existence of a strict matching family on some cover of
\(a\), nonemptiness of \(F(a)\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Match}(F,a)\ \text{and}\ F(a)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{MWA}\) means matching without amalgamation.  It is not
a claim about every matching family on every cover.

Write \(u:F\to aF\) for the sheafification unit.  We say that \(F\) is
\emph{separated on the slice over \(a\)} if, for every \(X\to a\), two
sections of \(F(X)\) which agree after restriction to a cover of \(X\) are
equal.  This stronger slice condition, rather than separatedness only at
\(a\), is used whenever equality in \(aF\) is returned to equality in
\(F\).

Let \(\mathscr A\) be an abelian sheaf on \(\mathcal C\).  An
\emph{\(\mathscr A\)-banded prestack lift of \(F\)} is a prestack in
groupoids \(\mathfrak P\) with a fixed split cleavage, together with
compatible identifications
\[
 \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)\cong F,
 \qquad
 \underline{\operatorname{Aut}}_{\mathfrak P}(x)cong\mathscr A
\]
on every slice on which \(x\) is defined.  Let
\[
 \iota:\mathfrak P\longrightarrow\mathfrak L:=a(\mathfrak P)
\]
be stackification.  Standard compatibility of stackification with connected
components gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stackification-components-core}
 \pi_0(\mathfrak L)\cong aF,
\end{equation}
and the map induced by \(\iota\) on components is the sheafification unit.
We say that \(\iota\) is \emph{terminally essentially surjective} if
\(\mathfrak P(a)\to\mathfrak L(a)\) is essentially surjective.

The lift is \emph{representative-rigid} if there are maps
\[
 s_X:F(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ob}(\mathfrak P(X))
\]
selecting a representative of every component and satisfying, for every
\(f:Y\to X\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-representative-pullback}
 f^*s_X(t)=s_Y(f^*t)
\end{equation}
as a literal equality.  The equality is taken with respect to the fixed
split cleavage.  Ordinary choices of cartesian lifts are generally only
pseudofunctorial; the strictness in
\eqref{eq:strict-representative-pullback} is therefore a substantive extra
hypothesis, not a harmless choice of notation.  Split cleavages and their
relation to pseudofunctorial pullback are standard for fibred categories
\cite[Chap.~VI]{MacLaneMoerdijk1994}.

\begin{proposition}[Presheaf and prestack interface]
\label{prop:finite-site-semantic-interface}
With the notation above:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item a strict matching family determines a section of \((aF)(a)\); if
      \(F\) is separated on the slice over \(a\), every section of
      \((aF)(a)\) is represented by a strict matching family on a cover of
      \(a\).  Hence, under this separatedness hypothesis,
      \[
      \operatorname{Match}(F,a)
      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
      (aF)(a)\ne\varnothing;
      \]
\item \(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\).
      If \(\iota\) is terminally essentially surjective, these are also
      equivalent to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\);
\item under separatedness on the slice and terminal essential surjectivity,
      \(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\) holds exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is
      nonempty and \(\mathfrak L(a)\) is empty.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Applying \(u\) to a strict matching family gives a matching family in the
sheaf \(aF\), which has a unique amalgamation in \((aF)(a)\).  Conversely,
let \(\xi\in(aF)(a)\).  The plus--plus description of sheafification gives
a cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\) and sections \(s_i\in F(U_i)\) representing
\(\xi|_{U_i}\), with the following local equality on each overlap: there is
a cover \(\{V_{ijk}\to U_{ij}\}_k\) such that
\[
 s_i|_{V_{ijk}}=s_j|_{V_{ijk}}.
\]
Every \(U_{ij}\to a\) is an object of the slice.  Separatedness there turns
these locally witnessed equalities into
\(s_i|_{U_{ij}}=s_j|_{U_{ij}}\).  The \(s_i\) therefore form a strict
matching family.  This proves (i).

The isomorphism \(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong F(a)\) proves
the first equivalence in (ii).  The forward implication from
\(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\) is
given by \(\iota\), and the converse is terminal essential surjectivity.
Finally, (iii) is obtained by combining (i), (ii), and the definition of
\(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\).
\end{proof}

The article treats \((\mathcal C,F,\mathfrak P,\mathscr A)\) as supplied
finite-site lift data.  In particular, the realization theorem below is not
derived from a lower team-semantic model.  A narrow lower-language separation
example and the presentation bookkeeping removed from the core argument are
given in the technical appendix
\cite[Appendix~B]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} only as context; they
do not generate the lift.

\section{Homological images and aggregate quotients}
\label{sec:homological-images}

Fix a finite simplicial complex \(N\), a finite abelian group \(A\), and a
class \(\omega\in H^2(N,A)\).  The universal coefficient map is denoted by
\[
 \operatorname{ev}_\omega:
 H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow A.
\]
Define its \emph{homological image} and \emph{homological cokernel} by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:homological-image-cokernel}
 K_\omega:=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega),
 \qquad Q_\omega:=A/K_\omega.
\end{equation}
These definitions depend on the supplied finite presentation of the component
gerbe.  Refinement and retrivialization transport them by UCT naturality, but
no canonical identification along distinct comparison zigzags is asserted.
The resulting freely generated presentation groupoid and its elementary
naturality calculation are recorded in the technical appendix rather than
promoted to an invariance theorem.

For a finite family of component classes
\((\omega_v)_{v\in V}\), put \(K_v=K_{\omega_v}\) and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-quotients}
 Q_{\mathrm{lab}}:=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v,
 \qquad
 Q_{\mathrm{com}}:=A\Big/\sum_{v\in V}K_v.
\end{equation}
The first quotient retains enough information to map to every componentwise
quotient \(A/K_v\).  The second retains only characters which descend through
every one of them.

\begin{proposition}[UCT and aggregate subgroup package]
\label{prop:uct-aggregate-package}
With the notation above:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item The universal coefficient sequence is
      \[
      0\longrightarrow
      \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)
      \longrightarrow H^2(N,A)
      \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}
      \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A)
      \longrightarrow0.
      \]
      Thus \(K_\omega=0\) exactly when \(\omega\) lies in the displayed
      Ext subgroup.  In particular, nonzero classes can have zero
      homological image when \(H_1\) has torsion.
\item The quotient map \(q_\omega:A\to Q_\omega\) is initial among group
      homomorphisms \(q:A\to B\) satisfying
      \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\).  A character
      \(\chi:A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) factors through \(Q_\omega\)
      exactly when \(\chi(K_\omega)=0\).  Since finite Pontryagin duality
      separates points,
      \[
      K_\omega=\mathop{\bigcap}_{\chi(K_\omega)=0}\ker\chi.
      \]
\item For a nonempty finite family \((K_v)_{v\in V}\), there is a natural
      short exact sequence
      \begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}
      0\longrightarrow
      \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}
      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}
      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}
      \longrightarrow0.
      \end{equation}
      Moreover,
      \[
      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}}
      \cong\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v^\perp,
      \qquad
      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}}
      \cong\sum_{v\in V}K_v^\perp
      \]
      inside \(\widehat A\).
\item If \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), a subgroup
      \(K\le A\) occurs as \(K_\omega\) exactly when \(d(K)\le\beta\).
      Every finite family of such subgroups is simultaneously attained by
      the prestack of
      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Clause (i) is the cohomological universal coefficient theorem, natural in
both \(N\) and \(A\) \cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}.  Its middle-to-right map
evaluates a cohomology class on integral \(2\)-cycles, so its value at
\(\omega\) is \(\operatorname{ev}_\omega\).  Exactness identifies the
kernel with the Ext term.

For (ii), \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\) says precisely that \(q\)
vanishes on \(K_\omega\).  The universal property of the quotient gives a
unique factorization through \(A/K_\omega\).  Apply the same observation to
characters.  The intersection formula follows because characters of a
finite abelian group separate points \cite{Terras1999}.

The containment \(\bigcap_vK_v\subseteq\sum_vK_v\) gives the quotient map in
\eqref{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}.  Its kernel is
\((\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)\) by the third isomorphism theorem, proving
exactness.  For finite abelian groups, annihilators exchange sums and
intersections:
\[
 \Big(\sum_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\bigcap_vK_v^\perp,
 \qquad
 \Big(\bigcap_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\sum_vK_v^\perp.
\]
Dualizing the two quotients proves the character formulas in (iii).

Under the hypotheses of (iv), the Ext term vanishes and UCT becomes
\[
 H^2(N,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z^\beta,A).
\]
The image of a homomorphism from \(\mathbb Z^\beta\) is generated by the
images of the standard basis, so it has at most \(\beta\) generators.
Conversely, given generators \(k_1,\dots,k_\beta\) of \(K\), allowing zeros
when fewer are needed, the map
\[
 (n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto\sum_jn_jk_j
\]
has image \(K\).  Applying
\Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction} to a family of these maps
gives simultaneous realization.
\end{proof}

All clauses except simultaneous prestack realization are standard formal
consequences of UCT, finite duality, and subgroup arithmetic.  In particular,
there is no separate information-theoretic theorem hidden in the fibres of
these quotients.  Since a quotient fibre is a coset of its kernel, the minimum
cardinality of an unrestricted auxiliary set capable of separating every
fibre is simply the kernel cardinality.  For example,
\[
 |q_\omega^{-1}(\bar a)|=|K_\omega|,
 \qquad
 \left|\ker(Q_{\mathrm{lab}}\to Q_{\mathrm{com}})\right|
 =\left|\frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}\right|.
\]

The Ext clause also marks a limitation of the homological image.  If
\(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
\(\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)\ne0\), a nonzero gerbe class can
have \(K_\omega=0\) and \(Q_\omega=A\).  For instance, an
\(\mathbb RP^2\)-type nerve and suitable \(2\)-torsion coefficients exhibit
this behavior.  Conversely, when \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)\) is free, the Ext term
vanishes and zero evaluation forces \(\omega=0\).  These are UCT boundary
cases, not additional classification results.


 succeeded in 180ms:
The Editors
Annals of Pure and Applied Logic

Dear Editors,

We submit for your consideration the manuscript "Gluing Obstructions
and Homological Visibility in a State-Forcing Semantics."  The paper
addresses the following question: given a presheaf carrying a finite
abelian gluing obstruction, what part of that obstruction is
semantically visible -- that is, detectable by admissible characters --
without enlarging the state space?

The answer is developed within a four-layer conservative extension
chain that stratifies the passage from pointwise semantics through
information-state forcing to local objects and refinement dynamics.
Each layer strictly extends the one below and preserves the forcing
behavior of all formulas already expressible at lower layers.  The
first main result (Theorem A) is a forcing-necessity separation
theorem: compatible local sectionability and gluing-level absence are
undefinable in the information-state forcing language, so the
local-object enrichment is logically necessary.  The second result
(Theorem B) establishes a branched gerbe semantics in which each
visible value class determines a banded component gerbe, and
gluing-level absence holds exactly when every component gerbe is
non-neutral.  The third result (Theorem C) applies the universal
coefficient theorem to define the intrinsic visible quotient as the
cokernel of a homological evaluation map; the blind residual -- the
part of the obstruction invisible to every admissible character -- is a
pure Ext-type class.  The paper also proves the exact limit of comparison
with finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models: their support
presheaves canonically and refinement-functorially determine a split
realization stack, but all of its Giraud classes vanish.  The
Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative degree-one
torsor class, so a non-split banded lift is genuinely additional data.

APAL is our preferred venue because the paper draws on several
traditions that the journal has helped develop.  The conservative
extension chain builds on Kripke's semantics for intuitionistic logic,
Beth's semantic tableaux, and Fitting's model-theoretic forcing.  The
gerbe-theoretic layer applies the Giraud classification in a
site-specific way that connects to the topos-theoretic forcing of
Tierney and Johnstone; we discuss the relationship explicitly in the
conclusion, including the open question of whether the four-layer chain
admits a topos-internal reformulation via Lawvere--Tierney topologies.
The combination of Heyting-valued forcing separation with homological
algebra over finite Cech nerves lies squarely within the journal's
scope in categorical logic and sheaf-theoretic methods.

The manuscript is 92 pages in amsart format, contains
38 references, and is self-contained: all definitions, hypotheses, and
proofs are given in full.  No external data or computational
verification is required.  Results on multi-observer extensions are
deferred to a sequel and are not needed for the present paper.

Thank you for considering this submission.

Sincerely,
The Authors

+\begin{corollary}[Two-component realization on a wedge of \(2\)-spheres]

+\begin{proposition}[Standard component-gerbe package]

-\begin{proof}

-\[
-\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
-\]
-Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
-\[
-\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
-=
-\Phi(c_{ijk}),
-\]
-which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
-
-The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
-\[
-(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
-\]
-is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
+The classification of abelian-banded gerbes identifies equivalence classes
+with \(H^2\), with the neutral gerbes representing zero
+\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}.  On a site with terminal object \(a\), neutrality
+is exactly existence of an object over \(a\), proving (ii).  For (iii), the
+component compatibility makes \(\Phi\) restrict to the full component
+substacks.  Applying \(\Phi\) to local objects and overlap arrows applies
+\(\theta\) to their triple-overlap defect cocycle.  This is the standard
+naturality of Giraud classification under a banded equivalence
+\cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
 \end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}

+\begin{theorem}[Terminal rigidity for representative-rigid lifts]
+\label{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}

+representative-rigid \(\mathscr A\)-banded prestack lift of \(F\).  Write

-\[

-\[

-defines a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle $c=(c_{ijk})\in \check Z^2(\mathcal U,\Band)$;

-\begin{lemma}[\v{C}ech calculus for component gerbes]\label{lem:cech-branch-gerbe-calculus}

-\begin{definition}[Presentation-comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
-For finite nerve representatives of a fixed component obstruction class, an
-\emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
-\Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
-cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
-The \emph{presentation-comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
-objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
-morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
-presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
-component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
-zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
-between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
-hypothesis is imposed.
-\end{definition}

+Connectedness and the coherent trivializations identify that section group

-\begin{remark}[Necessity of homology equivalences and chosen paths]\label{rem:homology-equality}

 \[

+Acyclicity makes every row with \(q>0\) vanish, so the edge map is an

+For (iii), open stars in successive barycentric subdivisions have arbitrarily
+small mesh.  Given \(x\in O\) with \(O\subseteq X\) open, a sufficiently
+fine subdivision has a vertex whose open star contains \(x\) and lies in
+\(O\).  Hence the union of all these stars is a basis.  Adding their finite
+intersections makes it stable under intersections, and a family of basis

-Then, for every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $q_*(\omega)=0$ in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)$;
-\item $q$ factors uniquely through
-\[
-\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\omega}.
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-Hence, when $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, the homological cokernel is initial among coefficient quotients that annihilate the obstruction class itself.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)=0
-\]
-for every abelian group $B$. Thus, in the criterion of \Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}, the zero-evaluation condition is equivalent to $q_*(\omega)=0$, and the conclusion follows.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{remark}[Presentation-relative invariance without a canonical splitting]\label{rem:no-canonical-splitting}
-For a fixed finite nerve representative, the quotient
-$Q_{\omega}$ and the subgroup
-$K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$ are invariants of the chosen
-presentation. Across comparison-equivalent presentations they are transported
-functorially only along chosen morphisms in the presentation-comparison
-groupoid, as in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}; different zigzags
-with the same endpoints may carry different coefficient automorphisms. By
-contrast, the universal coefficient sequence need not split canonically. Thus
-the theory isolates a homological cokernel and homological image subgroup
-at each presentation, with comparison-zigzag functoriality, without requiring
-any noncanonical decomposition of $\omega$ into $H_2$-evaluated and UCT-Ext
-summands.
-\end{remark}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Comparison with cocycle-coordinate quotients]\label{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}
-Let $\alpha$ be any finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Then the homological cokernel
-\[
-Q_{\omega}
-\]
-admits a canonical surjective homomorphism onto the cocycle-coordinate quotient
-\[
-A/H_\alpha.
-\]
-Equivalently, every cocycle-coordinate quotient is a quotient of the homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $q:A\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha$ be the canonical quotient. By
-\suppresult{Cocycle-coordinate quotient}, the quotient kills every cocycle
-value $\alpha_{ijk}$ pointwise, so the pushed-forward cocycle representative
-is zero. Hence $q_*(\omega)=0$, and in particular it lies in the
-$\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup of $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A/H_\alpha)$. Apply
-\Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}
-Let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Write
-\[
-C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
-\]
-for the simplicial group of integral $2$-chains on the finite nerve. The \emph{chain-level evaluation map} of $\alpha$ is the homomorphism
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
-\]
-defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
-:=
-\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
-\]
-\end{definition}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Chain-coordinate versus homology-evaluation quotient]\label{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:chain-level-evaluation}, the following hold.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $2$-boundaries and therefore induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A.
-\]
-\item The induced homomorphism $\overline\alpha$ is exactly the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.
-\item The strict coordinate-image subgroup and the presentation-relative homological image subgroup satisfy
-\[
-H_\alpha=\mathrm{Im}(\widetilde\alpha),
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)).
-\]
+\item The universal coefficient sequence is
+      \[
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow H^2(N,A)
+      \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}
+      \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \]
+      Thus \(K_\omega=0\) exactly when \(\omega\) lies in the displayed
+      Ext subgroup.  In particular, nonzero classes can have zero
+      homological image when \(H_1\) has torsion.
+\item The quotient map \(q_\omega:A\to Q_\omega\) is initial among group
+      homomorphisms \(q:A\to B\) satisfying
+      \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\).  A character
+      \(\chi:A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) factors through \(Q_\omega\)
+      exactly when \(\chi(K_\omega)=0\).  Since finite Pontryagin duality
+      separates points,
+      \[
+      K_\omega=\mathop{\bigcap}_{\chi(K_\omega)=0}\ker\chi.
+      \]
+\item For a nonempty finite family \((K_v)_{v\in V}\), there is a natural
+      short exact sequence
+      \begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \end{equation}
+      Moreover,
+      \[
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}}
+      \cong\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v^\perp,
+      \qquad
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}}
+      \cong\sum_{v\in V}K_v^\perp
+      \]
+      inside \(\widehat A\).
+\item If \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
+      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), a subgroup
+      \(K\le A\) occurs as \(K_\omega\) exactly when \(d(K)\le\beta\).
+      Every finite family of such subgroups is simultaneously attained by
+      the prestack of
+      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}.
 \end{enumerate}
-Thus the gap between chain-coordinate quotient and homology-evaluation quotient is exactly the gap between the image of the cocycle on all $2$-chains and its image on $2$-cycles.
 \end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, then
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)=(\delta\alpha)(c)=0
-\]
-because $\alpha$ is a cocycle. Hence $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $B_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ and induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=Z_2/B_2\to A.
-\]
-This proves \textup{(i)}.
-
-For any $2$-cycle $z=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\in Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, set
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z):=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma)=\widetilde\alpha(z).
-\]
-If $z'$ is another $2$-cycle homologous to $z$, then $z-z'=\partial c$ for some $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$. By \textup{(i)},
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z)-\alpha^{\sharp}(z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(z-z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)
-=
-0.
-\]
-Therefore $\alpha^{\sharp}$ depends only on the homology class of $z$ and defines a homomorphism
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A,\qquad
-[z]\longmapsto \alpha^{\sharp}(z).
-\]
-By the definition of the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$, this homomorphism is exactly the image of the cohomology class $\omega=[\alpha]$ under
-\[
-\eta_A:H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\to \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A).
-\]
-Thus
-\[
-\overline\alpha([z])=\alpha^{\sharp}(z)=\eta_A(\omega)([z])=\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}([z])
-\]
-for every $[z]\in H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, proving \textup{(ii)}.
-
-For \textup{(iii)}, the image of $\widetilde\alpha$ is exactly the subgroup generated by the simplex values $\alpha_{ijk}$, hence it is $H_\alpha$ by \suppresult{Finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative}. The equality
-\[
-\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))
-\]
-is immediate from \textup{(i)}, and \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient} identifies this image with $K_{\omega}$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Coincidence of the chain-coordinate and homology-evaluation quotients]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-coincidence-criterion}
-Let $\alpha$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of $\omega$. The following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $A/H_\alpha\cong Q_{\omega}$;
-\item $H_\alpha=K_{\omega}$;
-\item $\widetilde\alpha(C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Equivalently, the chain-coordinate quotient agrees with the homology-evaluation quotient exactly when every value of the cocycle on a $2$-chain already occurs on a $2$-cycle.
-\end{corollary}
 
 \begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is immediate from the quotient descriptions
-\[
-A/H_\alpha
-\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}.
-\]
-The equivalence of \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} is exactly \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}(iii).
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{theorem}[Nonzero UCT-Ext classes and vanishing $H_2$ evaluation]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admissible
-parameter, global component section, banded groupoid lift, trivialized constant finite
-abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
-$\omega$ as a derived component class, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $Q_{\omega}=A$;
-\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-trivializing for that component class. If, in addition, the banded groupoid lift is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
-\]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
-\]
-so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. By the universal coefficient sequence, \textup{(iii)} holds exactly when $\omega\in\ker(\eta_A)$, and this kernel is the stated $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.
-
-If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
-On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies
-\[
-\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\]
-for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-trivializing.
-
-Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen global component section $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
-\]
-Suppose towards a contradiction that
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-By clause \textup{(i)} of \suppresult{Banded groupoid lift and stackification}, this yields an object of the terminal fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$, and its image under the stackification morphism
-\[
-\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
-\]
-defines an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Because there is only one global component section, every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in the unique component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v(a)$. Hence
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
-\]
-By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this implies that $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral, contradicting the non-neutrality already proved. Therefore
-\[
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-Combining this with $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ and admissibility of $r$, we obtain
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
-\]
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Vanishing evaluation when $H_2=0$]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}
-Assume
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
-\]
-Then, for every obstruction class $\omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$,
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A.
-\]
-Every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve therefore has zero $H_2$ evaluation, and every character is class-trivializing.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
-\[
-\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0,
-\]
-so $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ for every $\omega$. Apply \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[No nonzero classes with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation when $H_1$ is free]\label{cor:h1-free-no-blindness}
-Assume that $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian. Then
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\omega=0.
-\]
-Equivalently, every nonzero component obstruction class has nonzero $H_2$ evaluation. In particular, if $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve produces a proper homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0.
-\]
-Hence the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$ is injective. By \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0.
-\]
-Injectivity of $\eta_A$ therefore gives $K_{\omega}=0$ if and only if $\omega=0$. If $\omega\neq 0$, then $K_{\omega}\neq 0$, so $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ is a proper quotient of the finite group $A$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{example}[A nonzero class with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation on an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve]\label{ex:rp2-character-blind}
-This is a finite-nerve mechanism example.  Let $\mathcal U$ be a finite cover
-whose \v{C}ech nerve is a finite triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^2$, and take
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-H_2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)=0,
-\qquad
-H_1(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~2.2]{Hatcher2002}. The universal coefficient sequence therefore yields
-\[
-H^2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}. Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A,
-\]
-by \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}. Thus the homological cokernel is all of $A$, although the obstruction class is nonzero. Every character is therefore class-trivializing. If this is the unique global component section of the admissible parameter under consideration and \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, then \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} yields a matching family without global amalgamation whose component class is trivialized by every character.
-
-The last sentence is conditional on the usual banded-stack-lift data: an
-admissible parameter, a banded stack lift with constant band
-$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and the
-\textup{(H4)} comparison identifying the displayed finite-nerve class with the
-derived component class; the matching-without-amalgamation conclusion also requires
-separatedness on the slice site associated to the parameter.  The unconditional content of the example is the
-homological mechanism
-\[
-\omega\in \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A),
-\qquad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0,
-\]
-which makes the homological cokernel equal to $A$ although the
-obstruction class is nonzero.  Thus the example records the UCT
-$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel of the finite nerve, while the component-gerbe conclusion
-enters only after the admissible-parameter and banded-lift hypotheses have been
-supplied.
-\end{example}
-
-\begin{example}[A single-component surjective-homological-evaluation class on $S^2$]\label{ex:s2-single-branch-maximal-collapse}
-Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S^2\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite good cover of $S^2$, let $N:=N(\mathcal U)$ be its nerve, and let $\mathcal C_a$ be the corresponding slice site for one admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ with $a=[r]_p$. Take the constant band
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-on $\mathcal C_a$. Define the presheaf of local sections
-\[
-F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}:\mathcal C_a^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
-\]
-by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(U)=\{v\}
-\]
-for every nonempty proper finite intersection $U$ of members of $\mathcal U$, by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing,
-\]
-and by the identity map on every restriction between proper intersections. Then the cover
-\[
-\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
-\]
-supports the compatible family constantly equal to $v$, while there is no global section at $a$. Hence
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r),
-\qquad
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-The restricted presheaf is separated on the slice: over \(a\) there are no two
-sections to compare, and over every proper nonempty intersection there is
-only the section \(v\).
-Because
-\[
-H^2(N,A)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,
-\]
-choose a simplicial cocycle
-\[
-\alpha\in Z^2(N,A)
-\]
-representing the nonzero class. For each $U_i$ choose a local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$, and choose isomorphisms
-\[
-\phi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim} x_j|_{U_{ij}}
-\]
-on the pairwise overlaps such that
-\[
-\phi_{ik}^{-1}\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}=\alpha_{ijk}\in A
-\]
-on each triple overlap. This is the single-label instance of the
-cocycle-to-prestack construction isolated in
-\suppresult{$2$-cocycle-defined banded prestack for one component}, used under the same generated-subsite
-admissibility convention as \suppresult{Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion};
-equivalently, it is the standard local-trivialization construction for gerbes
-\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Sec.~5]{Breen2006}, \cite{Murray1996}. It
-yields a prestack presentation $\mathfrak P_r$ on $\mathcal C_a$ with the following properties:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item over each member $U_i$ of the cover there is the chosen local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$;
-\item the chosen transition maps have triple-overlap defect exactly $\alpha$;
-\item the presheaf of isomorphism classes satisfies
-\[
- \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus the example begins with an explicit presheaf of local sections and then chooses local lift objects and transition data whose component presheaf is the given functor; the component gerbe is recovered from those data by stackification rather than being taken as primitive input.
-
-Let
-\[
-\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r).
-\]
-Because $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$, the sheaf of connected components of $\mathfrak L_r$ has exactly one global section at $a$, represented by the constant compatible family above. Therefore
-\[
-\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}.
-\]
-But $\alpha$ is nonzero, so the descent datum is ineffective and no object exists over $a$ in the resulting stack; equivalently, the unique component gerbe is non-neutral. Hence
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
-\qquad
-\omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
-\]
-Combining this with the already computed presheaf-level facts gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
-\qquad
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r),
-\qquad
-\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\},
-\qquad
-\mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
-\qquad
-\omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
-\]
-The good cover $\mathcal U$ trivializes the constant band, all finite intersections are contractible, and therefore the $H^1$-vanishing and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction,def:finite-nerve-presentation} are satisfied.
-
-Since
-\[
-H_1(N,\mathbb Z) = 0,
-\qquad
-H_2(N,\mathbb Z) \cong \mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Secs.~2.1, 2.2]{Hatcher2002}, the universal coefficient theorem gives
-\[
-H^2(N, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
-\cong
-\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
-\cong
-\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}.
-\]
-Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class, and let $[S^2]$ denote the fundamental class in $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)$. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_\omega([S^2]) = 1 \in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
-\]
-so the homological evaluation map is surjective. By \Cref{cor:maximal-collapse},
-\[
-K_\omega = A = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
-\qquad
-Q_\omega = 0.
-\]
-Hence
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
-\qquad
-\omega=\omega_v\neq 0,
-\qquad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\twoheadrightarrow A,
-\qquad
-K_\omega=A,
-\qquad
-Q_\omega=0.
-\]
-Since $K_\omega = A$, \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} gives
-\[
-X_\omega = \mathrm{Ann}(K_\omega) = \mathrm{Ann}(A) = \{1\},
-\]
-so only the trivial character is class-trivializing. Equivalently, $Q_\omega = A/K_\omega = 0$.
-
-This example therefore verifies the full downstream hypothesis chain
-\[
-(\mathcal C_a,\mathfrak P_r,A,\omega,\mathrm{ev}_\omega,K_\omega,Q_\omega)
-\]
-inside a concrete site-theoretic example, once the banded stack lift has been fixed by the chosen cocycle data. It is the opposite extreme from the zero-evaluation case of \Cref{ex:rp2-character-blind}: for an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=0$, every character is class-trivializing, and the obstruction is entirely in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel with $Q_\omega=A$; for the present $S^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=A$, only the trivial character is class-trivializing, and the obstruction is entirely detected on $H_2$, with $Q_\omega=0$.
-\end{example}
-
-\begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the homological quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
-An \emph{auxiliary register for the homological quotient} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
-\[
-\iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow Q_{\omega}\times R
-\]
-such that
-\[
-\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
-\]
-\end{definition}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Fibre size of the homological quotient]\label{cor:intrinsic-hidden-state-lower-bound}
-Every auxiliary register for the homological quotient satisfies
-\[
-|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|.
-\]
-Equivalently,
-\[
-\log_2|R|\ge \log_2|K_{\omega}|.
-\]
-This lower bound is sharp.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, the fibres of $\pi_{\omega}$ are exactly the cosets of $K_{\omega}$, so every fibre has cardinality $|K_{\omega}|$. The same fibre-counting argument as in \suppresult{Fibre size of an auxiliary register} therefore shows that any auxiliary register preserving the first projection must satisfy $|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|$.
-
-For sharpness, take $R:=K_{\omega}$ and choose a set-theoretic section $s_{\omega}:Q_{\omega}\to A$ of $\pi_{\omega}$. Then
-\[
-\iota_{\omega}(x):=\bigl(\pi_{\omega}(x),x-s_{\omega}(\pi_{\omega}(x))\bigr)
-\]
-is injective.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of the homological quotient and fibre size]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}
-Write the finite abelian group $A$ as a direct sum of its $p$-primary components:
-\[
-A=\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}.
-\]
-Let $\omega_p\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A_{(p)})$ be the image of $\omega$ under the projection onto the $p$-primary summand. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p},
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}\cong \bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p},
-\]
-where
-\[
-K_{\omega,p}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p}).
-\]
-Consequently,
-\[

+A stack in groupoids has a sheaf of connected components.  A global section
+of that sheaf need not be represented by a global object of the stack, but it
+does select a maximal subgerbe.  This is Giraud's component-gerbe construction
+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  The component is represented by a
+global object precisely when its gerbe is neutral, or equivalently when its
+Giraud \(H^2\)-class vanishes.  These classical facts are the starting point
+of the article.
+
+Our setting is deliberately finite and presentation-relative.  We fix a site
+with terminal object, a presheaf \(F\), an abelian-banded prestack lift
+\(\mathfrak P\), and its stackification \(\mathfrak L\).  The connected
+components of \(\mathfrak P\) recover \(F\), while those of
+\(\mathfrak L\) recover the sheafification \(aF\).  If \(F\) is separated on
+the terminal slice and stackification is essentially surjective on the
+terminal fibre, a strict matching family without an amalgamation occurs
+exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is nonempty and every component gerbe selected by a
+section of \((aF)(a)\) is non-neutral.  This is a comparison between a strict
+presheaf predicate and standard gerbe theory, not a new classification of
+gerbes.
+

+strong kind of prestack presentation.  Suppose one selects a representative

+\subsection*{Organization}
 
-\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2em,labelindent=0pt]
-\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
-A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
-\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
-$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
-$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
-\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
-The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
-satisfaction.
-\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
-An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
-the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
-is not part of the definition.
-\item[Typed expansion class.]
-The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
-fixed lower model.
-\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
-An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
-exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
-are attached to $r$.
-\item[{Base object $a=[r]_p$.}]
-The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
-the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
-\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
-The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
-specified pretopology and pullbacks.
-\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
-The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
-\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
-A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
-\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
-A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
-terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
-hypothesis.
-\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
-A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
-strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
-\item[Global component section $v$.]
-An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
-$(aF)(a)$.
-\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
-The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
-$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
-\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
-The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
-replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
-zigzags need not give the same comparison.
-\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
-For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
-and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
-\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
-$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
-$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
-\item[Label-aware quotient.]
-$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
-componentwise homological cokernels.
-\item[Common-character quotient.]
-$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
-\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
-The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
-common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
-\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
-A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
-cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
-\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
-The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
-the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
-\item[Typed readout.]
-The partial output attached to an admissible parameter: inadmissible if no
-typed data are attached, uniquely determined if the sheafified global section
-is unique, and non-unique-or-absent otherwise.
-\item[Indexed refinement system.]
-A family of state-refinement relations indexed by information coordinates,
-each monotone for the state preorder and the specified time order.
-\item[Information-determining axis set.]
-A finite set of refinement coordinates whose information values determine any
-decided truth value among the states reachable along those coordinates.
-\item[Pairwise commuting refinements and common refinement.]
-Refinements for which every indicated finite family has a state refining all
-its members.
-\item[Readout-preserving rewrite.]
-A rewrite between partial outputs that preserves both definedness and value.
-\item[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf.]
-A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is the
-given empirical-model support presheaf and whose automorphism sheaves are the
-specified band.
-\end{description}
+Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the minimal presheaf and prestack
+interface.  Section~\ref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} records the standard Giraud
+component package, proves the comparison criterion, and gives the full
+terminal-rigidity proof.  Section~\ref{sec:homological-visibility} proves the
+connected-overlap, basis-site, and derived comparisons before constructing
+the prescribed finite-label prestack.  Section~\ref{sec:homological-images}

-For $\mathbb L_1\preceq\mathbb L_2$, the displayed clauses fix the object language of the expansion: $\Sigma_2$ is the disjoint expansion of $\Sigma_1$ by the local-section and site symbols listed in \textup{(ii)}, $\Mod_2$ is the class of $\Sigma_2$-expansions whose $\Sigma_1$-reduct is obtained by $U_{2,1}$, and $\pi^M_{2,1}$ is the identity on the underlying information state.
