-\[
-U_{i+1,i}(M_{i+1})=M_i,
-\]
-and, with the state projection forgetting only the newly added layer
-coordinates, preserves satisfaction of every $\mathbb L_i$-formula:
-\[
-M_{i+1},p\Vdash_{i+1}\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-M_i,\pi^{M_{i+1}}_{i+1,i}(p)\Vdash_i\varphi
-\qquad(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_i).
-\]
-Thus arbitrary finite pullback subsites, arbitrary presheaves of local sections on
-those subsites, and arbitrary supplied banded prestack or banded stack-lift data
-are admissible only in the typed expansion class defined by this proposition,
-once they satisfy the displayed typing and theorem-level hypotheses. This is a
-model-class convention for the expanded layers, not a semantic existence or
-closure theorem for an independently restricted class of models. The construction
-theorems below therefore have two parts: an algebraic construction of typed
-site, presheaf, prestack, stackification, and cohomology data, followed by the
-typed-expansion step which declares those well-typed data to be an
-\(\mathbb L_{i+1}\)-model without changing lower-layer satisfaction.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By the expansion convention just fixed, $\Mod_{i+1}$ is exactly the class of
-$\Sigma_{i+1}$-expansions of admissible $\Sigma_i$-models by the corresponding
-well-typed layer data.  The hypotheses on $D_{i+1}$ therefore put
-$M_i[D_{i+1}]$ in $\Mod_{i+1}$ and make its reduct under $U_{i+1,i}$ equal to
-$M_i$.  The state projection is the projection specified for the adjacent
-layer boundary and forgets only the new layer coordinates.  Since lower atomic
-satisfaction clauses are assumed to be interpreted through the reduct, all
-hypotheses of \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} hold for the adjacent pair
-$\mathbb L_i\preceq\mathbb L_{i+1}$.  Applying that lemma gives the displayed
-satisfaction equivalence for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_i$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Concrete instantiation of the finite chain]\label{prop:chain-instantiation}
-The chain
-\[
-\mathbb L_0\xhookrightarrow{\iota} \mathbb L_1\preceq \mathbb L_2\preceq \mathbb L_3\preceq \mathbb L_4
-\]
-is instantiated as follows.
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=3em]
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb L_1$ (pointwise states to information states: singleton-state embedding).}
-The language embedding
-\[
-e_{0,1}:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow \Sigma_1
-\]
-is the inclusion of the underlying many-sorted symbols. In addition, $\Sigma_1$ contains the parameter sorts $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ (one for each designated sort $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$) together with their equality; no geometric predicates or site structure is imposed at this step. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{1,0}:\Mod_1\to\Mod_0
-\]
-forgets the information-state presentation and the reference carrier sets, remembering only the underlying many-sorted structure of $\Sigma_0$. A pointwise state $\rho$ in $\mathbb L_0$ is represented inside $\mathbb L_1$ by the singleton information state
-\[
-\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho):=(\Gamma,\{\rho\}).
-\]
-By \Cref{prop:singleton-conservativity},
-\[
-M,\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{1,0}(M),\rho\Vdash_0\varphi
-\]
-for every $\mathbb L_0$-formula $\varphi$. This is a singleton-state embedding in the sense of \Cref{def:singleton-semantic-embedding}: it preserves satisfaction of $\mathbb L_0$-formulas on the canonical singleton image but does not provide a state projection from arbitrary $\mathbb L_1$-states back to $\mathbb L_0$-states.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_1\leadsto\mathbb L_2$ (information states to presheaves of local sections).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{1,2}:\Sigma_1\hookrightarrow \Sigma_2
-\]
-adjoins the admissibility predicates, the local-section predicates $\LocSec_s$, $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, the site-structure symbols (covers, refinement preorder, pullbacks), and the associated geometric notation. The parameter sorts $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and their equality are already present in $\Sigma_1$; the step from $\mathbb L_1$ to $\mathbb L_2$ equips admissible parameters with the geometric structure needed to state local-to-global questions. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{2,1}:\Mod_2\to\Mod_1
-\]
-forgets the reference-refinement sites, covers, and presheaves of local sections but retains the parameter sorts and their carrier sets. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{2,1}:\St_2(M)\to \St_1(U_{2,1}(M))
-\]
-is the identity on the underlying information state $(\Gamma_p,R_p)$. Since the satisfaction clauses for formulas already in $\mathrm{Form}_1$ never inspect the added presheaf data, one has
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_2\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{2,1}(M),\pi^M_{2,1}(p)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_1$.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_2\leadsto\mathbb L_3$ (presheaves to obstruction data).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{2,3}:\Sigma_2\hookrightarrow \Sigma_3
-\]
-adjoins the predicates and symbols used to talk about structural absence, global component sections, component gerbes, and obstruction classes. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{3,2}:\Mod_3\to\Mod_2
-\]
-drops the banded groupoid lift, band, component-gerbe, and obstruction data. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{3,2}:\St_3(M)\to \St_2(U_{3,2}(M))
-\]
-again leaves the underlying state unchanged. Formulas from $\mathrm{Form}_2$ are evaluated exactly as before, so
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_3\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{3,2}(M),\pi^M_{3,2}(p)\Vdash_2\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_2$.
-
-\item \textbf{$\mathbb L_3\leadsto\mathbb L_4$ (obstruction data to refinement dynamics).}
-The embedding
-\[
-e_{3,4}:\Sigma_3\hookrightarrow \Sigma_4
-\]
-adjoins the update relations, axis indices, support notions, and rewrite language of the refinement layer. The forgetful functor
-\[
-U_{4,3}:\Mod_4\to\Mod_3
-\]
-forgets the dynamic axes, update structure, and rewrite operations. The state projection
-\[
-\pi^M_{4,3}:\St_4(M)\to \St_3(U_{4,3}(M))
-\]
-forgets only the new dynamic bookkeeping. Because the satisfaction clauses for $\mathrm{Form}_3$ do not depend on that added bookkeeping, one has
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_4\varphi
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-U_{4,3}(M),\pi^M_{4,3}(p)\Vdash_3\varphi
-\]
-for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_3$.
+\item a strict matching family determines a section of \((aF)(a)\); if
+      \(F\) is separated on the slice over \(a\), every section of
+      \((aF)(a)\) is represented by a strict matching family on a cover of
+      \(a\).  Hence, under this separatedness hypothesis,
+      \[
+      \operatorname{Match}(F,a)
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      (aF)(a)\ne\varnothing;
+      \]
+\item \(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\).
+      If \(\iota\) is terminally essentially surjective, these are also
+      equivalent to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\);
+\item under separatedness on the slice and terminal essential surjectivity,
+      \(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\) holds exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is
+      nonempty and \(\mathfrak L(a)\) is empty.
 \end{enumerate}
-The base boundary $\mathbb L_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb L_1$ is a singleton-state embedding: pointwise states embed faithfully into information states, preserving satisfaction of all $\mathbb L_0$-formulas on that canonical image. The three higher boundaries $\mathbb L_1\preceq\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3\preceq\mathbb L_4$ are truth-preserving reduct expansions in the sense of \Cref{def:conservative-extension}, each with an explicit forgetful functor and state projection.
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-For the first boundary, the data displayed in \textup{(i)} give the language embedding
-\[
-e_{0,1}:\Sigma_0\hookrightarrow\Sigma_1,
-\]
-the forgetful functor $U_{1,0}$, and for each pointwise state $\rho$ the canonical singleton information state
-\[
-\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)=(\Gamma,\{\rho\}).
-\]
-\Cref{prop:singleton-conservativity} gives, for every $\mathbb L_0$-formula $\varphi$,
+Applying \(u\) to a strict matching family gives a matching family in the
+sheaf \(aF\), which has a unique amalgamation in \((aF)(a)\).  Conversely,
+let \(\xi\in(aF)(a)\).  The plus--plus description of sheafification gives
+a cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\) and sections \(s_i\in F(U_i)\) representing
+\(\xi|_{U_i}\), with the following local equality on each overlap: there is
+a cover \(\{V_{ijk}\to U_{ij}\}_k\) such that
 \[
-M,\iota_{0,1}^M(\rho)\Vdash_1\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{1,0}(M),\rho\Vdash_0\varphi.
+ s_i|_{V_{ijk}}=s_j|_{V_{ijk}}.
 \]
-These are exactly the three pieces of structure and the preservation condition required in \Cref{def:singleton-semantic-embedding}. Notice that the verification uses only singleton information states; it does not assert a projection from arbitrary $\mathbb L_1$-states to pointwise states.
+Every \(U_{ij}\to a\) is an object of the slice.  Separatedness there turns
+these locally witnessed equalities into
+\(s_i|_{U_{ij}}=s_j|_{U_{ij}}\).  The \(s_i\) therefore form a strict
+matching family.  This proves (i).
 
-For $\mathbb L_1\preceq\mathbb L_2$, the displayed clauses fix the object language of the expansion: $\Sigma_2$ is the disjoint expansion of $\Sigma_1$ by the local-section and site symbols listed in \textup{(ii)}, $\Mod_2$ is the class of $\Sigma_2$-expansions whose $\Sigma_1$-reduct is obtained by $U_{2,1}$, and $\pi^M_{2,1}$ is the identity on the underlying information state. Equivalently, this is the presheaf instance of the typed-expansion interface of \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. Atomic $\Sigma_1$-formulas use only symbols retained by $U_{2,1}$. Thus \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} gives, for every $\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_1$,
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_2\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{2,1}(M),\pi^M_{2,1}(p)\Vdash_1\varphi,
-\]
-which is \Cref{def:conservative-extension}.
-
-The same lemma applies to $\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3$. Here $\Sigma_3$ is the disjoint expansion of $\Sigma_2$ by the banded-groupoid-lift, band, component-gerbe, matching-without-amalgamation, and obstruction-class symbols listed in \textup{(iii)}. The admissible models are precisely the corresponding well-typed expansions singled out in \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. The functor $U_{3,2}$ forgets precisely those symbols, while $\pi^M_{3,2}$ leaves the underlying state unchanged. Atomic $\Sigma_2$-formulas contain no symbols for the forgotten gerbe or obstruction data, so \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_3\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{3,2}(M),\pi^M_{3,2}(p)\Vdash_2\varphi
-\qquad(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_2).
-\]
-Thus $\mathbb L_2\preceq\mathbb L_3$.
-
-Finally, $\Sigma_4$ is obtained from $\Sigma_3$ by adjoining only the refinement-dynamic axes, update structure, support notions, and rewrite operations listed in \textup{(iv)}. This is the refinement-dynamic instance of \Cref{prop:admissible-layer-expansion-interface}. The functor $U_{4,3}$ forgets exactly that dynamic structure, and $\pi^M_{4,3}$ forgets only the corresponding state bookkeeping. Atomic $\Sigma_3$-formulas are interpreted through the reduct, so \Cref{lem:layer-reduct-induction} yields
-\[
-M,p\Vdash_4\varphi
-\Longleftrightarrow
-U_{4,3}(M),\pi^M_{4,3}(p)\Vdash_3\varphi
-\qquad(\varphi\in\mathrm{Form}_3).
-\]
-Consequently the three upper steps are truth-preserving reduct expansions, and the displayed finite chain has exactly the asserted form.
+The isomorphism \(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong F(a)\) proves
+the first equivalence in (ii).  The forward implication from
+\(\mathfrak P(a)\ne\varnothing\) to \(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\) is
+given by \(\iota\), and the converse is terminal essential surjectivity.
+Finally, (iii) is obtained by combining (i), (ii), and the definition of
+\(\operatorname{MWA}(F,a)\).
 \end{proof}
 
-Hence the truth-preserving-reduct part of the chain begins at $\mathbb L_1$.
+The article treats \((\mathcal C,F,\mathfrak P,\mathscr A)\) as supplied
+finite-site lift data.  In particular, the realization theorem below is not
+derived from a lower team-semantic model.  A narrow lower-language separation
+example and the presentation bookkeeping removed from the core argument are
+given in the technical appendix,
+\Cref{supp-sec:auxiliary-separation}, only as context; they do not generate
+the lift.

 \begin{abstract}
-On the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres, a nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups exactly when $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial, and the finite-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models.
+For a stack, Giraud's component construction identifies the full substack
+over a global component section as its maximal component gerbe.  We apply
+this standard construction to a banded prestack lift of a presheaf on a
+finite site.  Under slice separatedness and terminal essential surjectivity,
+matching without amalgamation is equivalent to non-neutrality of every
+global component gerbe.  A representative-rigidity theorem shows that a
+strictly pullback-stable choice of lift representatives forces terminal
+effectivity when the band has vanishing first cohomology.  On a finite good
+cover with connected nonempty intersections and $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$, we
+give a self-contained Cech-cocycle prestack construction simultaneously
+controlling the component presheaf, terminal fibre, neutral labels, and
+prescribed evaluation maps $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$.  UCT and elementary
+subgroup arithmetic yield the aggregate quotients.  For the selected
+open-star sites of $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, a nonzero finite abelian group
+$G$ occurs as the two-component comparison kernel with complementary nonzero
+images exactly when $d(G)\le2\beta$ and $G$ is not cyclic of prime-power
+order.  This is a realization corollary for supplied lift data and does not
+transfer to bare empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

-\varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.

-The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
-\[
-\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
-\]
-Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
-\[
-\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
-=
-\Phi(c_{ijk}),
-\]
-which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
-
-The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
-\[
-(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
-\]
-is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
+The classification of abelian-banded gerbes identifies equivalence classes
+with \(H^2\), with the neutral gerbes representing zero
+\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}.  On a site with terminal object \(a\), neutrality
+is exactly existence of an object over \(a\), proving (ii).  For (iii), the
+component compatibility makes \(\Phi\) restrict to the full component
+substacks.  Applying \(\Phi\) to local objects and overlap arrows applies
+\(\theta\) to their triple-overlap defect cocycle.  This is the standard
+naturality of Giraud classification under a banded equivalence
+\cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
 \end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}

+\begin{theorem}[Terminal rigidity for representative-rigid lifts]

-\begin{lemma}[\v{C}ech calculus for component gerbes]\label{lem:cech-branch-gerbe-calculus}

-\begin{definition}[Presentation-comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
-For finite nerve representatives of a fixed component obstruction class, an
-\emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
-\Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
-cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
-The \emph{presentation-comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
-objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
-morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
-presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
-component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
-zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
-between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
-hypothesis is imposed.
-\end{definition}

-\begin{theorem}[Initiality among zero-evaluation quotients]\label{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}

-$K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$ are invariants of the chosen
-presentation. Across comparison-equivalent presentations they are transported
-functorially only along chosen morphisms in the presentation-comparison
-groupoid, as in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}; different zigzags
-with the same endpoints may carry different coefficient automorphisms. By
-contrast, the universal coefficient sequence need not split canonically. Thus
-the theory isolates a homological cokernel and homological image subgroup
-at each presentation, with comparison-zigzag functoriality, without requiring
-any noncanonical decomposition of $\omega$ into $H_2$-evaluated and UCT-Ext
-summands.
-\end{remark}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Comparison with cocycle-coordinate quotients]\label{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}
-Let $\alpha$ be any finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Then the homological cokernel
-\[
-Q_{\omega}
-\]
-admits a canonical surjective homomorphism onto the cocycle-coordinate quotient
-\[
-A/H_\alpha.
-\]
-Equivalently, every cocycle-coordinate quotient is a quotient of the homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $q:A\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha$ be the canonical quotient. By
-\suppresult{Cocycle-coordinate quotient}, the quotient kills every cocycle
-value $\alpha_{ijk}$ pointwise, so the pushed-forward cocycle representative
-is zero. Hence $q_*(\omega)=0$, and in particular it lies in the
-$\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup of $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A/H_\alpha)$. Apply
-\Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}.
-\end{proof}
+Define its \emph{homological image} and \emph{homological cokernel} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:homological-image-cokernel}
+ K_\omega:=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega),
+ \qquad Q_\omega:=A/K_\omega.
+\end{equation}
+These definitions depend on the supplied finite presentation of the component
+gerbe.  Refinement and retrivialization transport them by UCT naturality, but
+no canonical identification along distinct comparison zigzags is asserted.
+The resulting freely generated presentation groupoid and its elementary
+naturality calculation are recorded in the technical appendix rather than
+promoted to an invariance theorem.
 
-\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}
-Let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Write
-\[
-C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
-\]
-for the simplicial group of integral $2$-chains on the finite nerve. The \emph{chain-level evaluation map} of $\alpha$ is the homomorphism
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
-\]
-defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
-:=
-\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
-\]
-\end{definition}
+For a finite family of component classes
+\((\omega_v)_{v\in V}\), put \(K_v=K_{\omega_v}\) and define
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-quotients}
+ Q_{\mathrm{lab}}:=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v,
+ \qquad
+ Q_{\mathrm{com}}:=A\Big/\sum_{v\in V}K_v.
+\end{equation}
+The first quotient retains enough information to map to every componentwise
+quotient \(A/K_v\).  The second retains only characters which descend through
+every one of them.
 
-\begin{proposition}[Chain-coordinate versus homology-evaluation quotient]\label{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:chain-level-evaluation}, the following hold.
+\begin{proposition}[UCT and aggregate subgroup package]
+\label{prop:uct-aggregate-package}
+With the notation above:
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $2$-boundaries and therefore induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A.
-\]
-\item The induced homomorphism $\overline\alpha$ is exactly the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.
-\item The strict coordinate-image subgroup and the presentation-relative homological image subgroup satisfy
-\[
-H_\alpha=\mathrm{Im}(\widetilde\alpha),
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)).
-\]
+\item The universal coefficient sequence is
+      \[
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow H^2(N,A)
+      \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}
+      \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \]
+      Thus \(K_\omega=0\) exactly when \(\omega\) lies in the displayed
+      Ext subgroup.  In particular, nonzero classes can have zero
+      homological image when \(H_1\) has torsion.
+\item The quotient map \(q_\omega:A\to Q_\omega\) is initial among group
+      homomorphisms \(q:A\to B\) satisfying
+      \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\).  A character
+      \(\chi:A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) factors through \(Q_\omega\)
+      exactly when \(\chi(K_\omega)=0\).  Since finite Pontryagin duality
+      separates points,
+      \[
+      K_\omega=\mathop{\bigcap}_{\chi(K_\omega)=0}\ker\chi.
+      \]
+\item For a nonempty finite family \((K_v)_{v\in V}\), there is a natural
+      short exact sequence
+      \begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \end{equation}
+      Moreover,
+      \[
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}}
+      \cong\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v^\perp,
+      \qquad
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}}
+      \cong\sum_{v\in V}K_v^\perp
+      \]
+      inside \(\widehat A\).
+\item If \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
+      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), a subgroup
+      \(K\le A\) occurs as \(K_\omega\) exactly when \(d(K)\le\beta\).
+      Every finite family of such subgroups is simultaneously attained by
+      the prestack of
+      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}.
 \end{enumerate}
-Thus the gap between chain-coordinate quotient and homology-evaluation quotient is exactly the gap between the image of the cocycle on all $2$-chains and its image on $2$-cycles.
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-If $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, then
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)=(\delta\alpha)(c)=0
-\]
-because $\alpha$ is a cocycle. Hence $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $B_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ and induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=Z_2/B_2\to A.
-\]
-This proves \textup{(i)}.
+Clause (i) is the cohomological universal coefficient theorem, natural in
+both \(N\) and \(A\) \cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}.  Its middle-to-right map
+evaluates a cohomology class on integral \(2\)-cycles, so its value at
+\(\omega\) is \(\operatorname{ev}_\omega\).  Exactness identifies the
+kernel with the Ext term.
 
-For any $2$-cycle $z=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\in Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, set
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z):=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma)=\widetilde\alpha(z).
-\]
-If $z'$ is another $2$-cycle homologous to $z$, then $z-z'=\partial c$ for some $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$. By \textup{(i)},
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z)-\alpha^{\sharp}(z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(z-z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)
-=
-0.
-\]
-Therefore $\alpha^{\sharp}$ depends only on the homology class of $z$ and defines a homomorphism
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A,\qquad
-[z]\longmapsto \alpha^{\sharp}(z).
-\]
-By the definition of the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$, this homomorphism is exactly the image of the cohomology class $\omega=[\alpha]$ under
-\[
-\eta_A:H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\to \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A).
-\]
-Thus
-\[
-\overline\alpha([z])=\alpha^{\sharp}(z)=\eta_A(\omega)([z])=\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}([z])
-\]
-for every $[z]\in H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, proving \textup{(ii)}.
+For (ii), \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\) says precisely that \(q\)
+vanishes on \(K_\omega\).  The universal property of the quotient gives a
+unique factorization through \(A/K_\omega\).  Apply the same observation to
+characters.  The intersection formula follows because characters of a
+finite abelian group separate points \cite{Terras1999}.
 
-For \textup{(iii)}, the image of $\widetilde\alpha$ is exactly the subgroup generated by the simplex values $\alpha_{ijk}$, hence it is $H_\alpha$ by \suppresult{Finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative}. The equality
+The containment \(\bigcap_vK_v\subseteq\sum_vK_v\) gives the quotient map in
+\eqref{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}.  By the third isomorphism theorem its
+kernel is
 \[
-\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))
+ \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v},
 \]
-is immediate from \textup{(i)}, and \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient} identifies this image with $K_{\omega}$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Coincidence of the chain-coordinate and homology-evaluation quotients]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-coincidence-criterion}
-Let $\alpha$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of $\omega$. The following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $A/H_\alpha\cong Q_{\omega}$;
-\item $H_\alpha=K_{\omega}$;
-\item $\widetilde\alpha(C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Equivalently, the chain-coordinate quotient agrees with the homology-evaluation quotient exactly when every value of the cocycle on a $2$-chain already occurs on a $2$-cycle.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is immediate from the quotient descriptions
+which proves exactness.  For finite abelian groups, annihilators exchange sums and
+intersections:
 \[
-A/H_\alpha
-\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}.
+ \Big(\sum_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\bigcap_vK_v^\perp,
+ \qquad
+ \Big(\bigcap_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\sum_vK_v^\perp.
 \]
-The equivalence of \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} is exactly \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}(iii).
-\end{proof}
+Dualizing the two quotients proves the character formulas in (iii).
 
-\begin{theorem}[Nonzero UCT-Ext classes and vanishing $H_2$ evaluation]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admissible
-parameter, global component section, banded groupoid lift, trivialized constant finite
-abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
-$\omega$ as a derived component class, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $Q_{\omega}=A$;
-\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
+Under the hypotheses of (iv), the Ext term vanishes and UCT becomes
 \[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
+ H^2(N,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z^\beta,A).
 \]
-\end{enumerate}
-If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-trivializing for that component class. If, in addition, the banded groupoid lift is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
+The image of a homomorphism from \(\mathbb Z^\beta\) is generated by the
+images of the standard basis, so it has at most \(\beta\) generators.
+Conversely, given generators \(k_1,\dots,k_\beta\) of \(K\), allowing zeros
+when fewer are needed, the map
 \[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
+ (n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto\sum_jn_jk_j
 \]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
-\]
-so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. By the universal coefficient sequence, \textup{(iii)} holds exactly when $\omega\in\ker(\eta_A)$, and this kernel is the stated $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.
-
-If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
-On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies
-\[
-\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\]
-for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-trivializing.
-
-Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen global component section $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
-\]
-Suppose towards a contradiction that
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-By clause \textup{(i)} of \suppresult{Banded groupoid lift and stackification}, this yields an object of the terminal fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$, and its image under the stackification morphism
-\[
-\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
-\]
-defines an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Because there is only one global component section, every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in the unique component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v(a)$. Hence
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
-\]
-By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this implies that $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral, contradicting the non-neutrality already proved. Therefore
-\[
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-Combining this with $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ and admissibility of $r$, we obtain
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
-\]
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Vanishing evaluation when $H_2=0$]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}
-Assume
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
-\]
-Then, for every obstruction class $\omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$,
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A.
-\]
-Every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve therefore has zero $H_2$ evaluation, and every character is class-trivializing.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
-\[
-\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0,
-\]
-so $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ for every $\omega$. Apply \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[No nonzero classes with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation when $H_1$ is free]\label{cor:h1-free-no-blindness}
-Assume that $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian. Then
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\omega=0.
-\]
-Equivalently, every nonzero component obstruction class has nonzero $H_2$ evaluation. In particular, if $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve produces a proper homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0.
-\]
-Hence the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$ is injective. By \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0.
-\]
-Injectivity of $\eta_A$ therefore gives $K_{\omega}=0$ if and only if $\omega=0$. If $\omega\neq 0$, then $K_{\omega}\neq 0$, so $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ is a proper quotient of the finite group $A$.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{example}[A nonzero class with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation on an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve]\label{ex:rp2-character-blind}
-This is a finite-nerve mechanism example.  Let $\mathcal U$ be a finite cover
-whose \v{C}ech nerve is a finite triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^2$, and take
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-H_2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)=0,
-\qquad
-H_1(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~2.2]{Hatcher2002}. The universal coefficient sequence therefore yields
-\[
-H^2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}. Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A,
-\]
-by \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}. Thus the homological cokernel is all of $A$, although the obstruction class is nonzero. Every character is therefore class-trivializing. If this is the unique global component section of the admissible parameter under consideration and \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, then \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} yields a matching family without global amalgamation whose component class is trivialized by every character.
-
-The last sentence is conditional on the usual banded-stack-lift data: an
-admissible parameter, a banded stack lift with constant band
-$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and the
-\textup{(H4)} comparison identifying the displayed finite-nerve class with the
-derived component class; the matching-without-amalgamation conclusion also requires
-separatedness on the slice site associated to the parameter.  The unconditional content of the example is the
-homological mechanism
-\[
-\omega\in \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A),
-\qquad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0,
-\]
-which makes the homological cokernel equal to $A$ although the
-obstruction class is nonzero.  Thus the example records the UCT
-$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel of the finite nerve, while the component-gerbe conclusion
-enters only after the admissible-parameter and banded-lift hypotheses have been
-supplied.
-\end{example}
-
-\begin{example}[A single-component surjective-homological-evaluation class on $S^2$]\label{ex:s2-single-branch-maximal-collapse}
-Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S^2\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite good cover of $S^2$, let $N:=N(\mathcal U)$ be its nerve, and let $\mathcal C_a$ be the corresponding slice site for one admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ with $a=[r]_p$. Take the constant band
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-on $\mathcal C_a$. Define the presheaf of local sections
-\[
-F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}:\mathcal C_a^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
-\]
-by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(U)=\{v\}
-\]
-for every nonempty proper finite intersection $U$ of members of $\mathcal U$, by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing,
-\]
-and by the identity map on every restriction between proper intersections. Then the cover
-\[
-\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
-\]
-supports the compatible family constantly equal to $v$, while there is no global section at $a$. Hence
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r),
-\qquad
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-The restricted presheaf is separated on the slice: over \(a\) there are no two
-sections to compare, and over every proper nonempty intersection there is
-only the section \(v\).
-Because
-\[
-H^2(N,A)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,
-\]
-choose a simplicial cocycle
-\[
-\alpha\in Z^2(N,A)
-\]
-representing the nonzero class. For each $U_i$ choose a local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$, and choose isomorphisms
-\[
-\phi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim} x_j|_{U_{ij}}
-\]
-on the pairwise overlaps such that
-\[
-\phi_{ik}^{-1}\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}=\alpha_{ijk}\in A
-\]
-on each triple overlap. This is the single-label instance of the
-cocycle-to-prestack construction isolated in
-\suppresult{$2$-cocycle-defined banded prestack for one component}, used under the same generated-subsite
-admissibility convention as \suppresult{Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion};
-equivalently, it is the standard local-trivialization construction for gerbes
-\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Sec.~5]{Breen2006}, \cite{Murray1996}. It
-yields a prestack presentation $\mathfrak P_r$ on $\mathcal C_a$ with the following properties:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item over each member $U_i$ of the cover there is the chosen local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$;
-\item the chosen transition maps have triple-overlap defect exactly $\alpha$;
-\item the presheaf of isomorphism classes satisfies
-\[
- \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus the example begins with an explicit presheaf of local sections and then chooses local lift objects and transition data whose component presheaf is the given functor; the component gerbe is recovered from those data by stackification rather than being taken as primitive input.
-
-Let
-\[
-\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r).
-\]
-Because $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$, the sheaf of connected components of $\mathfrak L_r$ has exactly one global section at $a$, represented by the constant compatible family above. Therefore
-\[
-\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}.
-\]
-But $\alpha$ is nonzero, so the descent datum is ineffective and no object exists over $a$ in the resulting stack; equivalently, the unique component gerbe is non-neutral. Hence
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
-\qquad
-\omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
-\]
-Combining this with the already computed presheaf-level facts gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
-\qquad
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r),
-\qquad
-\Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\},
-\qquad
-\mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
-\qquad
-\omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
-\]
-The good cover $\mathcal U$ trivializes the constant band, all finite intersections are contractible, and therefore the $H^1$-vanishing and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction,def:finite-nerve-presentation} are satisfied.
-
-Since
-\[
-H_1(N,\mathbb Z) = 0,
-\qquad
-H_2(N,\mathbb Z) \cong \mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Secs.~2.1, 2.2]{Hatcher2002}, the universal coefficient theorem gives
-\[
-H^2(N, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
-\cong
-\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
-\cong
-\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}.
-\]
-Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class, and let $[S^2]$ denote the fundamental class in $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)$. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_\omega([S^2]) = 1 \in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
-\]
-so the homological evaluation map is surjective. By \Cref{cor:maximal-collapse},
-\[
-K_\omega = A = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
-\qquad
-Q_\omega = 0.
-\]
-Hence
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
-\qquad
-\omega=\omega_v\neq 0,
-\qquad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\twoheadrightarrow A,
-\qquad
-K_\omega=A,
-\qquad
-Q_\omega=0.
-\]
-Since $K_\omega = A$, \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} gives
-\[
-X_\omega = \mathrm{Ann}(K_\omega) = \mathrm{Ann}(A) = \{1\},
-\]
-so only the trivial character is class-trivializing. Equivalently, $Q_\omega = A/K_\omega = 0$.
-
-This example therefore verifies the full downstream hypothesis chain
-\[
-(\mathcal C_a,\mathfrak P_r,A,\omega,\mathrm{ev}_\omega,K_\omega,Q_\omega)
-\]
-inside a concrete site-theoretic example, once the banded stack lift has been fixed by the chosen cocycle data. It is the opposite extreme from the zero-evaluation case of \Cref{ex:rp2-character-blind}: for an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=0$, every character is class-trivializing, and the obstruction is entirely in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel with $Q_\omega=A$; for the present $S^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=A$, only the trivial character is class-trivializing, and the obstruction is entirely detected on $H_2$, with $Q_\omega=0$.
-\end{example}

-\begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the homological quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
-An \emph{auxiliary register for the homological quotient} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
-\[
-\iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow Q_{\omega}\times R
-\]
-such that
-\[
-\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
-\]
-\end{definition}
-

+A stack in groupoids has a sheaf of connected components.  A global section
+of that sheaf need not be represented by a global object of the stack, but it
+does select a maximal subgerbe.  This is Giraud's component-gerbe construction
+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  The component is represented by a
+global object precisely when its gerbe is neutral, or equivalently when its
+Giraud \(H^2\)-class vanishes.  These classical facts are the starting point
+of the article.
+
+Our setting is deliberately finite and presentation-relative.  We fix a site
+with terminal object, a presheaf \(F\), an abelian-banded prestack lift
+\(\mathfrak P\), and its stackification \(\mathfrak L\).  The connected
+components of \(\mathfrak P\) recover \(F\), while those of
+\(\mathfrak L\) recover the sheafification \(aF\).  If \(F\) is separated on
+the terminal slice and stackification is essentially surjective on the
+terminal fibre, a strict matching family without an amalgamation occurs
+exactly when \((aF)(a)\) is nonempty and every component gerbe selected by a
+section of \((aF)(a)\) is non-neutral.  This is a comparison between a strict
+presheaf predicate and standard gerbe theory, not a new classification of
+gerbes.
+
+The first paper-specific point is a rigidity statement for a particularly
+strong kind of prestack presentation.  Suppose one selects a representative
+of every presheaf component and requires those representatives to be stable
+under pullback as literal equalities with respect to a split cleavage.  Under
+slice separatedness, terminal essential surjectivity then forces the
+sheafification unit
 \[

+terminal sheafification unit, and the sheaf gluing condition at the terminal
+object.  The proof in \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} distinguishes the

+\subsection*{Organization}
 
-\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2em,labelindent=0pt]
-\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
-A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
-\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
-$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
-$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
-\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
-The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
-satisfaction.
-\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
-An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
-the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
-is not part of the definition.
-\item[Typed expansion class.]
-The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
-fixed lower model.
-\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
-An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
-exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
-are attached to $r$.
-\item[{Base object $a=[r]_p$.}]
-The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
-the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
-\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
-The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
-specified pretopology and pullbacks.
-\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
-The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
-\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
-A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
-\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
-A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
-terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
-hypothesis.
-\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
-A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
-strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
-\item[Global component section $v$.]
-An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
-$(aF)(a)$.
-\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
-The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
-$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
-\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
-The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
-replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
-zigzags need not give the same comparison.
-\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
-For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
-and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
-\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
-$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
-$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
-\item[Label-aware quotient.]
-$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
-componentwise homological cokernels.
-\item[Common-character quotient.]
-$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
-\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
-The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
-common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
-\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
-A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
-cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
-\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
-The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
-the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
-\item[Typed readout.]
-The partial output attached to an admissible parameter: inadmissible if no
-typed data are attached, uniquely determined if the sheafified global section
-is unique, and non-unique-or-absent otherwise.
-\item[Indexed refinement system.]
-A family of state-refinement relations indexed by information coordinates,
-each monotone for the state preorder and the specified time order.
-\item[Information-determining axis set.]
-A finite set of refinement coordinates whose information values determine any
-decided truth value among the states reachable along those coordinates.
-\item[Pairwise commuting refinements and common refinement.]
-Refinements for which every indicated finite family has a state refining all
-its members.
-\item[Readout-preserving rewrite.]
-A rewrite between partial outputs that preserves both definedness and value.
-\item[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf.]
-A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is the
-given empirical-model support presheaf and whose automorphism sheaves are the
-specified band.
-\end{description}
+Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the minimal presheaf and prestack
+interface.  Section~\ref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} records the standard Giraud
+component package, proves the comparison criterion, and gives the full

 \begin{abstract}
-On the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres, a nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups exactly when $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. +For a stack, Giraud's component construction identifies the full substack

+\begin{proposition}[Standard component-gerbe package]

+      \]

-\begin{lemma}[Transport of Giraud classes under banded equivalence]\label{lem:giraud-class-transport}
-Let $\mathfrak G$ be a $\Band$-banded gerbe and let $\mathfrak G'$ be a $\Band'$-banded gerbe on the same site $\mathcal C$. Suppose
-\[
-\Phi:\mathfrak G\to\mathfrak G'
-\]
-is an equivalence of stacks whose induced maps on automorphism sheaves identify the bands through an isomorphism
-\[
-\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-\theta_*[\mathfrak G]=[\mathfrak G']
-\qquad\text{in}\qquad
-H^2(\mathcal C,\Band').
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Choose a cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ which locally trivializes $\mathfrak G$, objects $x_i\in\mathfrak G(U_i)$, and descent isomorphisms
-\[
-\varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.
-\]
-The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
-\[
-\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
-\]
-Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
-\[
-\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
-=
-\Phi(c_{ijk}),
-\]
-which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
-
-The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
-\[
-(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
-\]
-is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
+The classification of abelian-banded gerbes identifies equivalence classes
+with \(H^2\), with the neutral gerbes representing zero
+\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}.  On a site with terminal object \(a\), neutrality
+is exactly existence of an object over \(a\), proving (ii).  For (iii), the
+component compatibility makes \(\Phi\) restrict to the full component
+substacks.  Applying \(\Phi\) to local objects and overlap arrows applies
+\(\theta\) to their triple-overlap defect cocycle.  This is the standard
+naturality of Giraud classification under a banded equivalence
+\cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
 \end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}
-In the pullback-based setting of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}, and using only the banded groupoid lift and component data fixed there, every global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ determines a full substack $\mathfrak G_v\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ that is a banded $\Band$-gerbe over $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$.  \end{theorem}
 
 \begin{proof}

-\[

-\]
-is a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf of

-\[
-\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong (a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(a),
-\]

-\[

-\{x\in\mathfrak L_r(U)\mid [x]\ \text{restricts to}\ v|_U\}
-\]
-is therefore exactly the $v$-component substack
-$\mathfrak E_r[v]$ of \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}.
+By \Cref{prop:finite-site-semantic-interface}(i), matching is equivalent to
+\((aF)(a)\ne\varnothing\).  By clause (ii) of that proposition and terminal
+essential surjectivity, \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\) is equivalent to
+\(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\).  The latter holds exactly when one of the
+full components \(\mathfrak G_v\) contains an object over \(a\).  By
+\Cref{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package}(ii), this is equivalent to

-\begin{theorem}[\v{C}ech obstruction of a component gerbe on an acyclic cover]\label{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction}

+\begin{theorem}[Terminal rigidity for representative-rigid lifts]
+\label{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}
+Let \(F\) be separated on the slice over \(a\), and let \(\mathfrak P\) be a
+representative-rigid \(\mathscr A\)-banded prestack lift of \(F\).  Write
+\(u:F\to aF\) and \(\iota:\mathfrak P\to\mathfrak L=a(\mathfrak P)\).
 Then:
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item for every pair $(i,j)$ there exists an isomorphism
-\[
-\theta_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim} x_j|_{U_{ij}};
-\]
-\item on each triple overlap $U_{ijk}$, the element
-\[
-c_{ijk}:=\theta_{ik}^{-1}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ \theta_{jk}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ \theta_{ij}|_{U_{ijk}}
-\in \Band(U_{ijk})
-\]
-defines a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle $c=(c_{ijk})\in \check Z^2(\mathcal U,\Band)$;
-\item the class $[c]\in \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)$ depends only on the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and the chosen cover: changing the local lift objects or the comparison isomorphisms changes $c$ by a \v{C}ech coboundary, and refinements of acyclic covers pull this class back functorially;
-\item the class $[c]$ vanishes if and only if the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral over $a$.
+\item terminal essential surjectivity of \(\iota\) implies that
+      \(u_a:F(a)\to(aF)(a)\) is surjective;
+\item if \(H^1(\mathcal C,\mathscr A)=0\), surjectivity of \(u_a\) implies
+      terminal essential surjectivity of \(\iota\).
 \end{enumerate}
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}

-Then the associated cocycle satisfies

-\begin{definition}[Presentation-comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
-For finite nerve representatives of a fixed component obstruction class, an
-\emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
-\Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
-cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
-The \emph{presentation-comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
-objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
-morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
-presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
-component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
-zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
-between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
-hypothesis is imposed.
-\end{definition}

-\begin{theorem}[Initiality among zero-evaluation quotients]\label{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}
-In the finite nerve representative of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
-\[
-\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_\omega=A/K_\omega
-\]
-be the homological cokernel. For every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $q$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$;
-\item $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)=K_\omega$;
-\item $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$;
-\item $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
-\]
-of the universal coefficient sequence.
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus $Q_\omega$ is initial among coefficient quotients for which the pushed-forward obstruction has zero $H_2$ evaluation. This is the pullback-site, finite-nerve form of the companion initiality theorem \cite[Theorem~6.13]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure}.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is the universal property of the quotient
-\[
-\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_\omega.
-\]
-Indeed, a homomorphism $q:A\to B$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$ if and only if $K_\omega\subseteq\ker q$, which is exactly the assertion that $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)$.
-
-For \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)}, use naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the coefficient homomorphism $q$. The naturality square gives
-\[
-\eta_B(q_*\omega)=q\circ \eta_A(\omega)=q\circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega.
-\]
-Thus $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q$ vanishes on the image of $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$, namely on $K_\omega$.
-
-Finally, the universal coefficient exact sequence for the finite nerve is
-\[
-0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
-\xrightarrow{\eta_B}
-\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\to 0.
-\]
-Therefore $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the kernel of $\eta_B$, which is precisely the displayed UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup. This proves all equivalences and the initiality statement.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Class-trivializing initiality when $H_1$ vanishes]\label{cor:h1-vanishing-class-trivializing}
-Assume
-\[
-H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
+ \operatorname{ev}_\omega:
+ H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow A.
 \]
-Then, for every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $q_*(\omega)=0$ in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)$;
-\item $q$ factors uniquely through
-\[
-\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\omega}.
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-Hence, when $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, the homological cokernel is initial among coefficient quotients that annihilate the obstruction class itself.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)=0
-\]
-for every abelian group $B$. Thus, in the criterion of \Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}, the zero-evaluation condition is equivalent to $q_*(\omega)=0$, and the conclusion follows.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Presentation-relative invariance without a canonical splitting]\label{rem:no-canonical-splitting}
-For a fixed finite nerve representative, the quotient
-$Q_{\omega}$ and the subgroup
-$K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$ are invariants of the chosen
-presentation. Across comparison-equivalent presentations they are transported
-functorially only along chosen morphisms in the presentation-comparison
-groupoid, as in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}; different zigzags
-with the same endpoints may carry different coefficient automorphisms. By
-contrast, the universal coefficient sequence need not split canonically. Thus
-the theory isolates a homological cokernel and homological image subgroup
-at each presentation, with comparison-zigzag functoriality, without requiring
-any noncanonical decomposition of $\omega$ into $H_2$-evaluated and UCT-Ext
-summands.
-\end{remark}

-\begin{corollary}[Comparison with cocycle-coordinate quotients]\label{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}
-Let $\alpha$ be any finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Then the homological cokernel
-\[
-Q_{\omega}
-\]
-admits a canonical surjective homomorphism onto the cocycle-coordinate quotient
-\[
-A/H_\alpha.
-\]
-Equivalently, every cocycle-coordinate quotient is a quotient of the homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let $q:A\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha$ be the canonical quotient. By
-\suppresult{Cocycle-coordinate quotient}, the quotient kills every cocycle
-value $\alpha_{ijk}$ pointwise, so the pushed-forward cocycle representative
-is zero. Hence $q_*(\omega)=0$, and in particular it lies in the
-$\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup of $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A/H_\alpha)$. Apply
-\Cref{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}.
-\end{proof}
+Define its \emph{homological image} and \emph{homological cokernel} by
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:homological-image-cokernel}
+ K_\omega:=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega),
+ \qquad Q_\omega:=A/K_\omega.
+\end{equation}
+These definitions depend on the supplied finite presentation of the component
+gerbe.  Refinement and retrivialization transport them by UCT naturality, but
+no canonical identification along distinct comparison zigzags is asserted.
+The resulting freely generated presentation groupoid and its elementary
+naturality calculation are recorded in the technical appendix rather than
+promoted to an invariance theorem.
 
-\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}
-Let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Write
-\[
-C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
-\]
-for the simplicial group of integral $2$-chains on the finite nerve. The \emph{chain-level evaluation map} of $\alpha$ is the homomorphism
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
-\]
-defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
-:=
-\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
-\]
-\end{definition}
+For a finite family of component classes
+\((\omega_v)_{v\in V}\), put \(K_v=K_{\omega_v}\) and define
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-quotients}
+ Q_{\mathrm{lab}}:=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v,
+ \qquad
+ Q_{\mathrm{com}}:=A\Big/\sum_{v\in V}K_v.
+\end{equation}
+The first quotient retains enough information to map to every componentwise
+quotient \(A/K_v\).  The second retains only characters which descend through
+every one of them.
 
-\begin{proposition}[Chain-coordinate versus homology-evaluation quotient]\label{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:chain-level-evaluation}, the following hold.
+\begin{proposition}[UCT and aggregate subgroup package]
+\label{prop:uct-aggregate-package}
+With the notation above:
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $2$-boundaries and therefore induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A.
-\]
-\item The induced homomorphism $\overline\alpha$ is exactly the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.
-\item The strict coordinate-image subgroup and the presentation-relative homological image subgroup satisfy
-\[
-H_\alpha=\mathrm{Im}(\widetilde\alpha),
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)).
-\]
+\item The universal coefficient sequence is
+      \[
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow H^2(N,A)
+      \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}
+      \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \]
+      Thus \(K_\omega=0\) exactly when \(\omega\) lies in the displayed
+      Ext subgroup.  In particular, nonzero classes can have zero
+      homological image when \(H_1\) has torsion.
+\item The quotient map \(q_\omega:A\to Q_\omega\) is initial among group
+      homomorphisms \(q:A\to B\) satisfying
+      \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\).  A character
+      \(\chi:A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) factors through \(Q_\omega\)
+      exactly when \(\chi(K_\omega)=0\).  Since finite Pontryagin duality
+      separates points,
+      \[
+      K_\omega=\mathop{\bigcap}_{\chi(K_\omega)=0}\ker\chi.
+      \]
+\item For a nonempty finite family \((K_v)_{v\in V}\), there is a natural
+      short exact sequence
+      \begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \end{equation}
+      Moreover,
+      \[
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}}
+      \cong\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v^\perp,
+      \qquad
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}}
+      \cong\sum_{v\in V}K_v^\perp
+      \]
+      inside \(\widehat A\).
+\item If \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
+      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), a subgroup
+      \(K\le A\) occurs as \(K_\omega\) exactly when \(d(K)\le\beta\).
+      Every finite family of such subgroups is simultaneously attained by
+      the prestack of
+      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}.
 \end{enumerate}
-Thus the gap between chain-coordinate quotient and homology-evaluation quotient is exactly the gap between the image of the cocycle on all $2$-chains and its image on $2$-cycles.
 \end{proposition}
 
 \begin{proof}
-If $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, then
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)=(\delta\alpha)(c)=0
-\]
-because $\alpha$ is a cocycle. Hence $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $B_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ and induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=Z_2/B_2\to A.
-\]
-This proves \textup{(i)}.
+Clause (i) is the cohomological universal coefficient theorem, natural in
+both \(N\) and \(A\) \cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}.  Its middle-to-right map
+evaluates a cohomology class on integral \(2\)-cycles, so its value at
+\(\omega\) is \(\operatorname{ev}_\omega\).  Exactness identifies the
+kernel with the Ext term.
 
-For any $2$-cycle $z=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\in Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, set
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z):=\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma)=\widetilde\alpha(z).
-\]
-If $z'$ is another $2$-cycle homologous to $z$, then $z-z'=\partial c$ for some $c\in C_3(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$. By \textup{(i)},
-\[
-\alpha^{\sharp}(z)-\alpha^{\sharp}(z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(z-z')
-=
-\widetilde\alpha(\partial c)
-=
-0.
-\]
-Therefore $\alpha^{\sharp}$ depends only on the homology class of $z$ and defines a homomorphism
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A,\qquad
-[z]\longmapsto \alpha^{\sharp}(z).
-\]
-By the definition of the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$, this homomorphism is exactly the image of the cohomology class $\omega=[\alpha]$ under
-\[
-\eta_A:H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\to \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A).
-\]
-Thus
-\[
-\overline\alpha([z])=\alpha^{\sharp}(z)=\eta_A(\omega)([z])=\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}([z])
-\]
-for every $[z]\in H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, proving \textup{(ii)}.
+For (ii), \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\) says precisely that \(q\)
+vanishes on \(K_\omega\).  The universal property of the quotient gives a
+unique factorization through \(A/K_\omega\).  Apply the same observation to
+characters.  The intersection formula follows because characters of a
+finite abelian group separate points \cite{Terras1999}.
 
-For \textup{(iii)}, the image of $\widetilde\alpha$ is exactly the subgroup generated by the simplex values $\alpha_{ijk}$, hence it is $H_\alpha$ by \suppresult{Finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative}. The equality
+The containment \(\bigcap_vK_v\subseteq\sum_vK_v\) gives the quotient map in
+\eqref{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}.  By the third isomorphism theorem its
+kernel is
 \[
-\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))
+ \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v},
 \]
-is immediate from \textup{(i)}, and \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient} identifies this image with $K_{\omega}$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Coincidence of the chain-coordinate and homology-evaluation quotients]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-coincidence-criterion}
-Let $\alpha$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of $\omega$. The following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $A/H_\alpha\cong Q_{\omega}$;
-\item $H_\alpha=K_{\omega}$;
-\item $\widetilde\alpha(C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Equivalently, the chain-coordinate quotient agrees with the homology-evaluation quotient exactly when every value of the cocycle on a $2$-chain already occurs on a $2$-cycle.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is immediate from the quotient descriptions
+which proves exactness.  For finite abelian groups, annihilators exchange sums and
+intersections:
 \[
-A/H_\alpha
-\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}.
+ \Big(\sum_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\bigcap_vK_v^\perp,
+ \qquad
+ \Big(\bigcap_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\sum_vK_v^\perp.
 \]
-The equivalence of \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} is exactly \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}(iii).
-\end{proof}
+Dualizing the two quotients proves the character formulas in (iii).
 
-\begin{theorem}[Nonzero UCT-Ext classes and vanishing $H_2$ evaluation]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admissible
-parameter, global component section, banded groupoid lift, trivialized constant finite
-abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
-$\omega$ as a derived component class, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $Q_{\omega}=A$;
-\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
+Under the hypotheses of (iv), the Ext term vanishes and UCT becomes
 \[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
+ H^2(N,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z^\beta,A).
 \]
-\end{enumerate}
-If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-trivializing for that component class. If, in addition, the banded groupoid lift is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
+The image of a homomorphism from \(\mathbb Z^\beta\) is generated by the
+images of the standard basis, so it has at most \(\beta\) generators.
+Conversely, given generators \(k_1,\dots,k_\beta\) of \(K\), allowing zeros
+when fewer are needed, the map
 \[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
+ (n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto\sum_jn_jk_j
 \]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
-\]
-so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. By the universal coefficient sequence, \textup{(iii)} holds exactly when $\omega\in\ker(\eta_A)$, and this kernel is the stated $\operatorname{Ext}$-subgroup. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.
-
-If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
-On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies
-\[
-\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\]
-for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-trivializing.
-
-Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen global component section $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
-\]
-Suppose towards a contradiction that
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-By clause \textup{(i)} of \suppresult{Banded groupoid lift and stackification}, this yields an object of the terminal fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$, and its image under the stackification morphism
-\[
-\iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r
-\]
-defines an object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$. Because there is only one global component section, every object of $\mathfrak L_r(a)$ lies in the unique component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v(a)$. Hence
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
-\]
-By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this implies that $\mathfrak G_v$ is neutral, contradicting the non-neutrality already proved. Therefore
-\[
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-Combining this with $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ and admissibility of $r$, we obtain
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
-\]
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Vanishing evaluation when $H_2=0$]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}
-Assume
-\[
-H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0.
-\]
-Then, for every obstruction class $\omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$,
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A.
-\]
-Every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve therefore has zero $H_2$ evaluation, and every character is class-trivializing.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)=0$, then
-\[
-\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0,
-\]
-so $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ for every $\omega$. Apply \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[No nonzero classes with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation when $H_1$ is free]\label{cor:h1-free-no-blindness}
-Assume that $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian. Then
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\omega=0.
-\]
-Equivalently, every nonzero component obstruction class has nonzero $H_2$ evaluation. In particular, if $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve produces a proper homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0.
-\]
-Hence the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$ is injective. By \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0.
-\]
-Injectivity of $\eta_A$ therefore gives $K_{\omega}=0$ if and only if $\omega=0$. If $\omega\neq 0$, then $K_{\omega}\neq 0$, so $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ is a proper quotient of the finite group $A$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{example}[A nonzero class with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation on an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve]\label{ex:rp2-character-blind}
-This is a finite-nerve mechanism example.  Let $\mathcal U$ be a finite cover
-whose \v{C}ech nerve is a finite triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^2$, and take
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-H_2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)=0,
-\qquad
-H_1(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~2.2]{Hatcher2002}. The universal coefficient sequence therefore yields
-\[
-H^2(\mathbb{R}P^2,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)
-\cong
-\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}. Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class. Then
-\[
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=0,
-\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A,
-\]
-by \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions}. Thus the homological cokernel is all of $A$, although the obstruction class is nonzero. Every character is therefore class-trivializing. If this is the unique global component section of the admissible parameter under consideration and \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, then \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} yields a matching family without global amalgamation whose component class is trivialized by every character.
-
-The last sentence is conditional on the usual banded-stack-lift data: an
-admissible parameter, a banded stack lift with constant band
-$\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and the
-\textup{(H4)} comparison identifying the displayed finite-nerve class with the
-derived component class; the matching-without-amalgamation conclusion also requires
-separatedness on the slice site associated to the parameter.  The unconditional content of the example is the
-homological mechanism
-\[
-\omega\in \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A),
-\qquad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0,
-\]
-which makes the homological cokernel equal to $A$ although the
-obstruction class is nonzero.  Thus the example records the UCT
-$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel of the finite nerve, while the component-gerbe conclusion
-enters only after the admissible-parameter and banded-lift hypotheses have been
-supplied.
-\end{example}

-\begin{example}[A single-component surjective-homological-evaluation class on $S^2$]\label{ex:s2-single-branch-maximal-collapse}
-Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S^2\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite good cover of $S^2$, let $N:=N(\mathcal U)$ be its nerve, and let $\mathcal C_a$ be the corresponding slice site for one admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ with $a=[r]_p$. Take the constant band
-\[
-A=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z
-\]
-on $\mathcal C_a$. Define the presheaf of local sections
-\[
-F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}:\mathcal C_a^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}
-\]
-by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(U)=\{v\}
-\]
-for every nonempty proper finite intersection $U$ of members of $\mathcal U$, by
-\[
-F_{p,s}(a)=\varnothing,
-\]
-and by the identity map on every restriction between proper intersections. Then the cover
-\[
-\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
-\]
-supports the compatible family constantly equal to $v$, while there is no global section at $a$. Hence
-\[
-M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r),
-\qquad
-M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
-\]
-The restricted presheaf is separated on the slice: over \(a\) there are no two
-sections to compare, and over every proper nonempty intersection there is
-only the section \(v\).
-Because
-\[
-H^2(N,A)\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,
-\]
-choose a simplicial cocycle
-\[
-\alpha\in Z^2(N,A)
-\]
-representing the nonzero class. For each $U_i$ choose a local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$, and choose isomorphisms
-\[
-\phi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim} x_j|_{U_{ij}}
-\]
-on the pairwise overlaps such that
-\[
-\phi_{ik}^{-1}\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}=\alpha_{ijk}\in A
-\]
-on each triple overlap. This is the single-label instance of the
-cocycle-to-prestack construction isolated in
-\suppresult{$2$-cocycle-defined banded prestack for one component}, used under the same generated-subsite
-admissibility convention as \suppresult{Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion};
-equivalently, it is the standard local-trivialization construction for gerbes
-\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Sec.~5]{Breen2006}, \cite{Murray1996}. It
-yields a prestack presentation $\mathfrak P_r$ on $\mathcal C_a$ with the following properties:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item over each member $U_i$ of the cover there is the chosen local lift object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$;
-\item the chosen transition maps have triple-overlap defect exactly $\alpha$;
-\item the presheaf of isomorphism classes satisfies
-\[
- \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
-\]
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus the example begins with an explicit presheaf of local sections and then chooses local lift objects and transition data whose component presheaf is the given functor; the component gerbe is recovered from those data by stackification rather than being taken as primitive input.
-
-Let
-\[
-\mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r).
-\]

-\begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of the homological quotient and fibre size]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}

-\[

-\end{proof}
