 \begin{abstract}
-On the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ $2$-spheres, a nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups exactly when $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial, and the finite-group characterization does not transfer to bare empirical models.
+For a stack, Giraud's component construction identifies the full substack
+over a global component section as its maximal component gerbe.  We apply
+this standard construction to a banded prestack lift of a presheaf on a
+finite site.  Under slice separatedness and terminal essential surjectivity,
+matching without amalgamation is equivalent to non-neutrality of every
+global component gerbe.  A representative-rigidity theorem shows that a
+strictly pullback-stable choice of lift representatives forces terminal
+effectivity when the band has vanishing first cohomology.  On a finite good
+cover with connected nonempty intersections and $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$, we
+give a self-contained Cech-cocycle prestack construction simultaneously
+controlling the component presheaf, terminal fibre, neutral labels, and
+prescribed evaluation maps $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$.  UCT and elementary
+subgroup arithmetic yield the aggregate quotients.  For the selected
+open-star sites of $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, a nonzero finite abelian group
+$G$ occurs as the two-component comparison kernel with complementary nonzero
+images exactly when $d(G)\le2\beta$ and $G$ is not cyclic of prime-power
+order.  This is a realization corollary for supplied lift data and does not
+transfer to bare empirical models.
 \end{abstract}

+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v]\text{ is neutral}
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v](a)\ne\varnothing.
+      \]
+\item Suppose \(\Phi:\mathfrak E\to\mathfrak E'\) is a banded equivalence,
+      its band map is \(\theta:\mathscr A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr A'\),
+      and its component map carries \(v\) to \(v'\).  Then \(\Phi\)
+      restricts to a banded equivalence
+      \(\mathfrak E[v]\simeq\mathfrak E'[v']\), and
+      \[
+      \theta_*[\mathfrak E[v]]=[\mathfrak E'[v']].
+      \]
 \end{enumerate}
-
-When a statement compares global component sections with the strict predicate

-it separately assumes that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice.
-Without this separatedness assumption global component sections are only

-\begin{remark}[\v{C}ech versus derived cohomology]\label{rem:cech-vs-derived}
-Hypothesis \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, equivalently the hypothesis of
-\Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}, is the precise comparison
-assumption governing the passage between \v{C}ech and derived $H^2$. It
-requires the comparison isomorphism itself; acyclicity in positive degrees is
-one standard sufficient Leray condition, not an unstated assumption unless
-explicitly invoked. Without this hypothesis, the component obstruction class lives in
-the filtered colimit
-\[
-\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)} \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band),
-\]
-and the non-neutrality statement in \Cref{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction} is purely \v{C}ech-theoretic. With \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, this colimit is canonically identified with the derived $H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$, and the obstruction class $\omega_v$ is an element of derived cohomology. All theorems in this subsection state explicitly whether they use only the \v{C}ech-level data or additionally require the comparison isomorphism.
-\end{remark}

-\begin{remark}[Relation to the companion paper]

-\begin{lemma}[Equivalence data and component transport]\label{lem:extension-equivalence-component-transport}

+Clause (i) is precisely the component-gerbe construction of

-\begin{lemma}[Transport of Giraud classes under banded equivalence]\label{lem:giraud-class-transport}
-Let $\mathfrak G$ be a $\Band$-banded gerbe and let $\mathfrak G'$ be a $\Band'$-banded gerbe on the same site $\mathcal C$. Suppose
-\[
-\Phi:\mathfrak G\to\mathfrak G'
-\]
-is an equivalence of stacks whose induced maps on automorphism sheaves identify the bands through an isomorphism
-\[
-\theta:\Band\xrightarrow{\sim}\Band'.
-\]
-Then
-\[
-\theta_*[\mathfrak G]=[\mathfrak G']
-\qquad\text{in}\qquad
-H^2(\mathcal C,\Band').
-\]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Choose a cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ which locally trivializes $\mathfrak G$, objects $x_i\in\mathfrak G(U_i)$, and descent isomorphisms
-\[
-\varphi_{ij}:x_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j|_{U_{ij}}.
-\]
-The usual Giraud cocycle $c_{ijk}\in\Band(U_{ijk})$ is defined by
-\[
-\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=c_{ijk}\in\operatorname{Aut}(x_i|_{U_{ijk}})\cong\Band(U_{ijk}).
-\]
-Applying $\Phi$ gives local lift objects $\Phi(x_i)$ of $\mathfrak G'$ and comparison isomorphisms $\Phi(\varphi_{ij})$. The corresponding defect is
-\[
-\Phi(\varphi_{ik})^{-1}\Phi(\varphi_{jk})\Phi(\varphi_{ij})
-=
-\Phi(c_{ijk}),
-\]
-which is identified with $\theta(c_{ijk})$ under the band isomorphism. Thus the transported local trivialization of $\mathfrak G'$ has cocycle $\theta_*(c)$. Refining the cover or changing the local lift objects changes both cocycles by the corresponding coboundary, exactly as in the standard local-trivialization classification of banded gerbes \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}. Hence the cohomology class of $\mathfrak G'$ is $\theta_*[\mathfrak G]$.
-
-The functoriality invoked here is the usual naturality of Giraud's classification with respect to a morphism of bands. Equivalently, the assignment
-\[
-(\mathfrak G,\Band)\longmapsto [\mathfrak G]\in H^2(\mathcal C,\Band)
-\]
-is functorial for banded equivalences: an equivalence of gerbes whose automorphism sheaves are identified by $\theta$ transports a local descent-defect cocycle to its pointwise image under $\theta$, and this construction is independent of all choices after passage to cohomology.
+The classification of abelian-banded gerbes identifies equivalence classes
+with \(H^2\), with the neutral gerbes representing zero
+\cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}.  On a site with terminal object \(a\), neutrality
+is exactly existence of an object over \(a\), proving (ii).  For (iii), the
+component compatibility makes \(\Phi\) restrict to the full component
+substacks.  Applying \(\Phi\) to local objects and overlap arrows applies
+\(\theta\) to their triple-overlap defect cocycle.  This is the standard
+naturality of Giraud classification under a banded equivalence
+\cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
 \end{proof}

+\begin{theorem}[Presheaf-to-component-gerbe comparison criterion]
+\label{thm:gerbe-null-semantics}

+ \operatorname{Match}(F,a)&(aF)(a)\ne\varnothing

+ \quad\text{(terminal essential surjectivity)},\\[2mm]

-\begin{theorem}[Supporting component gerbes of global component sections]\label{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}
-In the pullback-based setting of \Cref{def:component-gerbes}, and using only the banded groupoid lift and component data fixed there, every global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ determines a full substack $\mathfrak G_v\subseteq \mathfrak L_r$ that is a banded $\Band$-gerbe over $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. In particular, neither essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ nor the derived comparison hypothesis \textup{(H4)} is used here.
 \end{theorem}
 
 \begin{proof}
-By \suppresult{Components of the stackification}, the stackification
-\[
-\mathfrak E_r:=\mathfrak L_r
-\]
-is a $\Band$-banded stack lift of the component sheaf of
-$a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$. The global component section $v$ is a section of
-\[
-\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong (a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(a),
-\]
-and the full substack
-\[
-\mathfrak G_v(U)=
-\{x\in\mathfrak L_r(U)\mid [x]\ \text{restricts to}\ v|_U\}
-\]
-is therefore exactly the $v$-component substack
-$\mathfrak E_r[v]$ of \Cref{def:banded-stack-lift}.
+By \Cref{prop:finite-site-semantic-interface}(i), matching is equivalent to
+\((aF)(a)\ne\varnothing\).  By clause (ii) of that proposition and terminal
+essential surjectivity, \(F(a)\ne\varnothing\) is equivalent to
+\(\mathfrak L(a)\ne\varnothing\).  The latter holds exactly when one of the
+full components \(\mathfrak G_v\) contains an object over \(a\).  By
+\Cref{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package}(ii), this is equivalent to
+neutrality of at least one component gerbe.  Negating that statement while
+retaining nonemptiness of \((aF)(a)\) proves
+\eqref{eq:matching-gerbe-criterion}; the cohomological form follows from the
+same standard package.
+\end{proof}
 
-We recall why this is a gerbe. Because $\mathfrak L_r$ is a stack in
-groupoids, every descent datum for objects whose component lies over

-$\mathfrak G_v$ is a full substack. Local nonemptiness follows from the
-definition of a global component section as a section of the sheaf of connected
-components: after passing to a cover of any object $U$, the section

-is the local form of equality in the component sheaf: if two objects of
-$\mathfrak G_v(U)$ have component $v|_U$, then they become isomorphic
-after a cover of $U$. Fullness is built into the definition of
-$\mathfrak G_v$, so no morphisms between objects in the component are
-discarded. Finally, for every object $x$ of $\mathfrak G_v(U)$, the
-automorphism sheaf of $x$ inside $\mathfrak G_v$ is the same as its
-automorphism sheaf inside $\mathfrak L_r$, and this sheaf is identified
-with $\Band|_{\mathcal C_a/U}$ by the banding of the groupoid lift
-prestack and its stackification. Thus $\mathfrak G_v$ is a
-$\Band$-banded gerbe.
+The criterion is a site-theoretic reformulation of the meet-semilattice
+comparison in the companion manuscript

-\begin{theorem}[\v{C}ech obstruction of a component gerbe on an acyclic cover]\label{thm:cech-component-gerbe-obstruction}

+\begin{theorem}[Terminal rigidity for representative-rigid lifts]
+\label{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}

+representative-rigid \(\mathscr A\)-banded prestack lift of \(F\).  Write
+\(u:F\to aF\) and \(\iota:\mathfrak P\to\mathfrak L=a(\mathfrak P)\).

-\begin{definition}[Presentation-comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
-For finite nerve representatives of a fixed component obstruction class, an
-\emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
-\Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
-cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
-The \emph{presentation-comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
-objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
-morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
-presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
-component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
-zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
-between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
-hypothesis is imposed.
-\end{definition}

-\begin{proof}
-For every character $\chi:A\to\mathbb T$, naturality of the universal coefficient sequence gives a commutative square
+Fix a finite simplicial complex \(N\), a finite abelian group \(A\), and a
+class \(\omega\in H^2(N,A)\).  The universal coefficient map is denoted by
 \[
-\begin{CD}
-H^2(N(\mathcal U),A) @>\eta_A>> \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A) \\
-@V\chi_*VV @VV(\chi\circ -)V \\
-H^2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb T) @>\eta_{\mathbb T}>> \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),\mathbb T).
-\end{CD}
-\]
-Since $\mathbb T$ is divisible and hence injective in $\mathbf{Ab}$, one has
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),\mathbb T)=0
-\]
-\cite[Sec.~2.3]{Weibel1994}. Thus $\eta_{\mathbb T}$ is an isomorphism by \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}. Therefore
-\[
-\chi_*(\omega)=0
-\Longleftrightarrow
-\eta_{\mathbb T}(\chi_*(\omega))=0
-\Longleftrightarrow
-\chi\circ \eta_A(\omega)=0
-\Longleftrightarrow
-\chi\circ \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0.
-\]
-This proves the first displayed identity, and the second is simply the definition of the annihilator of a subgroup of $A$.
-
-Let $H:=K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})\le A$. By the first part of the proof, $X_{\omega}=\mathrm{Ann}(H)$. Finite abelian duality implies
-\[
-\bigcap_{\chi\in \mathrm{Ann}(H)}\ker\chi=H
-\]
-\cite[Part~I, Chaps.~2, 12]{Terras1999}. Hence
-\[
-K_{\omega}
-=
-\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi.
-\]
-The final isomorphism follows immediately:
-\[
-Q_{\omega}
-=
-A/K_{\omega}
-\cong
-A\Big/\!\bigcap_{\chi\in X_{\omega}}\ker\chi.
-\qedhere
-\]
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Character detection of the homological cokernel]\label{cor:intrinsic-character-detection}
-The quotient map
-\[
-\pi_{\omega}:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_{\omega}
-\]
-induces a natural isomorphism
-\[
-\widehat{Q_{\omega}}\cong X_{\omega}.
-\]
-For elements $x,y\in A$, one has
-\[
-\pi_{\omega}(x)=\pi_{\omega}(y)
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\chi(x)=\chi(y)\ \text{for every class-trivializing }\chi.
-\]
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
-\[
-X_{\omega}=\mathrm{Ann}(K_{\omega})=K_{\omega}^{\perp}.
-\]
-Characters of $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ are exactly the characters of $A$ that kill $K_{\omega}$, so precomposition with $\pi_{\omega}$ identifies $\widehat{Q_{\omega}}$ with $X_{\omega}$. The separation statement follows from finite abelian duality applied to the finite group $Q_{\omega}$ \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Initiality among zero-evaluation quotients]\label{thm:intrinsic-pure-ext-initiality}
-In the finite nerve representative of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let
-\[
-\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow Q_\omega=A/K_\omega
-\]
-be the homological cokernel. For every surjective homomorphism $q:A\twoheadrightarrow B$, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $q$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$;
-\item $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)=K_\omega$;
-\item $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$;
-\item $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
-\]
-of the universal coefficient sequence.
-\end{enumerate}
-Thus $Q_\omega$ is initial among coefficient quotients for which the pushed-forward obstruction has zero $H_2$ evaluation. This is the pullback-site, finite-nerve form of the companion initiality theorem \cite[Theorem~6.13]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure}.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is the universal property of the quotient
-\[
-\pi_\omega:A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_\omega.
-\]
-Indeed, a homomorphism $q:A\to B$ factors uniquely through $\pi_\omega$ if and only if $K_\omega\subseteq\ker q$, which is exactly the assertion that $q$ kills $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)$.
-
-For \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)}, use naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the coefficient homomorphism $q$. The naturality square gives
-\[
-\eta_B(q_*\omega)=q\circ \eta_A(\omega)=q\circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega.
-\]
-Thus $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q$ vanishes on the image of $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$, namely on $K_\omega$.
-
-Finally, the universal coefficient exact sequence for the finite nerve is
-\[
-0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),B)
-\xrightarrow{\eta_B}
-\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),B)
-\to 0.
-\]
-Therefore $\eta_B(q_*\omega)=0$ if and only if $q_*(\omega)$ lies in the kernel of $\eta_B$, which is precisely the displayed UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ subgroup. This proves all equivalences and the initiality statement.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{remark}[Presentation-relative invariance without a canonical splitting]\label{rem:no-canonical-splitting}
-For a fixed finite nerve representative, the quotient
-$Q_{\omega}$ and the subgroup
-$K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$ are invariants of the chosen
-presentation. Across comparison-equivalent presentations they are transported
-functorially only along chosen morphisms in the presentation-comparison
-groupoid, as in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}; different zigzags
-with the same endpoints may carry different coefficient automorphisms. By
-contrast, the universal coefficient sequence need not split canonically. Thus
-the theory isolates a homological cokernel and homological image subgroup
-at each presentation, with comparison-zigzag functoriality, without requiring
-any noncanonical decomposition of $\omega$ into $H_2$-evaluated and UCT-Ext
-summands.
-\end{remark}

+\begin{equation}\label{eq:homological-image-cokernel}

-\begin{definition}[Chain-level evaluation of a presentation]\label{def:chain-level-evaluation}
-Let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of the class $\omega$. Write
-\[
-C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
-\]
-for the simplicial group of integral $2$-chains on the finite nerve. The \emph{chain-level evaluation map} of $\alpha$ is the homomorphism
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
-\]
-defined by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices:
-\[
-\widetilde\alpha\!\left(\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\sigma\right)
-:=
-\sum_{\sigma} n_{\sigma}\alpha(\sigma).
-\]
-\end{definition}
+For a finite family of component classes
+\((\omega_v)_{v\in V}\), put \(K_v=K_{\omega_v}\) and define
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-quotients}
+ Q_{\mathrm{lab}}:=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v,
+ \qquad
+ Q_{\mathrm{com}}:=A\Big/\sum_{v\in V}K_v.
+\end{equation}
+The first quotient retains enough information to map to every componentwise
+quotient \(A/K_v\).  The second retains only characters which descend through
+every one of them.
 
-\begin{proposition}[Chain-coordinate versus homology-evaluation quotient]\label{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:chain-level-evaluation}, the following hold.
+\begin{proposition}[UCT and aggregate subgroup package]
+\label{prop:uct-aggregate-package}
+With the notation above:
 \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $\widetilde\alpha$ vanishes on $2$-boundaries and therefore induces a homomorphism
-\[
-\overline\alpha:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A.
-\]
-\item The induced homomorphism $\overline\alpha$ is exactly the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.
-\item The strict coordinate-image subgroup and the presentation-relative homological image subgroup satisfy
-\[
-H_\alpha=\mathrm{Im}(\widetilde\alpha),
-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\overline\alpha)=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)).
-\]
+\item The universal coefficient sequence is
+      \[
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow H^2(N,A)
+      \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}
+      \operatorname{Hom}(H_2(N,\mathbb Z),A)
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \]
+      Thus \(K_\omega=0\) exactly when \(\omega\) lies in the displayed
+      Ext subgroup.  In particular, nonzero classes can have zero
+      homological image when \(H_1\) has torsion.
+\item The quotient map \(q_\omega:A\to Q_\omega\) is initial among group
+      homomorphisms \(q:A\to B\) satisfying
+      \(q\circ\operatorname{ev}_\omega=0\).  A character
+      \(\chi:A\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) factors through \(Q_\omega\)
+      exactly when \(\chi(K_\omega)=0\).  Since finite Pontryagin duality
+      separates points,
+      \[
+      K_\omega=\mathop{\bigcap}_{\chi(K_\omega)=0}\ker\chi.
+      \]
+\item For a nonempty finite family \((K_v)_{v\in V}\), there is a natural
+      short exact sequence
+      \begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence}
+      0\longrightarrow
+      \frac{\sum_vK_v}{\bigcap_vK_v}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{lab}}
+      \longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{com}}
+      \longrightarrow0.
+      \end{equation}
+      Moreover,
+      \[
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{com}}}
+      \cong\bigcap_{v\in V}K_v^\perp,
+      \qquad
+      \widehat{Q_{\mathrm{lab}}}
+      \cong\sum_{v\in V}K_v^\perp
+      \]
+      inside \(\widehat A\).
+\item If \(H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0\) and
+      \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), a subgroup
+      \(K\le A\) occurs as \(K_\omega\) exactly when \(d(K)\le\beta\).
+      Every finite family of such subgroups is simultaneously attained by
+      the prestack of
+      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}.
 \end{enumerate}
-Thus the gap between chain-coordinate quotient and homology-evaluation quotient is exactly the gap between the image of the cocycle on all $2$-chains and its image on $2$-cycles.
 \end{proposition}

-\begin{corollary}[Coincidence of the chain-coordinate and homology-evaluation quotients]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-coincidence-criterion}
-Let $\alpha$ be a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative of $\omega$. The following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $A/H_\alpha\cong Q_{\omega}$;
-\item $H_\alpha=K_{\omega}$;
-\item $\widetilde\alpha(C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))=\widetilde\alpha(Z_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z))$.
-\end{enumerate}
-Equivalently, the chain-coordinate quotient agrees with the homology-evaluation quotient exactly when every value of the cocycle on a $2$-chain already occurs on a $2$-cycle.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is immediate from the quotient descriptions
+which proves exactness.  For finite abelian groups, annihilators exchange sums and
+intersections:

-\qquad\text{and}\qquad
-Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}.
+ \Big(\sum_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\bigcap_vK_v^\perp,
+ \qquad
+ \Big(\bigcap_vK_v\Big)^\perp=\sum_vK_v^\perp.

-The equivalence of \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} is exactly \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}(iii).

-\begin{theorem}[Nonzero UCT-Ext classes and vanishing $H_2$ evaluation]\label{thm:character-blind-obstructions}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, with a chosen admissible
-parameter, global component section, banded groupoid lift, trivialized constant finite
-abelian band $A$, and the \textup{(H4)} comparison datum needed to regard
-$\omega$ as a derived component class, the following are equivalent:
-\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
-\item $K_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $Q_{\omega}=A$;
-\item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$;
-\item $\omega$ lies in the subgroup
+Under the hypotheses of (iv), the Ext term vanishes and UCT becomes
 \[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\subseteq H^2(N(\mathcal U),A).
+ H^2(N,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z^\beta,A).
 \]
-\end{enumerate}
-If these conditions hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then the chosen component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral, while every character of $A$ is class-trivializing for that component class. If, in addition, the banded groupoid lift is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre, \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice, and $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, then
+The image of a homomorphism from \(\mathbb Z^\beta\) is generated by the
+images of the standard basis, so it has at most \(\beta\) generators.
+Conversely, given generators \(k_1,\dots,k_\beta\) of \(K\), allowing zeros
+when fewer are needed, the map
 \[
-M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r).
+ (n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto\sum_jn_jk_j
 \]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}

-\[
-K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}),
-\]
-so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(iii)} are equivalent. Since $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$, conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. Hence all four conditions are equivalent.
-
-If they hold and $\omega\neq 0$, then \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} shows that the component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is non-neutral.
-On the other hand, $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0$ implies

-for every $\chi\in\widehat A$, so \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} shows that every character is class-trivializing.
-
-Assume now that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice and that $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$. Since the chosen global component section $v$ exists, \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches} gives

-\[

-\[

-\begin{corollary}[Vanishing evaluation when $H_2=0$]\label{cor:h2-vanishing-blindness}

-\begin{corollary}[No nonzero classes with vanishing $H_2$ evaluation when $H_1$ is free]\label{cor:h1-free-no-blindness}
-Assume that $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian. Then
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\omega=0.
-\]
-Equivalently, every nonzero component obstruction class has nonzero $H_2$ evaluation. In particular, if $|\Vis_{p,s}(r)|=1$, every nonzero component obstruction class on such a nerve produces a proper homological cokernel.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-If $H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is free abelian, then
-\[
-\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)=0.
-\]
-Hence the universal coefficient map $\eta_A$ is injective. By \Cref{thm:character-blind-obstructions},
-\[
-K_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=0
-\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\eta_A(\omega)=0.
-\]
-Injectivity of $\eta_A$ therefore gives $K_{\omega}=0$ if and only if $\omega=0$. If $\omega\neq 0$, then $K_{\omega}\neq 0$, so $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$ is a proper quotient of the finite group $A$.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{example}[A single-component surjective-homological-evaluation class on $S^2$]\label{ex:s2-single-branch-maximal-collapse}

-\begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the homological quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
-An \emph{auxiliary register for the homological quotient} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
-\[

-\]
-such that
-\[
-\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.

-\end{definition}

-\begin{corollary}[Fibre size of the homological quotient]\label{cor:intrinsic-hidden-state-lower-bound}
-Every auxiliary register for the homological quotient satisfies
-\[
-|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|.
-\]
-Equivalently,
-\[
-\log_2|R|\ge \log_2|K_{\omega}|.
-\]
-This lower bound is sharp.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, the fibres of $\pi_{\omega}$ are exactly the cosets of $K_{\omega}$, so every fibre has cardinality $|K_{\omega}|$. The same fibre-counting argument as in \suppresult{Fibre size of an auxiliary register} therefore shows that any auxiliary register preserving the first projection must satisfy $|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|$.
-
-For sharpness, take $R:=K_{\omega}$ and choose a set-theoretic section $s_{\omega}:Q_{\omega}\to A$ of $\pi_{\omega}$. Then
-\[
-\iota_{\omega}(x):=\bigl(\pi_{\omega}(x),x-s_{\omega}(\pi_{\omega}(x))\bigr)
-\]
-is injective.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of the homological quotient and fibre size]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}

-\[

-\]
-Let $\omega_p\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A_{(p)})$ be the image of $\omega$ under the projection onto the $p$-primary summand. Then
-\[

-\qquad
-K_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
-\qquad

-\]

-\[

-\[

-\[

-=

-\[

-=
-A/K_{\omega}
-\cong

-\]
-Since finite direct sums correspond to products of cardinalities, the logarithmic fibre-cardinality formula is immediate.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{corollary}[Surjective homological evaluation]\label{cor:maximal-collapse}
-In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, the following are equivalent:

+cardinality of an unrestricted auxiliary set capable of separating every

 \[

+ |q_\omega^{-1}(\bar a)|=|K_\omega|,

-\begin{proof}

+A stack in groupoids has a sheaf of connected components.  A global section
+of that sheaf need not be represented by a global object of the stack, but it

+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  The component is represented by a
+global object precisely when its gerbe is neutral, or equivalently when its
+Giraud \(H^2\)-class vanishes.  These classical facts are the starting point
+of the article.
+
+Our setting is deliberately finite and presentation-relative.  We fix a site
+with terminal object, a presheaf \(F\), an abelian-banded prestack lift
+\(\mathfrak P\), and its stackification \(\mathfrak L\).  The connected
+components of \(\mathfrak P\) recover \(F\), while those of

-The exact sequence and its finite-register interpretation are formal.  The
-existence results are not: on the finite intersection site associated to a
-connected good-cover nerve with $H_1=0$, we construct typed expansions whose
-componentwise evaluation maps have prescribed images, including mixtures of
-neutral and non-neutral component gerbes.  If $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong

-by at most $\beta$ elements.  The main classification follows by asking when
-$G$ decomposes as $K_1\oplus K_2$ with both summands nonzero and each generated
-by at most $\beta$ elements.
+The proof combines the prescribed-image prestack with the elementary fact
+that the indecomposable finite abelian groups are the cyclic prime-power
+groups.  It is not a classification attached to an arbitrary space,
+presentation, or empirical model.

+\subsection*{Organization}
 
-\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=2em,labelindent=0pt]
-\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
-A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
-\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
-$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
-$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
-\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
-The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
-satisfaction.
-\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
-An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
-the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
-is not part of the definition.
-\item[Typed expansion class.]
-The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
-fixed lower model.
-\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
-An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
-exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
-are attached to $r$.
-\item[{Base object $a=[r]_p$.}]
-The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
-the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
-\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
-The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
-specified pretopology and pullbacks.
-\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
-The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
-\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
-A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
-\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
-A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
-terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
-hypothesis.
-\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
-A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
-strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
-\item[Global component section $v$.]
-An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
-$(aF)(a)$.
-\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
-The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
-$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
-\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
-The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
-replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
-zigzags need not give the same comparison.
-\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
-For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
-and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
-\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
-$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
-$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
-\item[Label-aware quotient.]
-$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
-componentwise homological cokernels.
-\item[Common-character quotient.]
-$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
-\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
-The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
-common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
-\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
-A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
-cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
-\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
-The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
-the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
-\item[Typed readout.]
-The partial output attached to an admissible parameter: inadmissible if no
-typed data are attached, uniquely determined if the sheafified global section
-is unique, and non-unique-or-absent otherwise.
-\item[Indexed refinement system.]
-A family of state-refinement relations indexed by information coordinates,
-each monotone for the state preorder and the specified time order.
-\item[Information-determining axis set.]
-A finite set of refinement coordinates whose information values determine any
-decided truth value among the states reachable along those coordinates.
-\item[Pairwise commuting refinements and common refinement.]
-Refinements for which every indicated finite family has a state refining all
-its members.
-\item[Readout-preserving rewrite.]
-A rewrite between partial outputs that preserves both definedness and value.
-\item[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf.]
-A category fibred in groupoids whose presheaf of isomorphism classes is the
-given empirical-model support presheaf and whose automorphism sheaves are the
-specified band.
-\end{description}
+Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the minimal presheaf and prestack
+interface.  Section~\ref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} records the standard Giraud
+component package, proves the comparison criterion, and gives the full
+terminal-rigidity proof.  Section~\ref{sec:homological-visibility} proves the
+connected-overlap, basis-site, and derived comparisons before constructing
+the prescribed finite-label prestack.  Section~\ref{sec:homological-images}
+collects the UCT and aggregate consequences.  The wedge application and the

+\ref{sec:empirical-boundary}.  The separately compiled technical appendix
+contains only presentation bookkeeping, extended examples, and the narrow
+lower-language boundary argument; the proofs needed to certify the principal
+claims are all contained here.

\section{The wedge-of-spheres realization corollary}
\label{sec:wedge-application}

Fix \(\beta\ge1\), and let \(K_\beta\) be a finite connected simplicial
complex with
\[
 |K_\beta|\simeq\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2.
\]
For each \(m\ge0\), take the open-star cover of
\(\operatorname{Sd}^mK_\beta\), and let \(\mathcal B_\beta\) be the
all-subdivision basis site of
\Cref{prop:finite-site-comparison}(iii).  Every nonempty finite overlap is
contractible, hence connected, and the coherent coefficient trivializations
are those of the genuine constant sheaf.  Thus the hypothesis omitted by an
ordinary-nerve formulation with disconnected overlaps is satisfied here.

For two component classes with homological images \(K_1,K_2\le G\), the
kernel of the aggregate comparison is, by
\eqref{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence},
\[
 \frac{K_1+K_2}{K_1\cap K_2}.
\]
We ask when the selected realization construction makes this kernel equal to
the band itself by requiring
\begin{equation}\label{eq:complementary-images}
 K_1\cap K_2=0,
 \qquad K_1+K_2=G,
 \qquad K_1,K_2\ne0.
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}[Two-component realization on a wedge of \(2\)-spheres]
\label{thm:wedge-sphere-two-component-label-loss}
Let \(G\) be a finite abelian group and let \(d(G)\) be its minimal number
of generators.  The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item \(G\ne0\), \(d(G)\le2\beta\), and \(G\) is not cyclic of
      prime-power order;
\item on one of the selected finite open-star covers in
      \(\mathcal B_\beta\), the prestack construction of
      \Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction} has two non-neutral
      component gerbes whose homological images satisfy
      \eqref{eq:complementary-images}.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold,
\[
 Q_{\mathrm{lab}}\cong G,
 \qquad Q_{\mathrm{com}}=0,
 \qquad
 \ker(Q_{\mathrm{lab}}\to Q_{\mathrm{com}})\cong G,
\]
and the constructed component presheaf has matching without amalgamation.
The assertion is relative to this selected finite-site realization; it is not
a presentation-independent classification of gerbes or finite abelian groups.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every selected cover, the nerve is a barycentric subdivision of
\(K_\beta\).  The nerve and basis-site comparisons of
\Cref{prop:finite-site-comparison} give
\[
 H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
 \qquad
 H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta,
\]
and identify the finite Cech representatives with the corresponding derived
classes on \(\mathcal B_\beta\).

Assume (ii).  By \Cref{prop:uct-aggregate-package}(iv), each \(K_i\) is
generated by at most \(\beta\) elements.  The complementary-image equations
give
\[
 G=K_1\oplus K_2.
\]
Hence \(d(G)\le d(K_1)+d(K_2)\le2\beta\).  Since both summands are nonzero,
\(G\) is decomposable.  The indecomposable finite abelian groups are exactly
the cyclic groups of prime-power order \cite[Chap.~12]{DummitFoote2004}, so
(i) follows.

Conversely, suppose (i).  If \(d(G)=r\ge2\), choose an invariant-factor
decomposition
\[
 G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r},
 \qquad n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r,
\]
and let \(t=\min\{\beta,r-1\}\).  Put
\[
 K_1=C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_t},
 \qquad
 K_2=C_{n_{t+1}}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}.
\]
Both groups are nonzero.  We have \(d(K_1)\le\beta\), while
\(d(K_2)=r-t\le\beta\) because \(r\le2\beta\).

If \(d(G)=1\), then \(G\) is cyclic.  Its order is not a prime power, so it
has coprime factors \(a,b>1\).  The Chinese remainder theorem gives
\[
 G\cong C_a\oplus C_b.
\]
Taking \(K_1=C_a\) and \(K_2=C_b\) again gives two nonzero summands, each
generated by one element.  Thus in either case
\(G=K_1\oplus K_2\), with \(d(K_i)\le\beta\).

Choose homomorphisms
\[
 \phi_i:\mathbb Z^\beta\longrightarrow G
\]
with images \(K_i\), and transport them across
\(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\).  The finite-site realization
theorem, with label set \(\{1,2\}\), produces the two component gerbes and
their prescribed images.  Both maps are nonzero, so both gerbes are
non-neutral and the component presheaf has matching without amalgamation.
Finally, \eqref{eq:aggregate-quotients} and
\eqref{eq:aggregate-exact-sequence} give the three displayed quotient
identities.
\end{proof}

For \(\beta=1\), the statement says that a nonzero finite abelian group is
attained in this two-component manner precisely when it splits as a direct
sum of two nonzero cyclic groups.  This includes cyclic groups whose orders
have at least two distinct prime divisors and noncyclic two-generated groups,
but excludes every cyclic \(p\)-group.  This small case illustrates that the
criterion is the sharp arithmetic endpoint of the chosen realization, not a
new structural theorem about finite abelian groups.

\section{Boundary with empirical-model obstructions}
\label{sec:empirical-boundary}

Let \(X\) be a finite set of measurements, let \(O_x\) be a finite nonempty
outcome set for each \(x\in X\), and let \(\mathcal M\) be a finite antichain
of contexts covering \(X\).  For a finite empirical model \(e\), write
\[
 S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
\]
for its support presheaf on the downward-closed context category.  Adjoin a
terminal object \(X\), declare \(\mathcal M\) to cover it, and set
\[
 \widehat S_e(X)=\varprojlim_{U}S_e(U).
\]
Thus \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is the set of compatible supported local
assignments.  Let \(aS_e\) be the associated sheaf on this terminally
augmented context site.

\begin{theorem}[Empirical-model boundary]
\label{thm:empirical-model-boundary}
For every finite empirical model \(e\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item compatible supported families, globally supported assignments, global
      sections in the Abramsky--Brandenburger sense, and elements of
      \(\widehat S_e(X)\cong(aS_e)(X)\) are naturally the same set.  Hence
      strong contextuality is absence of a matching family at this
      set-valued level, not matching without amalgamation;
\item for every supplied abelian sheaf \(\mathscr A\),
      \[
      \operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\mathscr A
      \]
      is a canonical split \(\mathscr A\)-banded stack lift of \(aS_e\),
      and every one of its component gerbes is neutral;
\item the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction attached to
      \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) is a relative class
      \[
      \gamma_e(s)\in
      \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}),
      \]
      equivalently a torsor class.  It is not the Giraud \(H^2\)-class of a
      component gerbe.  There can be no construction recovering all such
      classes from a component-section map with component sheaf \(aS_e\):
      for a strongly contextual model the latter map has empty domain
      \((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), whereas the AMB classes remain indexed by
      local sections;
\item the homological images and the two-component criterion of
      \Cref{thm:wedge-sphere-two-component-label-loss} apply to an empirical
      model only after a band and a non-split banded prestack lift have been
      supplied as additional data.  They are not invariants of a bare
      empirical model.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The event presheaf
\(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf.  A compatible family
\((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\), with \(s_C\in S_e(C)\), therefore glues
uniquely to an assignment \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\), and its restrictions
lie in the stated supports.  Conversely, restricting such an assignment
gives the compatible family.  The terminal right Kan extension is the same
limit by definition, and the plus construction on the cover
\(\mathcal M\to X\) gives the same set in \((aS_e)(X)\).  This proves (i)
and agrees with the standard support formulation of contextuality
\cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}.

The discrete-groupoid functor sends a sheaf of sets to a stack with that
component sheaf and zero automorphism sheaves.  The classifying stack
\(\mathsf B\mathscr A\) has one component and automorphism sheaf
\(\mathscr A\).  Their product is therefore a split banded lift of
\(aS_e\).  In each component, the identity \(\mathscr A\)-torsor is a
global object, so the component gerbe is neutral and its Giraud class is
zero.  This proves (ii).

Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa apply the free-abelian presheaf
\(\mathcal F_e=\mathbb Z[S_e]\) and a relative kernel presheaf to obtain
the displayed degree-one Cech class
\cite[Sec.~4]{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}.  Car\`u identifies this
class with an appropriate torsor trivialized by the measurement cover
\cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}.  By contrast, the map in
\Cref{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package} is indexed by global sections
of the component sheaf and takes values in derived \(H^2\) of a sheaf band.
If \(e\) is strongly contextual, (i) gives
\((aS_e)(X)=\varnothing\), so every such component-section map has empty
domain.  Local sections \(s\in S_e(C_0)\) can still exist and index AMB
classes.  This degree and indexing mismatch proves (iii).

Finally, the canonical lift in (ii) has zero component classes and zero
homological image subgroups.  A non-split lift, a finite good-cover nerve,
and prescribed maps \(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\) are additional inputs to
\Cref{thm:prescribed-component-image-construction}; none is selected by the
support presheaf of a bare empirical model.  This proves (iv).
\end{proof}

The theorem concerns possibilistic support.  Probabilistic
noncontextuality asks for a distribution on the global assignment set with
the given marginals, a different extension problem which is not determined
by \(S_e\).  This distinction is independent of the degree mismatch above.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

The article starts with supplied finite-site data: a presheaf, an
abelian-banded prestack lift, and its stackification.  Giraud's component
construction then assigns the maximal component gerbe to each global section
of the component sheaf.  The use made of this standard input is narrow: under
slice separatedness and terminal essential surjectivity it compares the
strict presheaf predicate of matching without amalgamation with non-neutrality
of every global component.  Representative-rigidity shows why a strictly
pullback-stable choice of lift representatives is too restrictive in the
basic \(H^1\)-vanishing regime.

On a finite good-cover site, the connected-overlap hypothesis is what permits
the ordinary nerve to carry the full constant-coefficient Cech complex.  The
all-subdivision basis comparison identifies the generated site with the
ordinary sheaf theory of the underlying polyhedron.  Within this fixed
setting, the standard Cech-cocycle gerbe construction can be packaged into a
single prestack whose component presheaf, terminal behavior, neutrality
pattern, and evaluation images are prescribed simultaneously.

UCT and elementary subgroup arithmetic then yield the aggregate quotients.
For the selected open-star covers of
\(\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2\), the two-component realization criterion is
\[
 d(G)\le2\beta
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 G\text{ is not cyclic of prime-power order}.
\]
This is a sharp corollary of the selected realization, not a new
classification principle for finite abelian groups or gerbes.

Bare empirical models provide only the support presheaf and its canonical
split stack, whose component gerbes are neutral.  Their relative degree-one
obstructions are indexed differently and are not recovered by the
component-section map.  A non-split banded lift must therefore be supplied
before the finite-site results apply.

No crossed-module comparison is pursued: the present arguments begin after a
gerbe \(H^2\)-class and its Cech representative are supplied, and contain
neither the source-side degree-three chain model nor the comparison cochain
required to derive such a class from crossed-module data.

4: Let \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\) be a finite open cover of a space
5: \(X\).  Its ordinary nerve \(N=N(\mathcal U)\) records which finite
6: intersections are nonempty.  In order to identify Cech cochains with one
7: copy of a coefficient group for each simplex of \(N\), we impose the
8: following hypothesis throughout this section:
9: \begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-overlap-hypothesis}
10:  \begin{minipage}{0.82\textwidth}
11:  every nonempty finite intersection \(U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j\) is
12:  connected, and the chosen trivializations of the locally constant
13:  coefficient sheaf identify \(\Gamma(U_J,\mathscr A)\) coherently with
14:  the same group \(A\).
15:  \end{minipage}
16: \end{equation}
17: Without connectedness,
18: \(\Gamma(U_J,\mathscr A)\cong A^{\pi_0(U_J)}\), whereas the ordinary nerve
19: retains only the information that \(U_J\) is nonempty.  Thus
20: \eqref{eq:connected-overlap-hypothesis} is essential for the ordinary-nerve
21: formulation below.  A component nerve or local coefficients would be needed
22: without it.
23: 
24: For a fixed cover satisfying \eqref{eq:connected-overlap-hypothesis}, define
25: the \emph{finite intersection site} \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\) as follows.
26: Its objects are a terminal object \(a\), one object \(U_J\) for every
27: nonempty simplex \(J\) of \(N\), and a strict initial object \(\varnothing\)
28: representing all empty intersections.  There is an arrow
29: \(U_J\to U_K\) when \(K\subseteq J\), and
30: \[
31:  U_J\times_{U_L}U_K=
32:  \begin{cases}
33:  U_{J\cup K},&J\cup K\in N,\\
34:  \varnothing,&J\cup K\notin N.
35:  \end{cases}
36: \]
37: The pretopology is generated by the vertex cover \(\{U_i\to a\}\), its
38: pullbacks, identity covers, and the empty cover of \(\varnothing\).  Let
39: \(A_{\mathcal U}\) be the restriction of the sheaf of locally constant
40: \(A\)-valued functions on \(X\).  Hence
41: \[
42:  A_{\mathcal U}(U_J)=A,
43:  \qquad A_{\mathcal U}(\varnothing)=0,
44: \]
45: under the coherent trivializations in
46: \eqref{eq:connected-overlap-hypothesis}.

48: \begin{proposition}[Connected-overlap and basis-site comparison]
49: \label{prop:finite-site-comparison}
50: Let \(A\) be an abelian group.
51: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
52: \item For a finite cover satisfying
53:       \eqref{eq:connected-overlap-hypothesis}, the ordered Cech complex of
54:       \(A_{\mathcal U}\) is naturally the simplicial cochain complex of the
55:       ordinary nerve:
56:       \[
57:       \check C^q(\mathcal U,A_{\mathcal U})
58:       \cong C^q(N,A).
59:       \]
60: \item If the nonempty intersections are also
61:       \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-acyclic, the Leray comparison gives
62:       \[
63:       H^q(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})
64:       \cong \check H^q(\mathcal U,A_{\mathcal U})
65:       \cong H^q(N,A).
66:       \]
67: \item Let \(K\) be a finite simplicial complex, put \(X=|K|\), and let
68:       \(\mathcal U^{(m)}\) be the open-star cover of
69:       \(\operatorname{Sd}^mK\).  The category \(\mathcal B_K\) of all open
70:       stars in these covers and all their finite intersections is a basis
71:       for \(X\), stable under finite intersections after adjoining the empty
72:       set.  The topology generated on \(\mathcal B_K\) is the induced
73:       open-cover topology, and restriction gives an equivalence
74:       \[
75:       \mathbf {Sh}(X)\simeq\mathbf {Sh}(\mathcal B_K).
76:       \]
77:       Under this equivalence the genuine constant sheaf on
78:       \(\mathcal B_K\) is the restriction of the ordinary constant sheaf on
79:       \(X\).  Every nonempty basic intersection is contractible, the covers
80:       \((\mathcal U^{(m)})_{m\ge0}\) are filtered and cofinal, and
81:       \[
82:       \varinjlim_m\check H^2(\mathcal U^{(m)},A)
83:       \cong H^2(X,A).
84:       \]
85: \end{enumerate}
86: \end{proposition}
87: 
88: \begin{proof}
89: For (i), an ordered Cech \(q\)-cochain assigns a section of
90: \(A_{\mathcal U}\) to each nonempty ordered \((q+1)\)-fold intersection.
91: Connectedness and the coherent trivializations identify that section group
92: with one copy of \(A\), and the restriction maps with the identity of
93: \(A\).  Empty intersections have section group zero.  The ordered Cech
94: coboundary is therefore exactly the alternating simplicial coboundary.
95: 
96: For (ii), the Cech-to-derived spectral sequence for \(\mathcal U\) has
97: \[
98:  E_1^{p,q}=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}
99:  H^q(U_{i_0\cdots i_p},A_{\mathcal U}).
100: \]
101: Acyclicity makes every row with \(q>0\) vanish, so the edge map is an
102: isomorphism.  Clause (i) identifies its remaining row with the nerve
103: cochain complex; this is the usual Leray theorem
104: \cite[Chap.~III, Sec.~4]{Bredon1997}.
105: 
106: For (iii), open stars in successive barycentric subdivisions have arbitrarily
107: small mesh.  Given \(x\in O\) with \(O\subseteq X\) open, a sufficiently
108: fine subdivision has a vertex whose open star contains \(x\) and lies in
109: \(O\).  Hence the union of all these stars is a basis.  Adding their finite
110: intersections makes it stable under intersections, and a family of basis
111: objects covers precisely when their union covers in \(X\).  Thus its
112: generated topology is the topology induced from the open-set site.
113: 
114: The Comparison Lemma for a basis stable under intersections now gives the
115: displayed equivalence of sheaf categories; explicitly, restriction is fully
116: faithful because sections are recovered by gluing over basis covers, and its
117: quasi-inverse sends a basis sheaf to the sheaf whose sections on an open set
118: are compatible basis-local sections.  This also shows directly that locally
119: constant \(A\)-valued functions restrict to the genuine constant sheaf used
120: on \(\mathcal B_K\) \cite[Chap.~III, Sec.~7]{MacLaneMoerdijk1994}.
121: 
122: A nonempty intersection of open stars is the open star of the simplex spanned
123: by the corresponding vertices, hence is contractible.  Barycentric
124: subdivision refines the preceding cover, and every finite basis cover is
125: refined by a sufficiently late subdivision cover; the sequence is therefore
126: filtered and cofinal.  The basic intersections are acyclic for the constant
127: sheaf, so (ii), the sheaf-category equivalence, and cofinality give
128: \[
129:  \varinjlim_m\check H^2(\mathcal U^{(m)},A)
130:  \cong H^2(\mathcal B_K,A)
131:  \cong H^2(X,A).
132: \]
133: This proves every asserted comparison, including the passage from the
134: all-subdivision generated site to the usual topological site.
135: \end{proof}

\subsection{Construction of prescribed component data}

The preceding algebra isolates the componentwise and aggregate quotients attached to a given family of homological image subgroups. The next theorem gives a converse existence statement on connected finite nerves with vanishing first homology. It is internal to the fixed finite-nerve framework of the paper: the nerve, the constant band, and the comparison data are fixed in advance, and the theorem constructs a presheaf and banded groupoid lift with the prescribed images.

The construction proofs use the following explicit typed-expansion
interface. The site is not an arbitrary full subcategory of intersections.
It is the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve of a finite good-cover presentation, so that
the cohomological comparison used later is an actual Leray comparison rather
than a declared comparison datum.

\begin{lemma}[Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion]\label{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}
Let
\[
\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
\]
be a finite cover whose nerve $N=N(\mathcal U)$ is the nerve of a good cover
of a paracompact space $X\simeq |N|$. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ be the
finite intersection site associated to this chosen good-cover model, defined
as follows. Its objects are $a$, one strict initial object $\emptyset$, and
one object $U_J$ for each nonempty simplex $J\in N$. A geometric-realization functor
from this formal category to open subsets of \(X\) sends \(a\) to \(X\),
\(\emptyset\) to the empty open set, and \(U_J\) to the corresponding
nonempty good-cover intersection. This is a pullback-complete finite intersection site,
not the full subcategory on only nonempty intersections. The same strict
initial object represents every empty finite intersection. Thus the only
finite subsets represented by named non-initial objects are the simplices
of \(N\), but a finite subset \(J\subseteq I\) which is not a simplex is
not discarded from the site-level pullback calculus; whenever such a
subset arises as a pullback intersection, the pullback is the
distinguished object \(\emptyset\). In formulas
we write
\[
\widetilde U_J:=
\begin{cases}
U_J,& J\in N,\\
\emptyset,& J\notin N.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus empty intersections are not omitted from the site: all of them are
identified with the same strict initial pullback object $\emptyset$, and
the open set corresponding to \(\widetilde U_J\) is the actual intersection
\(\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j\), possibly empty. The order is generated by
\[
\emptyset\to U_J\to U_K\to a
\qquad (K\subseteq J,\; J,K\in N).
\]
There is a unique arrow \(\emptyset\to W\) for every object \(W\), and no
non-initial object maps to \(\emptyset\).
For any two arrows $U_J\to U_L$ and $U_K\to U_L$ with
$L\subseteq J\cap K$, their fibre product is
\[
U_J\times_{U_L}U_K=\widetilde U_{J\cup K}.
\]
If $J\cup K\notin N$, this means that the fibre product is the strict
initial object $\emptyset$. Any fibre product in which one factor is
$\emptyset$ is also $\emptyset$. The pretopology is the smallest
pretopology for which the vertex cover \(\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\), all of
its pullbacks along arrows of the formal category, all identity covers,
and the empty cover of \(\emptyset\) are covers. Equivalently, it is
obtained by repeatedly applying pullback stability and transitivity to
the vertex cover inside the formal category just described. For example,
the pullback of the vertex cover along \(U_J\to a\) is the family of
arrows
\[
\{\widetilde U_{J\cup\{i\}}\to U_J\}_{i\in I},
\]
with the terms for non-simplices equal to \(\emptyset\). Repeated
occurrences of \(\emptyset\) in such a pulled-back family may be
identified with the same initial object. They are harmless in matching
conditions because the coefficient sheaves used below have zero value at
\(\emptyset\), but the corresponding pullback object is still present in
the site. In particular, disjoint cover members \(U_i,U_j\to a\) have the
pullback \(U_i\times_aU_j=\emptyset\) in the site. The empty object is
omitted only from the nonempty \v{C}ech nerve and from the displayed
nonzero cochain groups, never from the local-reference-site structure.
Every pullback demanded by \Cref{def:local-reference-frame} is therefore
an object of \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\), including the empty pullback
objects produced by disjoint members of a covering family.
Thus closure under the pretopology axioms is part of the definition, not a
consequence of omitting any empty pullback object. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ is a pullback-based reference-refinement site
with terminal object $a$; in particular, for every pair of cover members
$U_i,U_j\to a$, the fibre product is the formal object $U_{\{i,j\}}$ if
$\{i,j\}\in N$ and is the strict initial object $\emptyset$ otherwise;
\item the cover $\mathcal U$ remains a cover of $a$ in
$\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, all pullbacks of members of this cover exist
there, and its nonempty \v{C}ech nerve is the finite simplicial complex
$N$;
\item for every abelian group $A$, let $A_{\mathcal U}$ denote the genuine
constant sheaf
on \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\)
\[
A_{\mathcal U}(W)=\operatorname{LC}(|W|,A),
\]
where \(|W|\subseteq X\) is the open set represented by \(W\). This is the
restriction of the genuine constant sheaf of locally constant
\(A\)-valued functions on the chosen good-cover space. It is this
sheaf, not the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the abstract
index category, that is used as the band. With these coefficients the
\v{C}ech cochain complex of
$\mathcal U$ with coefficients in $A_{\mathcal U}$ and the finite nerve
presentation of any class in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ are the same finite
cochain data after replacing $\mathcal C_a$ with
$\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$. This is a cochain-level identification because
the cover is a chosen good cover: on connected nonempty basic
intersections \(A_{\mathcal U}\) has value \(A\), while on the strict
initial object it has value \(0\);
\item on the slice
\(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/U_J\) over every nonempty proper intersection
object, every cover of a nonempty object contains an identity, while the
empty cover forces every abelian sheaf to take value \(0\) at the strict
initial object. Consequently the abelian sheaf category on the slice is
equivalent to the presheaf category on its full nonempty subcategory.
Evaluation at the terminal object is therefore exact and
\[
H^q(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/U_J,A_{\mathcal U})=0
\qquad(q>0).
\]
Thus the vertex cover is \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-Leray for an entirely internal
finite-site reason, and the Cech-to-derived comparison gives a natural
isomorphism
\[
H^n(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U},A_{\mathcal U})\cong \check H^n(\mathcal U,A_{\mathcal U})\cong H^n(N,A)
\]
for all $n$, and the \v{C}ech cocycle on the vertex cover maps to the
corresponding derived cohomology class;
\item for every contravariant functor
\[
F:\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set},
\]
there is a one-state $\mathbb L_2$-model $M_2$ with state $p$ and a
distinguished admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ such that $[r]_p=a$, the
local slice site of $r$ is exactly $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, and the local
object functor on that slice site is $F$; this model is the admissible
$\mathbb L_2$-expansion supplied by
\artresult{Typed-expansion model-class interface for the layer chain};
\item if, in addition, a category fibred in groupoids
\[
\mathfrak P\to\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}
\]
with abelian sheaf band $\Band$ satisfies
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)\cong F
\]
and the automorphism-sheaf condition of
\Cref{def:banded-groupoid-lift}, then $M_2$ has an admissible
$\mathbb L_3$-expansion $M_3$ in which $r$ has banded groupoid lift
$\mathfrak P$, band $\Band$, and stackification $a(\mathfrak P)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The formal index category is thin and has terminal object $a$. We first
verify the pullbacks, since they are part of the local-reference-site
structure and not merely a convention about the \v{C}ech cochain complex.
Suppose that \(U_J\to U_L\) and \(U_K\to U_L\) are two maps, so
\(L\subseteq J\cap K\). If \(J\cup K\in N\), then \(U_{J\cup K}\) maps to
both \(U_J\) and \(U_K\), and any object mapping to both over \(U_L\) is
indexed by a simplex containing \(J\cup K\), hence factors uniquely through
\(U_{J\cup K}\). If \(J\cup K\notin N\), no nonempty simplex can contain the
union, so the only object mapping to both over \(U_L\) is the strict initial
object \(\emptyset\). Pullbacks involving \(\emptyset\) are \(\emptyset\) by
strict initiality. Therefore every fibre product required by
\Cref{def:local-reference-frame} is an object of \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\).
In particular, for every pair in the covering family \(\{U_i\to a\}\) the
pullback is \(U_{\{i,j\}}\) when \(\{i,j\}\in N\) and is \(\emptyset\)
otherwise. This proves the pullback-object clause in \textup{(i)}; the
identity, pullback-stability, and transitivity pretopology axioms hold by
construction of the generated pretopology.

The covering family $\mathcal U$ is one of the generators of the
pretopology on $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$. A finite set $J\subseteq I$
spans a simplex precisely when the iterated pullback of the corresponding
$U_i$ is a nonempty object $U_J$ rather than $\emptyset$. Hence the
\v{C}ech nerve of the cover is $N$, proving \textup{(ii)}.

The sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\) is defined by restricting the genuine
constant sheaf of locally constant \(A\)-valued functions on \(X\) along
the geometric-realization functor \(W\mapsto |W|\). Equivalently,
\begin{lemma}[$2$-cocycle-defined banded prestack for one component]\label{lem:twisted-branch-prestack-model}
Let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite cover whose nerve $N$ is connected, let $A$ be a finite abelian group, let $\Lambda$ be a finite nonempty label set, and let
\[
\alpha_\lambda\in Z^2(N,A)
\qquad
(\lambda\in\Lambda)
\]
be normalized simplicial cocycles. Assume also that
\[
H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0.
\]
We use their alternating extension to all
ordered triples of indices: for pairwise distinct indices, permuting an
ordered simplex multiplies the value by the sign of the permutation, and any
triple with a repeated index has value $0$. Let
\[
A_{\mathcal U}
\]
denote the genuine constant sheaf on $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, i.e. the
sheaf of locally constant $A$-valued functions on the chosen good-cover
geometric realization restricted to the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve. Hence
$A_{\mathcal U}(U_J)=A$ for each nonempty basic intersection and
$A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0$.
Let
\[
\Lambda_0:=\{\lambda\in\Lambda\mid \alpha_\lambda=0\}.
\]
On the finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, define $F$ by
\[
F(W)=
\begin{cases}
\Lambda,& W\to a\text{ a nonempty proper formal intersection object},\\
\Lambda_0,& W=a,\\
\{\ast\},& W=\emptyset,
\end{cases}
\]
with identity restrictions among nonempty proper intersection objects,
inclusions $\Lambda_0\hookrightarrow\Lambda$ from $a$ to nonempty proper
intersections, and the unique restriction map to $F(\emptyset)$. For each
$\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, define a fibred groupoid $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ by
\[
\mathfrak P_\lambda(a)=\varnothing
\]
and, for every nonempty proper object $W$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, put
\[
I(W):=\{i\in I\mid W\to U_i\text{ in }\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\}.
\]
Thus $I(U_J)=J$ for a formal intersection object. Define objects
\[
x_i^{(\lambda,W)}\qquad (i\in I(W))
\]
and morphism sets
\[
\mathrm{Hom}\bigl(x_i^{(\lambda,W)},x_j^{(\lambda,W)}\bigr)
=A_{\mathcal U}(W),
\]
which is identified with \(A\) because \(W\) is a connected nonempty
basic intersection. With this identification, write morphisms as
\((a,i,j)\) with \(a\in A\), and define composition by
\[
(b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)=(a+b+\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,k).
\]
For a morphism $V\to W$, one has $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, because a map
$W\to U_i$ composes with $V\to W$. Restrictions therefore send
$x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ to $x_i^{(\lambda,V)}$ and $(a,i,j)$ to the same
coefficient-labelled morphism after applying the restriction map of
\(A_{\mathcal U}\). Over $\emptyset$ take the terminal groupoid and let
every restriction to $\emptyset$ be the unique functor. For each
$\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, let $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ be the neutral stack with
one object over every object and automorphism group
\(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\) over \(W\), so the fibre over \(\emptyset\) is
terminal because \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). Restrictions are exactly
the restriction maps of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\). Its stack property is
the \(H^1\)-vanishing criterion of
\Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}: object descent data are
\(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles on slices, and those torsors are
trivial on the formal good-cover slices used here. Its automorphism sheaf is
therefore the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$. Set
\[
\mathfrak P:=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathfrak P_\lambda.
\]
This denotes the fibrewise coproduct over every nonempty object, while over
$\emptyset$ the summands share the single terminal fibre and all
restrictions to $\emptyset$ are the unique functor. The band used below is
the genuine constant sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ on the finite intersection site, not the
identity-restriction constant presheaf.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item each nonzero summand $\mathfrak P_\lambda$ is a category fibred in groupoids, and the pullback functors are strictly functorial;
\item the identity, inverse, and associativity laws in each twisted fibre are respectively the normalized identities
\[
\alpha_{\lambda,iij}=\alpha_{\lambda,ijj}=0,
\qquad
\alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0,
\]
and the cocycle identity
\[
\alpha_{\lambda,jkl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
+\alpha_{\lambda,ijl}-\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}=0;
\]
\item $\mathfrak P$ is a prestack with genuine constant band $A_{\mathcal U}$;
\item its presheaf of connected components is $F$;
\item after stackification, the components over $a$ are naturally indexed by $\Lambda$, and the component indexed by $\lambda$ has \v{C}ech cocycle $\alpha_\lambda$ on $\mathcal U$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The sheaf $A_{\mathcal U}$ is fixed as part of the finite intersection site interface in
\Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}(iii)--(iv). Since every
nonempty object of the finite intersection site is represented by a connected
contractible intersection of the good cover, locally constant
$A$-valued functions on it are exactly constant functions with value in
$A$; the strict initial object has only the zero section. Thus the
coefficient notation $A$ below is shorthand for the actual sheaf sections
$A_{\mathcal U}(W)$ on nonempty basic objects, not for the
identity-restriction constant presheaf on an arbitrary site; equivalently,
we are using \Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding} throughout.
In particular, whenever an isomorphism or automorphism presheaf below is
written as \(A\) on nonempty objects and \(0\) on \(\emptyset\), it is
defined by the displayed identification with
\(A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}\). The prestack condition is
therefore a sheaf condition for a genuine sheaf on each slice, not a
claim that the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the index
category is already a sheaf.

For a nonempty proper formal intersection object $W$ and a fixed
$\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$, the displayed formula makes every morphism
invertible. The identity at $x_i^{(\lambda,W)}$ is $(0,i,i)$ because the
cocycle is normalized on repeated indices. The inverse of $(a,i,j)$ is
$(-a,j,i)$, again because the repeated-index normalization gives
$\alpha_{\lambda,iji}=0$. Associativity of
\[
(c,k,l)\circ\bigl((b,j,k)\circ(a,i,j)\bigr)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\bigl((c,k,l)\circ(b,j,k)\bigr)\circ(a,i,j)
\]
is equivalent, after cancelling $a+b+c$, to
\[
\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}+\alpha_{\lambda,ikl}
=
\alpha_{\lambda,jkl}+\alpha_{\lambda,ijl},
\]
which is the displayed cocycle identity, interpreted under the alternating
ordered-triple convention just fixed. This proves that each fibre is a
groupoid. If $V\to W$, then $I(W)\subseteq I(V)$, so every object and
morphism named over $W$ has the same name over $V$. The restriction maps
therefore preserve labels and restrict coefficients through the map
\(A_{\mathcal U}(W)\to A_{\mathcal U}(V)\). Under the connected
intersection identifications these coefficient restrictions are the
identity maps \(A\to A\) on nonempty objects; for restrictions to
\(\emptyset\) they are the unique maps to \(0\). Thus the same ordered
simplex indices are used wherever a nonempty coefficient is present, so
restrictions preserve identities, inverses, and composition. Since
inclusions \(I(W)\subseteq I(V)\) are transitive and
\(A_{\mathcal U}\) is a sheaf with functorial restrictions, restrictions
compose strictly. This proves \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}.

For each pair of objects in a twisted fibre over a nonempty object $W$, the
isomorphism presheaf on the slice \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W\) is defined
objectwise by
\[
V\longmapsto A_{\mathcal U}(V),
\]
with restrictions those of the sheaf \(A_{\mathcal U}\), whenever the two
restricted labels are both defined; over \(\emptyset\) this gives the
single section of \(A_{\mathcal U}(\emptyset)=0\). On connected nonempty
basic intersections this is the coefficient notation \(A\), but the
presheaf itself is the restriction of the genuine constant sheaf
\(A_{\mathcal U}\), not the identity-restriction constant presheaf on the
index category. By
\Cref{lem:formal-site-constant-sheaf-banding}, it is therefore a sheaf.
The same argument applies to automorphisms,
where the distinguished zero coefficient gives a canonical identification
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(x_i^{(\lambda,W)})
\cong A_{\mathcal U}|_{\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}/W}.
\]
Thus the prestack condition and the banding use the genuine constant sheaf
$A_{\mathcal U}$. The neutral summands indexed by \(\Lambda_0\) are stacks by
\Cref{lem:formal-site-neutral-stack-h1}. This invokes object descent, not
only morphism descent: a one-object \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-banded prestack has
descent data classified by \(A_{\mathcal U}\)-torsor cocycles, and those
torsors are trivial on every relevant slice. Taking the finite coproduct
over nonempty objects and the shared terminal fibre over $\emptyset$ preserves the prestack
condition: over nonempty objects this is the usual finite coproduct of
prestacks in groupoids, while the strict initial object has only the unique
matching datum. This proves \textup{(iii)} without any appeal to a
constant presheaf sheaf condition.

For every nonempty proper intersection object, each twisted summand is
connected and each neutral summand is one connected component; there are no
morphisms between distinct summands. Over $\emptyset$ the shared terminal
fibre has the unique lift object over the empty intersection, matching $F(\emptyset)=\{\ast\}$.
Hence
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(U)\cong\Lambda
\]
for every nonempty proper intersection object $U\to a$. Over $a$, the
nonzero summands have empty fibre and the neutral summands indexed by
\(\Lambda_0\) have one object, so
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P)(a)\cong\Lambda_0.
\]
These identifications are compatible with the restriction maps, giving \textup{(iv)}.

By \Cref{lem:formal-label-sheafification}, applied to the displayed
presheaf \(F\) and the subset \(\Lambda_0\subseteq\Lambda\), the
sheafification of \(F\) has terminal sections indexed by \(\Lambda\). By
\Cref{prop:stackification-components}, stackification identifies
\[
\pi_0(a(\mathfrak P))\cong aF,
\]
so the components over $a$ are indexed by $\Lambda$.

For a fixed $\lambda$, take on $U_i$ the object $x_i^{(\lambda,U_i)}$ if $\lambda\notin\Lambda_0$ and the distinguished constant object if $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$. On $U_{ij}$ take the morphism $(0,i,j)$ in the nonzero case and the identity in the zero case. The triple defect is
\[
(0,i,k)^{-1}\circ(0,j,k)\circ(0,i,j)
=
(\alpha_{\lambda,ijk},i,i)
\]
in the twisted case and is $0$ in the constant case. Under the band identification this is exactly $\alpha_{\lambda,ijk}$. Thus the Cech obstruction cocycle of the $\lambda$-component is $\alpha_\lambda$, proving \textup{(v)}.
\end{proof}

+\begin{equation}\label{eq:component-substack}
+ \mathfrak E[v](X)=
+ \{x\in\mathfrak E(X):[x]=v|_X\}.
+\end{equation}
+The equality in \eqref{eq:component-substack} is equality in the component
+sheaf, so it is local by construction.
 
-We begin by fixing the hypotheses used in the section. Individual statements invoke only the subcollection they require.

-\begin{definition}[\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis]\label{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}
-For an admissible parameter \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\) at \(p\), a band \(\Band\)
-on \(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a\), and a global component section \(v\), a
-\emph{\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis} consists of a filtered cofinal
-family
-\[
-\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\subseteq \Cov_{p,s}(a)
-\]
-such that every cover \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}\) in the family has a
-\v{C}ech nerve in the slice site, trivializes the band on all intersections
-used in degrees \(0,1,2\), and satisfies the following comparison condition:
-the canonical refinement map
-\[
-\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)}
-\check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)
-\longrightarrow
-H^2(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,\Band)
-\]
-is an isomorphism. One way to verify this condition is the usual Leray
-hypothesis: all nonempty finite intersections appearing in the family are
-\(\Band\)-acyclic in every positive degree needed for the derived
-comparison. The definition itself, however, records the comparison
-isomorphism as the required assumption; the later theorems do not silently
-infer derived \(H^2\) from a single \v{C}ech cocycle unless this hypothesis, or
-the explicit finite good-cover Leray theorem of
-\suppresult{Finite intersection site associated to the cover nerve, Leray comparison, and one-state admissible expansion}, is in force.
-\end{definition}
+The exact ancestry of this construction is classical.  Giraud proves that
+the projection of a stack to its sheaf of connected components is a gerbe
+over that sheaf, and that pullback along a component section gives the
+corresponding maximal subgerbe
+\cite[III, Prop.~2.1.5.3]{Giraud1971}.  The next proposition records this
+standard construction and the two compatibilities used later.  It is an
+input, not an originality claim.
 
-\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},nosep]
-\item\label{hyp:admitted-prestack} An admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$ with $a=[r]_p$, equipped with a banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r \to \mathcal C_a$ and band $\Band$ in the sense of \suppresult{Banded groupoid lift and stackification}.
-\item\label{hyp:band-identification} The band $\Band$ is identified with a fixed abelian sheaf on the slice site $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$.
-\item\label{hyp:global-conservativity} The banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \suppresult{Essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre}.
-\item\label{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted} For every global component section \(v\), a
-\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis in the sense of
-\Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package} has been fixed.
+\begin{proposition}[Standard component-gerbe package]
+\label{prop:standard-component-gerbe-package}
+Let \(\mathfrak E\) be a stack in groupoids on \(\mathcal C\), and let
+\(v\in\pi_0(\mathfrak E)(a)\).
+\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
+\item The full substack \(\mathfrak E[v]\) is the maximal gerbe over the
+      section \(v\).  If \(\mathfrak E\) is banded by an abelian sheaf
+      \(\mathscr A\), then \(\mathfrak E[v]\) has the restricted
+      \(\mathscr A\)-banding.
+\item Its Giraud class satisfies
+      \[
+      [\mathfrak E[v]]=0\text{ in }H^2(\mathcal C,\mathscr A)
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v]\text{ is neutral}
+      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+      \mathfrak E[v](a)\ne\varnothing.
+      \]
+\item Suppose \(\Phi:\mathfrak E\to\mathfrak E'\) is a banded equivalence,
+      its band map is \(\theta:\mathscr A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr A'\),
+      and its component map carries \(v\) to \(v'\).  Then \(\Phi\)
+      restricts to a banded equivalence
+      \(\mathfrak E[v]\simeq\mathfrak E'[v']\), and
+      \[
+      \theta_*[\mathfrak E[v]]=[\mathfrak E'[v']].
+      \]
 \end{enumerate}
-
-When a statement compares global component sections with the strict predicate
-\(\CompSec_s\), or with \(\NoAmalg_s\) through that predicate,
-it separately assumes that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice.
-Without this separatedness assumption global component sections are only
-sheafified sections, and no strict compatible family is asserted.
